sweeps.family: INTRADAY MOMENTUM (Gao-Han-Li-Zhou 2018 first/last half-hour; LETF-rebalancing into the close; Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon 2024 noise-band breakout; plus moving the NVDL overnight entry earlier or later than 15:52)

candidates.name: A1 Gao canonical, SPY to 3x S&P (both directions)
candidates.exact_rule: At 10:00 ET compute r1 = SPY(10:00)/SPY prior close - 1. If r1>0, buy 3x long S&P (SPXL; modeled as daily-reset 3x SPY) at 15:31. If r1<0, buy 3x inverse (SPXS). Sell at 15:50. At most 3 trades in any 5 sessions.
candidates.instrument: SPXL / SPXS (synthetic 3x SPY; real SPXL/SPXS 15:31-15:50 corr 0.995-0.996 with synthetic, mean diff <0.003%)
candidates.mechanism: Gao et al. intraday momentum. The effect does show up in the underlying for 2005-2015 (sign(r1) x SPY 15:30-16:00 = +0.027%, t 3.66), but almost all of it falls in 15:50-16:00 (+0.024%, t 5.2), after a trade that must exit at 15:50. In 2016-2026 it is gone (t -0.37) and in the last 2y slightly negative. The executable 15:31-15:50 window earns about 0 gross (-0.006%).
candidates.data_used: 1-min SPY 2005-01-03..2026-03-31 (HF mito0o852/OHLCV-1m, validated against Robinhood bars) + Robinhood 10-min 2026-03-25..2026-10-13

candidates.name: A2 Gao canonical, QQQ to TQQQ/SQQQ
candidates.exact_rule: r1 = QQQ(10:00)/QQQ prior close - 1. If r1>0 buy TQQQ at 15:31, else buy SQQQ. Sell at 15:50. PDT cap 3 per 5 sessions.
candidates.mechanism: Same as A1. QQQ underlying: sign(r1) x 15:30-16:00 = +0.010% (t 1.71) in H1 and about 0 after. Gross on 15:31-15:50 is +0.001%.
candidates.data_used: 1-min QQQ 2011-03-24..2026-03-31 (the ticker was QQQQ before 2011-03 and was not extracted) + RH 10-min tail

candidates.name: A3 Gao canonical, IWM to TNA/TZA
candidates.exact_rule: r1 = IWM(10:00)/IWM prior close - 1. If r1>0 buy TNA at 15:31, else buy TZA. Sell at 15:50. PDT cap 3/5.
candidates.mechanism: Strongest underlying Gao effect of the three ETFs in H1 (IWM sign(r1) x last half-hour +0.041%, t 4.38), again concentrated after 15:50. Gone in H2 (-0.008%, t -1.24).

candidates.name: A4 Day-return momentum, long-only TQQQ
candidates.exact_rule: If QQQ(15:30)/QQQ prior close - 1 > 0, buy TQQQ at 15:31 and sell at 15:50. Otherwise no trade. PDT cap 3/5.
candidates.mechanism: Same-day trend continuation into the close. Gross is -0.001%/trade, so there is nothing to pay the 0.12% round trip.

candidates.name: A5 Gao 12th half-hour (15:00-15:30) sign, SPY
candidates.exact_rule: Sign of SPY 15:00 to 15:30. If >0 buy SPXL at 15:31, if <0 buy SPXS. Sell at 15:50. PDT cap 3/5.
candidates.mechanism: Gao's second predictor. On the underlying, sign(h12) x 15:31-15:50 is +0.003% (t 0.95), so it is negligible. QQQ and IWM are no better (-0.13% and -0.10% net).

candidates.name: A6 Strong first-half-hour filter, long-only SPXL
candidates.exact_rule: If r1 = SPY(10:00)/prior close - 1 is > 0 and |r1| exceeds its trailing-250-session 80th percentile (no look-ahead), buy SPXL at 15:31 and sell at 15:50. PDT cap 3/5.
candidates.mechanism: Larger morning moves were supposed to give stronger continuation. Gross is +0.073%, below cost. The same filter on QQQ and IWM, and a high-volatility-regime filter, are also negative (-0.05% to -0.14%).

candidates.name: A7 LETF-rebalancing big-move day, SPY (both directions)
candidates.exact_rule: If |SPY(15:30)/prior close - 1| > 2%, buy SPXL (up day) or SPXS (down day) at 15:31 and sell at 15:50. PDT cap 3/5.
candidates.mechanism: Leveraged-ETF rebalancing demand scales with L(L-1) x the day's return and trades at or near the close, mostly after 15:50. The 15:31-15:50 slice was positive only in 2005-2015. At 1%, and on QQQ/IWM, the results are negative (-0.04% to -0.10%).

candidates.name: A8 LETF-rebalancing big up-day, QQQ long-only TQQQ
candidates.exact_rule: If QQQ(15:30)/prior close - 1 > +2%, buy TQQQ at 15:31 and sell at 15:50. PDT cap 3/5.
candidates.mechanism: Same as A7. The point estimate is positive but not significant in any long window, and it turns negative at 0.15%/side.

candidates.name: B0a Unconditional earlier overnight entry at 15:00
candidates.exact_rule: Buy the §3(c) NVDL/NVDX overnight position at 15:00 instead of 15:52 every night. Exit at 09:31 as now.
candidates.mechanism: NVDA (and NVDL) drift down in mid-to-late afternoon and recover after 15:52 (NVDL 15:52-16:00: +0.055%/night in 2016-2026, t 4.1). 15:52 sits near the late-day low, so moving the entry earlier gives up return. No added trading cost, since it replaces the 15:52 fill.
candidates.data_used: 1-min NVDA 2005-2026-03 + RH 10-min tail (15:52 proxied by 15:50 after 2026-03-31); NVDA earnings-proxy days excluded (top-4 next-day gaps per year)

candidates.name: B0b Unconditional earlier overnight entry at 15:31
candidates.exact_rule: Buy the overnight NVDL position at 15:31 instead of 15:52 every night.
candidates.mechanism: Same as B0a. Entering anywhere from 15:15 to 15:45 costs 0.018-0.027%/night on average. Delaying past 15:52 also costs: 15:52-15:55 is +0.039%/night in 2016-2026 (t 5.1).

candidates.name: B1 Enter at 15:00 if NVDA is up on the day (task variant b)
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA(15:00)/prior close - 1 > 0, buy the overnight NVDL position at 15:00. Otherwise buy at 15:52 as now.
candidates.in_sample: H1: n=1353 signal nights, -0.017%/signal night, t -0.45
candidates.mechanism: Intraday momentum predicts that up days keep rising into the close. Over 15:00-15:52 they do not. The mirror rule (enter at 15:00 on down days, B1r) is also negative: -0.052%, H2 -0.150% (t -3.7).

candidates.name: B2 Enter at 15:31 if NVDA is up at 15:30 (task variant b)
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA(15:30)/prior close - 1 > 0, buy NVDL at 15:31 instead of 15:52.
candidates.mechanism: Same as B1. The mirror on down days (B2r) gives -0.028%. With the 15:00-15:30 half-hour as the signal (B3) it gives -0.027% (t -1.58). With QQQ or SPY up at 15:30 as the signal (B4/B5) it gives -0.009% / -0.019%, and last 2y -0.079% / -0.092%.

candidates.name: B6 Gao first half-hour signal for the NVDL entry
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA(10:00)/prior close - 1 > 0, buy NVDL at 15:31 instead of 15:52.
candidates.mechanism: Gao predictor applied to the entry time. Negative. Using QQQ(10:00) as the signal gives -0.008% (t -0.53).

candidates.name: B7b Enter at 15:00 on big NVDA up days (LETF rebalancing)
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA(15:00)/prior close - 1 > +2%, buy NVDL at 15:00 instead of 15:52.
candidates.mechanism: NVDA's leveraged-ETF AUM must buy into the close on big up days. It worked only before 2016 and has reversed in the last 2y. The 15:31 version (B7) is -0.006%.

candidates.name: B8 Delay entry to 15:58 on NVDA down days
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA(15:50)/prior close - 1 < 0, buy NVDL at 15:58 instead of 15:52. Value = minus the NVDL return from 15:52 to 15:58.
candidates.mechanism: Selling into the close on down days (rebalancing). The effect has decayed and has been negative in the last 2y. A 15:58 entry also collides with the §4 rule that cancels unfilled orders at 15:58. Delaying only on down >2% days (B8b) gives +0.046% overall but -0.076% in the last 2y. Delaying to 15:55 (B8c) gives +0.007%.

candidates.name: B9 Full-size early overnight entry on an NVDA noise-band breakout
candidates.exact_rule: Skipped on NVDA earnings days. For each checkpoint h in {11:00, 11:30, ..., 15:30}: sigma_h = mean over the prior 14 sessions of |NVDA(h)/NVDA open - 1|, and UB_h = max(today's open, prior close) x (1+sigma_h). At the first h where NVDA's price at h is above UB_h, buy the whole §3(c) NVDL/NVDX position at h+1 min (marketable limit) instead of at 15:52. Hold to 09:31 as usual. No stop and no same-day sell. If there is no breakout, enter at 15:52.
candidates.instrument: NVDL / NVDX (synthetic 2x NVDA; on real NVDL signal days 2023-03..2026-10: n=226, +0.197%, t 1.35, corr 0.989 with synthetic)
candidates.in_sample: H1 2005-01..2015-11: n=748 signal nights, +0.196%/signal night, t 1.84
candidates.mechanism: Volatility-scaled breakout momentum (Zarattini et al. 2024): once NVDA leaves its usual intraday range, dealer gamma hedging and the rebalancing of NVDA single-stock leveraged ETFs (NVDL/NVDX/NVDU) push the same way into the close. Entering every night at 11:01 earns +0.026% (t 0.58), so the edge is conditional, not drift. Lower-band breakdown days go the other way (-0.139%). No added trading cost, since it replaces the 15:52 fill. The catch is tail risk: worst afternoon -17.75% (2020-03-20) and sd 2.76%/signal night. In a joint block bootstrap with the overnight leg, P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) rises from 26.5% to 33.7% (2y), 28.4% to 35.4% (8y) and 26.1% to 31.9% (2005-2026). Log growth/session changes by -6.1 / +3.8 / +4.5 bp. This fails the do-not-raise-PAUSE goal.
candidates.data_used: 1-min NVDA 2005-01..2026-03 (HF mito0o852/OHLCV-1m) + RH 10-min tail; real NVDL 1-min 2022-12..2026-03 and RH 10-min to 2026-10-13 for validation; earnings-proxy days excluded

candidates.name: B9p Partial early entry: 1 NVDL share on breakout, rest at 15:52
candidates.exact_rule: Same signal as B9. At the first breakout from 11:00, buy exactly 1 NVDL share (about 35-38% of the overnight position at E~$103) at h+1 min with a marketable limit. At 15:52, size the remaining NVDL/NVDX from the cash left under the §3(c) cap (0.98*E). Hold everything to 09:31. No stop and no same-day sell. Not in PAUSE, not on NVDA earnings days.
candidates.in_sample: Per-signal edge on the early share is the same as B9: H1 +0.196% (t 1.84)
candidates.out_of_sample: H2 +0.277% (t 2.86). Last 2y +0.017% (t 0.08). Joint bootstrap (fraction 0.38, multiplier 1.0): P(PAUSE<=60) 26.5% to 27.3% (2y), 28.4% to 29.0% (8y), 26.1% to 25.7% (2005-26). Log growth -2.1 / +1.7 / +1.9 bp/session. Multiplier 1.5 is similar (27.6 / 29.2 / 25.4%).
candidates.mechanism: Same as B9. At about 1/3 of the position, the added afternoon variance is small enough that PAUSE risk is roughly unchanged, but so is the expected gain (about $5-6/yr, about +2 bp/session over the long samples, -2 bp over the last 2y). The worst case is -17.75% x ~0.35 = about -6% of equity in one afternoon. This is the best candidate in the family. It was found after the pre-specified (b) variants failed (data-snooping risk), and the last 2 years show no edge. A pre-registered shadow log should come before any live use.

candidates.name: C1 Noise-band breakout day trade, QQQ to TQQQ long-only
candidates.exact_rule: Same noise band as B9, computed on QQQ (14-day sigma, UB = max(open, prior close) x (1+sigma_h)), checked at 11:00..15:30. On the first close above UB_h, buy TQQQ at h+1 min. Sell at the first later half-hour where QQQ is back below UB_h (fill +1 min); otherwise sell at 15:50. One entry per day, PDT cap 3 per 5 sessions.
candidates.mechanism: Zarattini et al. intraday-momentum breakout. Gross is +0.192%/trade, against +0.055% for holding TQQQ 11:01-15:50 every day, so the breakout adds about 0.14% gross. That survives only the tight cost model (half-spread + 0.05%), not 0.15%/side. Joint bootstrap with the overnight leg at 0.06%/side: P(PAUSE<=60) changes by +4.2 / +0.4 / +1.2 pts (2y / 8y / 2011-26), log growth -2.3 / +0.8 / +1.2 bp. At 0.15%/side, worse in every window. It uses the PDT slots that §7 reserves for emergencies, and the TQQQ sell must fill before the 15:52 entry.
candidates.data_used: 1-min QQQ 2011-03..2026-03 + RH 10-min tail; real TQQQ vs synthetic corr 0.997

candidates.name: C2 Noise-band breakout, SPY both directions (paper's canonical form)
candidates.exact_rule: SPY noise band (14d, multiplier 1), checks from 10:00. Above UB: buy SPXL at h+1m. Below LB = min(open, prior close) x (1-sigma): buy SPXS. Band-re-entry stop at half-hours, else exit 15:50. 1 entry/day, PDT 3/5.
candidates.instrument: SPXL / SPXS (SPXL ~$294 is not affordable at E=$103)
candidates.mechanism: Gross +0.069%/trade: the paper's edge does not cover 3x-ETF costs, the 15:50 exit or the 1-min fill lag. Start 11:00 gives -0.020%. Lookback 10/20 and multiplier 1.5 stay between -0.01% and +0.03%. IWM versions run -0.08% to -0.14% (t about -3).

candidates.name: C4 Noise-band breakout day trade, NVDA to NVDL long-only (with stop)
candidates.exact_rule: NVDA noise band from 11:00. On the first break above UB, buy NVDL at h+1m. Band-re-entry stop, else sell 15:50. PDT 3/5.
candidates.mechanism: Same signal as B9, but as a stopped day trade. B9 dominates it: B9 makes the same bet with no PDT slot, no extra round trip and no sell-then-rebuy before 15:52.

notes: Data source: Robinhood intraday history is not usable for a 10-year test. For SPY, 30-min, 10-min, hour and auto-interval (15-second) requests before about 2026-01-30 return only interpolated=true filler bars (a constant ~775). The SPX/NDX/RUT index historicals return not_found for 2015 and 2024. I therefore used the public Hugging Face 1-minute dataset mito0o852/OHLCV-1m: all US tickers, 2005-01..2026-03, downloaded month by month, keeping 22 tickers.

Data validation: the dataset's SPY 09:30-09:39 and 15:59 closes match Robinhood 10-min bars exactly on the 2026-03 overlap. Median |open-to-close difference| against Robinhood daily bars is 0.013% (SPY/QQQ). The >0.5% mismatches sit mostly in 2005-2010 Robinhood daily bars (odd 4-decimal closes), plus a few closing-auction days. Real-vs-synthetic segment correlations are 0.985-0.998 for TQQQ, SQQQ, SPXL, SPXS, UPRO, TNA, TZA, NVDL and NVDX. Robinhood 10-min bars (2026-03-25..2026-10-13) fill the tail; there 15:31 is proxied by 15:30 and 15:52 by 15:50. QQQ starts 2011-03-24 because the ticker was QQQQ before that and I did not extract it.

Gao et al. replicates in the underlying only in 2005-2015. Over 2005-2026, sign(prior close to 10:00) x SPY 15:30-16:00 is +0.012% (t 2.63): H1 +0.027% (t 3.66), H2 -0.002% (t -0.37), last 2y -0.004%. OLS slope 0.088 (R2 2.6%) in H1 vs 0.017 (R2 0.16%) in H2. IWM shows the same pattern (H1 t 4.38, H2 t -1.24). Most of it is in 15:50-16:00 (SPY H1 t 5.2), which a trade that must be flat by 15:50 cannot capture. In the executable 15:31-15:50 window, gross is about 0 (-0.006% to +0.02%) against a 0.12% (tight) or 0.30% (0.15%/side) round trip. All 60+ variants tried on SPY/QQQ/IWM (both directions or long-only, trailing-quantile strength filter, high-vol regime, h12 agreement, LETF big-move 1%/2%) are negative after costs, except tiny-sample big-move cases with t < 1.1.

Keep the 15:52 entry. Moving the NVDL entry earlier subtracts: 15:00-15:52 averages -0.088%/night in 2016-2026 (t -3.6) and -0.117% in the last 2y. Real NVDL over 2023-26 shows -0.124% (n=841). Delaying also subtracts: 15:52-16:00 is +0.055%/night in 2016-2026 (t 4.1), and 15:52-15:55 is +0.039% (t 5.1). 15:52 sits at the late-day low (15:45-15:52 is -0.022%, t -2.8). None of the simple up/down-day conditions (B1-B8) fixes this out of sample.

Only one signal survives the long sample: a volatility-scaled noise-band breakout on NVDA (B9). It is positive in both halves and robust across parameters, with no PDT use and no extra cost. But it is flat in the last 2 years. At full size it raises P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) by about 6-7 points, which violates the brief. At 1 NVDL share early (B9p) PAUSE risk is roughly unchanged, but the gain is only about $5-6/yr at E=$103 (about +2 bp/session long-run, -2 bp over the last 2y). I found it after the pre-specified variants failed, so it carries snooping risk. Recommendation: a free shadow log of B9p for at least one quarter, pre-registered with this exact rule, before any live use. Recording the 11:00-15:30 half-hour NVDA prices and the 14-day sigma is enough to score it after the close.

The joint-bootstrap PAUSE baselines here (about 26-28% within 60 sessions, overnight-only) are higher than the day-leg review's 1y figure (4.5%). This bootstrap uses synthetic 2x NVDA 15:52 to 09:31 returns at 0.93 exposure over 2y, 8y and 21y windows, net of 0.10% per night, with earnings-proxy nights in cash. Only the differences between arms in the same window are meaningful.

Practical constraints. SPXL (~$294) and UPRO (~$154) cannot be bought at E=$103. One TQQQ share is about 75% of E. SQQQ, SPXS, TNA, NVDL and NVDX are affordable. Spreads quoted on 2026-10-14 at 09:47 ET: TQQQ 0.013%, SQQQ 0.03%, SPXS 0.04%, SPXL 0.03%, NVDL 0.03%, TNA 0.018%. So 0.06%/side (half-spread + 0.05%) is the realistic tight cost, with 0.15%/side as the stress case. Any PDT-using rule (A/C families) spends slots that RULES_v3 §7 now reserves for emergency exits, and must be flat by 15:50 to fund the 15:52 entry.

Scratch files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/wf3/intraday-momentum/. scripts/ holds extract.py, build_daily.py, prep.py, finalA.py, finalB.py, finalC2.py, c3_detail.py, c4_control.py, b9_breakout_entry.py, b9_robust.py, joint_risk.py, joint_risk_b9.py, joint_risk_b9b.py, validate.py and validate_daily.py. Outputs are finalA.txt, finalB.txt, finalC.txt, finalC2.txt, finalA.json, finalB.json, finalC2.json, daily_cp.parquet (per-ticker daily checkpoint prices) and B9_base.parquet. data1m/ holds the per-month 1-min extracts (613 MB) and rh/ the Robinhood JSON. Nothing under /home/user/test-trading was modified, and no orders or account tools were used.

sweeps.family: CALENDAR & EVENT EFFECTS: pre-FOMC drift, turn of the month, pre-holiday sessions, options expiration, FOMC-cycle even weeks. Each is tested in three forms: an intraday day trade (uses PDT slots), holding NVDL through the day instead of the 09:31 exit (or moving the entry to 09:31), and swapping the overnight instrument on specific nights.

candidates.name: FOMC-eve overnight (status-quo check, no change)
candidates.exact_rule: No change. Keep the NVDA-2x overnight leg on every FOMC-eve night: 15:52 on the day before a scheduled FOMC statement to 09:31 on FOMC day. Never add an FOMC blackout. Next one: 2026-10-27 -> 10-28. That night is also NVDL's expected ex-date: the opening drop is the distribution, not a loss.
candidates.in_sample: 2006-2016, 82 meetings: synthetic NVDA-2x close->open +0.626% gross (t 2.05), +0.326% net of 0.15%/side. SPY overnight into FOMC day +0.199% (t 2.7) vs +0.032% on an average night.
candidates.out_of_sample: 2016-2026, 83 meetings: +1.229% gross (t 3.76), +0.929% net (t 2.84). Last 2 years, 16 meetings: +0.945% gross, +0.645% net (t 0.95). Real ETFs: NVDL 2022-12+ (n 31) +1.059% vs +0.420% on other nights; TQQQ 2010+ (n 132) +0.718% (t 4.15) vs +0.124%, last 2y +0.605% (t 2.58); SPXL +0.490% (t 3.42). SPY/QQQ/NVDA overnight into FOMC day is t >= 2.7 in both halves.
candidates.mechanism: Lucca & Moench pre-announcement drift (risk premium ahead of resolving FOMC uncertainty). In this data the drift sits in the overnight segment before the announcement, which the current leg already holds. It adds $0 versus the status quo (the night is worth about $4.79/yr gross of the current leg's value); the point is not to remove it.
candidates.data_used: Robinhood daily split-adjusted SPY/QQQ/NVDA 2006-01..2026-10-13 plus real NVDL/TQQQ/SPXL daily. 165 scheduled FOMC dates reconstructed from memory (unscheduled meetings excluded).

candidates.name: FOMC-eve TQQQ while the overnight leg is in cash mode (conditional)
candidates.exact_rule: Only while §3(f)'s edge-decay switch has the overnight leg in cash (not on NVDA earnings nights, not in PAUSE): buy 1 TQQQ (about 75% of E) at 15:52 on the FOMC eve with §4 mechanics, sell 09:31 FOMC day with §5 mechanics. In normal operation, do nothing.
candidates.in_sample: 2006-2016: synthetic 3x QQQ close->open net of 0.30% round trip +0.341% (t 1.51, n 82).
candidates.out_of_sample: 2016-2026: +0.570% (t 2.75, n 83). Last 2y: +0.360% (t 1.54, n 16). Real TQQQ 2010-2026 gross +0.718% (t 4.15) vs +0.124% on other nights. Positive in 13 of 21 years. On an average night TQQQ overnight is -0.167% net, so only the FOMC eve qualifies.
candidates.mechanism: Pre-FOMC drift in the index, not NVDA-specific. It is the one night that keeps a robust overnight premium if the NVDA-specific edge decays. The $2.80/yr assumes cash mode all year; in practice it is about $0 unless §3(f) fires.
candidates.data_used: Robinhood daily QQQ 2006-2026 for synthetic 3x; real TQQQ daily 2010-2026

candidates.name: Pre-FOMC intraday day trade, TQQQ 09:31->13:55
candidates.exact_rule: On scheduled FOMC days, after the 09:31 NVDL exit fills, buy 1 TQQQ at 09:31 and sell at 13:55. Tested as open->close because 13:55 bars do not exist before 2026.
candidates.out_of_sample: 2016-2026: -0.539% (t -1.36, n 83). Last 2y: -1.557% (t -1.77, n 16). Actual 2026 30-minute bars (5 meetings): TQQQ open->13:59 averaged -0.49%, SPY -0.22%. At 0.06%/side costs: still -0.359% in 2016-2026.
candidates.mechanism: Lucca-Moench morning drift. Consistent with the literature, it is gone after about 2015 in this data.
candidates.data_used: Daily QQQ open->close 2006-2026 as a proxy for 09:31->13:55 (unbiased only if post-14:00 mean ~0); Robinhood 30-minute bars 2026-01-30..2026-10-13 for 5 meetings

candidates.name: Pre-FOMC intraday day trade, 3x SPY 09:31->13:55
candidates.exact_rule: Same as the TQQQ version, on 3x SPY. SPXL ($294) and UPRO ($154) are not affordable at E=$103; the only affordable SPY product is SSO (2x).
candidates.mechanism: Same as above; it decayed after publication

candidates.name: Extend the NVDL overnight hold to 13:55 on FOMC day
candidates.exact_rule: On FOMC day, do not sell NVDL/NVDX at 09:31. Sell at 13:55 and re-enter at 15:52 as usual. Same number of trades; only the exit time moves.
candidates.in_sample: 2006-2016: synthetic 2x NVDA open->close (with the real-NVDL intraday haircut of 0.08%/day) +1.666% (t 3.11, n 82)
candidates.mechanism: Pre-FOMC drift. The full-sample figure comes entirely from 2006-2015.
candidates.data_used: Daily NVDA 2006-2026 with synthetic 2x and haircut; 2026 30-minute NVDL bars

candidates.name: FOMC eve: TQQQ instead of NVDL, held to 13:55
candidates.exact_rule: On the FOMC eve, buy 1 TQQQ at 15:52 instead of NVDL/NVDX, sell at 13:55 on FOMC day (not a day trade), then buy NVDL at 15:52 as usual.
candidates.in_sample: Gain over the NVDL overnight, 2006-2016: +0.959% (t 2.02, n 82)
candidates.out_of_sample: 2016-2026: -0.609% (t -1.35, n 83). Last 2y: -1.579% (t -1.28, n 16). Overnight-only swap: -0.173% (t -1.06), because NVDA-2x beats QQQ-3x on FOMC eves.
candidates.mechanism: Pre-FOMC drift. Swapping away from NVDA loses the larger overnight move, and the morning leg has decayed.
candidates.data_used: Daily QQQ/NVDA 2006-2026; close used as a proxy for 13:55

candidates.name: FOMC-1 TQQQ day trade
candidates.exact_rule: Day before FOMC: buy 1 TQQQ 09:31, sell 15:49
candidates.mechanism: Afternoon-before part of the Lucca-Moench window; not present after 2016

candidates.name: Post-FOMC reversal: inverse day trade on FOMC+1

notes: Bottom line: nothing in this family is ready to add to live trading. The one robust effect, the pre-FOMC overnight drift (SPY overnight into FOMC day +0.19% vs +0.03% on an average night, t 4.3, with both halves and real TQQQ last 2y at t >= 2.6), is already captured by holding NVDL every night. Keep it and never add an FOMC blackout. The morning-of-FOMC drift (09:31->13:55) is dead after 2015. The best new idea, E-TOM+3, is marginal: about 40 calendar cells were tested, its last 2 years are negative for NVDA, and it should be shadow-logged rather than adopted. The opex-week-Tuesday hold-through (also marginal) and quad-witching SPXU (marginal; decayed after 2022) belong in a shadow log at most.

Data limitation: Robinhood intraday bars (30-minute and hour) exist only from 2026-01-30; earlier requests return interpolated fill bars. SPX index historicals return not_found. So every 13:55 exit is proxied by the close, which is unbiased only if the post-14:00 mean is ~0. A check on the 5 FOMC meetings of 2026 (actual 30-minute bars): SPY open->13:59 averaged -0.22%, TQQQ -0.49%, NVDL -1.38%, and 14:00->close was negative on 4 of 5. A permission check on external intraday sources was denied, so no other data was used.

FOMC dates were reconstructed from memory: 165 scheduled statement days 2006-01-31..2026-09-16, with the 2020-03 emergency meetings excluded (the scheduled March 2020 meeting was replaced). Pre-2013 statement times varied (14:15; 12:30 on 2011-12 press-conference days); this does not matter for daily proxies. Upcoming meetings, also from memory and unverified: 2026-10-28 and 2026-12-09. The 10/27->10/28 FOMC-eve night coincides with NVDL's expected 10/28 ex-date (RULES §8): keep the position; the opening drop is the distribution.

Costs: main tables use 0.15%/side. Live spreads on 2026-10-14 were TQQQ/SQQQ/SPXU $0.01 (half-spread + 0.05% is about 0.06%/side) and NVDL $0.03 (about 0.09%/side); low-cost variants are reported where they change the verdict. Affordability at E=$103: SPXL $294 and UPRO $154 are NOT affordable. TQQQ $77 (1 share = 75% of E), SQQQ $34.6 (2 shares = 67%), SPXU $33.2 (3 shares = 97%), SSO $71.5, QLD $95, TNA $55.

Synthetic leverage check: daily-reset L x underlying tracks the real funds well. Intraday correlation is 0.998 for TQQQ, 0.962 for SPXL and 0.980 for NVDL. Real NVDL ran 0.08%/day below synthetic intraday and 0.105%/day below on close-to-close (2022-12..2026-10), so all NVDL hold-through numbers subtract 0.08%/day. SPY dividends: amounts are taken from adjustment_type=all for 2014-06 onward, and 0.5% is assumed on quarterly third Fridays before that; this matters only for overnight quad-witching returns. NVDA earnings nights in the simulations are approximated as the largest overnight gap in each Feb/May/Aug/Nov.

Cross-family warning, material to the whole strategy. At 0.15%/side the synthetic NVDA-2x overnight-only leg nets -0.056%/night over 2006-2026, +0.066% over 2016-2026 and +0.059% over the last 2y. Its log growth is negative except at about 0.09%/side in 2016-2026 (+0.04%/session). The daily round trip (0.18-0.30%) is larger than NVDA-2x's long-run intraday drift (about +0.03% after the haircut). The 09:31 exit is therefore a variance and PAUSE control, not a source of expected return: buy-and-hold NVDL had higher log growth but P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) of 72-77% vs 34-42%. Measuring real per-side fill costs is worth more than any calendar tweak.

Because skipping a round trip saves 0.18-0.30% on any day, a hold-through or shifted-entry candidate must beat a random-day placebo. Holding 12 random days a year adds about 0.00% log growth per session. E-TOM+3 adds +0.06% vs placebo (2006-26), and H-OPEXWK-Tue and H-TOM+3 about +0.03-0.04%. H-TOM+1..+3, H-PREHOL and H-FCEVEN mostly harvest the cost saving while raising PAUSE probability.

PAUSE simulation method: rolling 60- and 125-session windows (step 3) over 2006-2026, 2006-2016, 2016-2026 and the last 2y. Exposure is fixed at 93% of E, there is no PAUSE-sizing response, and PAUSE means E <= 0.8 x the trailing 20-session high. The absolute levels (26-55%) are far above the earlier 1-year bootstrap's 4.5% because the long sample includes 2008, 2018 and 2022; use them only for comparing candidates. The last-2y windows are dominated by 2 or 3 episodes, so their PAUSE deltas flip sign with the cost assumption.

Multiple testing: about 30 calendar tags x 4 underlyings x 3 segments were scanned (t1_underlying.py). A Bonferroni-style bar is about t > 3.2. Out of sample, only the FOMC-eve overnight effect clears it, in SPY/QQQ/NVDA and real TQQQ/SPXL.

PDT: every 'D-' candidate uses one PDT slot per trade. The TOM+1..+3 set uses 3 slots in 3 consecutive sessions, which leaves none for emergencies. Quad witching uses 4/yr, FOMC 8/yr and TOM+2/+3 24/yr. The hold-through, shifted-entry and replacement forms use no PDT slots and need no extra cash.

If anything is pre-registered: (1) shadow-log E-TOM+3 at real 09:31 NVDL prices (next dates 2026-11-04 and 2026-12-03) and judge it at the 2027-01-11 quarterly review; it needs more history than that to be credible. (2) Optionally allow the FOMC-eve TQQQ night only while §3(f) has the overnight leg in cash. (3) Do not trade quad-witching SPXU live; the 2022+ data say the effect is gone.

candidates.name: SKIP_DOWN_SESSION (UPONLY): hold overnight only when NVDA is up on the session at 15:50
candidates.exact_rule: At the 15:48 ENTRY wake, read NVDA's regular-session official open for today and NVDA's last price at 15:50. If last_1550 >= open, run the normal §3(c)/§4 15:52 entry (NVDL first, then NVDX filler). If last_1550 < open, place no entry and hold cash overnight. The 09:31 exit is unchanged and the earnings-night blackout is unchanged. No day trade is involved: skipping is simply not buying.
candidates.in_sample: Rule fixed a priori as the mirror of §1, so there is no fitted parameter. Daily close->open 2x NVDA excluding earnings nights: 2001-2013H1 after-UP +0.295%/night vs after-DOWN -0.011% (diff t -2.31). 1-minute executable 15:50 signal, 1552->0931 2x gross: 2005-2015 UP +0.151% vs DOWN -0.038%.
candidates.out_of_sample: Daily 2013H2-2026: UP +0.385% vs DOWN +0.067% (diff t -2.96). 1-minute data, 2016-2021.03: UP +0.545% vs DOWN +0.128%. 2021.04-2026.03: UP +0.630% vs DOWN +0.014%. REAL NVDL 2022-12..2026-03: UP +0.708% (t 4.1, n374) vs DOWN +0.006% (n349). Last 2y daily: diff -0.243% (t -0.8), same direction. BUT the most recent regime is reversed: last 1y daily UP +0.180% vs DOWN +0.533%; RH 5m real NVDL 2026-02-23..10-13 UP +0.181% vs DOWN +0.324% (n158, not significant). In 2026-04..10 the rule made ~$13/yr vs ~$45/yr for the current rule (0.07%/side). Calendar years better than the current rule: 16 of 22 at 0.07%/side, 20 of 22 at 0.15%/side. Bootstrap from 2016-2026, start E=103: P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) 10.0% vs 35.8% for the current rule; P(KILL within 250) 0.6% vs 5.4%; median E@250 151 vs 130. It also beats a random-half-of-nights control (14.4% / 110).
candidates.mechanism: NVDA-specific overnight continuation after up sessions: attention-driven overnight and pre-open buying after strong days (Berkman et al. 2012). Volatility clustering also concentrates gap-down risk after down sessions. 2016-2026: 58 of 1275 down-session nights were <= -6% (2x) vs 25 of 1350 up-session nights; 2005-2015: 46 vs 29. Not a market-wide effect: QQQ/SPY 2x show no difference, and only 6 of 11 large caps share the sign. It looks NVDA- and high-attention-specific (TSLA and MU have it too).

candidates.exact_rule: At 09:30 compare NVDA open to the prior close. If open < prior close, sell at 10:00; else sell at 09:31 as usual.
candidates.mechanism: Gap-down opening reversal: plausible, but it was arbitraged away after ~2021 and adds variance exactly on the worst nights.

candidates.name: COND_EXIT_1000_IF_GAPUP: exit at 10:00 only after a gap up
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA open > prior close, sell 10:00; else sell 09:31.
candidates.mechanism: None robust.

candidates.name: COND_ENTER_1500_IF_DOWN: enter at 15:00 when NVDA is below its open at 15:00, else 15:52
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA price at 15:00 < today's open, buy at 15:00; otherwise buy at 15:52. Exit 09:31.
candidates.mechanism: Down days keep falling into 15:50 (intraday momentum); buying early catches the decline.

candidates.name: COND_ENTER_1500_IF_UP: enter at 15:00 when NVDA is above its open at 15:00, else 15:52
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA at 15:00 >= open, buy at 15:00; otherwise 15:52. Exit 09:31.
candidates.mechanism: The old intraday-momentum effect is gone. The 15:00-15:45 drift is negative in recent years.

notes: The RULES §1 sentence 'after a down intraday session the next night averages ~2x better' is false over the long sample. Over 25 years of 2x NVDA (excluding earnings) the sign is the opposite: nights after UP sessions average +0.30..+0.49%/night and nights after DOWN sessions ~0. Both halves agree (t -2.3 and -3.0), as do 4 of 5 five-year blocks and 16 of 26 years. The claim holds only in the last ~12 months (t +1.0), the window it was drawn from. It should not be used, either as a rationale or as a 'skip nights after up sessions' rule; that rule (DOWNONLY) is strongly negative.

Main finding (promising): skip the night when NVDA is down on the session at 15:50. Signal = NVDA last price at 15:50 vs today's official open, checked at the existing 15:48 wake; no PDT slot. Results at 0.07%/side over 2016-2026:
- Keeps ~all the gross edge on ~half the nights.
- Per-trade net +0.382% (t 4.3) vs +0.149% for the current rule.
- CAGR +45% vs +24%; maxDD -46% vs -66%.
- Bootstrap P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) ~10% vs ~36%; P(KILL within 250) 0.6% vs 5.4%.
- It also beats a random-half-of-nights control, so the gain is not just lower exposure.
- Variant SKIP_BOTHDOWN (skip only if below both the open and the prior close) is slightly better (+$18/yr incremental) and close to break-even with the current rule in the 2026 regime, but it was chosen post hoc.

Main caveat: the current regime (2025-10..2026-10) is reversed. Down-session nights did better (real NVDL 2026-02..10: UP +0.18% vs DOWN +0.32%, not significant). Over 2026-04..10 UPONLY made ~$13/yr vs ~$45/yr for the current rule; SKIP_BOTHDOWN made ~$42/yr. If adopted, pre-register it and judge it only at the quarterly review. Do not flip on short windows; 10 of 26 years show the reversed sign.

Cross-asset check: the UP/DOWN effect is absent in QQQ and SPY (2x) and mixed across 11 large caps (6 of 11 share the sign; strong in NVDA, TSLA, MU 2016-2026). Read it as an NVDA/high-attention-stock effect, not a law. The risk side is more robust: 2x nights <= -6% are 2.3x as frequent after down sessions as after up sessions (2016-2026: 58 vs 25) and 1.6x as frequent in 2005-2015 (46 vs 29).

Timing grid conclusion: the current 15:52 entry / 09:31 exit is at or near the best of the tested options.
- Entries at 15:00 or 15:30 lose 0.03-0.17%/night in the last 5 years.
- Entering at the close loses 0.065%/night (t -4.8): the 15:52->16:00 window has positive drift (15:52-15:55 +0.04..0.075% at 2x, t ~4). Avoid fills slipping toward 15:58.
- Later exits (09:45/10:00/10:30), unconditional or after a gap-down, worked in 2005-2021 but are ~0 since 2021 and raise PAUSE risk. All dead.

Costs. 52 live overnight legs measured against 1-minute bars: entry fill +0.02% vs the 15:52 price; exit +0.06% vs the 09:31 price (sd 0.42); round trip ~0.08%. So 0.07%/side (half-spread + 0.05%) is realistic. 0.15%/side is a stress case.

The current strategy depends heavily on costs and regime:
- At 0.15%/side the synthetic current rule is ~0 or negative even in 2016-2026 (-0.011%/trade). In 2005-2015 it is negative at either cost level (CAGR -32% at 0.07%/side).
- The 10-year bootstrap gives P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) ~36% for the current rule, far above the ~4.5% from the earlier 1-year bootstrap. 2x NVDA overnight sd is ~3.3% over 10 years vs ~2.6% in the recent calm year.
- The skip rules cut this risk the most.

Data:
- Robinhood intraday history is short: hourly from 2025-12-22, 30-minute from 2026-01-30, 5-minute from 2026-02-23.
- The 10-year intraday tests therefore use a third-party 1-minute dataset (HuggingFace mito0o852/OHLCV-1m, 2005-01..2026-03), downloaded by the sibling wf3/intraday-momentum worker and read here as data only.
- Validation: the 1-minute 16:00 price matches the RH official close within 1% on 5341 of 5342 NVDA days. Synthetic 2x vs real NVDL 15:52->09:31 correlation is 0.996, with real 0.05%/night lower (applied as drag).
- The RH split-adjusted NVDA daily series is mis-scaled (~10x) before 2000-10-30, so those bars were dropped.
- NVDA earnings nights: known dates for 2019+; before that a max-volume-ratio heuristic (22 of 31 hits on known dates). Earnings nights are cash in every variant.

Dollar figures (expected_dollars_per_year_at_E103) are INCREMENTAL vs the current 15:52/09:31 every-night rule. They are arithmetic, at fixed E=$103, 0.88 exposure and 0.07%/side, over 2016-01..2026-10 (timing variants: paired diffs over 2016-2026.03). t_stat is the per-trade net t for the skip rules and the paired-difference t vs the current rule for the timing variants.

sweeps.family: OPENING-GAP AND OPENING-AUCTION EFFECTS (SPY/QQQ/IWM/NVDA gaps; 3x day trades 09:35->10:00/10:30; conditional replacement of the 09:31 overnight exit; gap-conditional entry/hold-through; pre-market and opening-auction exit)

candidates.name: C1-A: Conditional exit delay (NVDA gap-down >= 3% -> sell overnight leg at 10:00) [RECOMMENDED form]
candidates.exact_rule: Applies only to the existing overnight NVDL/NVDX position bought at 15:52 the previous day; on NVDA earnings nights the leg is already in cash. At 09:30:30 ET compare NVDA's official opening print with its prior official close. If NVDA open <= -3.0%: skip the 09:31 sell and run the §5 exit mechanics at 10:00:00 ET instead (marketable limit at bid - max(0.02, 0.15%), then the same re-price ladder). Set no stop between 09:31 and 10:00. Stop variants tested: an NVDA -1% stop below the 09:31 price turns +1.98%/event into -0.17%; -1.5% gives +0.89%; -2% gives +1.92%; -3% gives +1.84%. If anything, use only a catastrophic stop. On all other mornings keep the 09:31 exit. A late wake after 10:00 sells immediately. Triggering on NVDA's 09:31 trade <= -3% instead of the open gives the same result (n=81, +2.02%, t 3.7).
candidates.instrument: NVDL / NVDX (2x NVDA), signal = NVDA official open vs prior close
candidates.in_sample: H1 2011-07..2018-12, synthetic daily-reset 2x NVDA built from 1-min bars, return from 09:31 to 10:00 vs the 09:31 exit: n=16, +3.91% per event on the 2x position (t 3.3), median +2.98, win 94%.
candidates.out_of_sample: H2 2019-01..2026-10: n=56, +1.37%/event (t 2.1), median +0.47, 10%-trimmed +0.87, excluding top 3 +0.61, worst -6.14. Last 2y (2024-10-14..2026-10-13): n=13, +1.61 (t 1.4), median +0.82, but excluding top 3 = -0.02, so the recent mean is carried by crash-open rebounds (2024-08-05 +20%, 2025-04-07 +14%, 2025-01-27 +4.4%). Pre-period 2005..2011-06: n=31, +2.13 (t 2.1). 14 of 18 calendar years with events are positive. Real ETFs agree: NVDL 2023-09..2026-09 n=19, real +2.08%/event (t 1.6) vs synthetic +1.99%, corr 0.998; NVDX n=16, real +2.57%. Overnight-leg paired effect (93% exposure, 0.30% RT cost, earnings nights in cash): +0.032%/night over all nights (t 3.6, 2005-2026), +0.031 (t 2.0) in H2, +0.034 (t 1.3) in the last 2y. Block bootstrap, 60 sessions, from $103: P(PAUSE) 33.1->30.4% (2011+ data), 44.5->41.5% (2019+), 42.6->39.8% (last 2y); P(KILL) 0.42->0.22%, 0.82->0.34%, 0.80->0.24%; log growth/session 2019+ +0.021->+0.056%.
candidates.mechanism: Market-wide opening overreaction and liquidity provision. Overnight sellers, stop and market-on-open orders, and futures-led panic all hit the opening print. The first 30 minutes then revert as liquidity returns. The same 09:31->10:00 bounce after gaps <= -3% appears in all four underlyings (SPY +0.84% n=12, QQQ +1.68% n=18, IWM +0.44% n=23, NVDA +0.91% n=69, underlying %). It does not appear after NVDA-only gap-downs (market gap > -1%: n=12, +0.14%; H2 -0.78%), so it is a market-panic effect, not NVDA-specific. The bounce largely ends by 10:00: NVDA 10:00->15:50 after such gaps is -0.10% (H2 -0.27%).

candidates.name: Idiosyncratic NVDA gap-down exit delay (NVDA <= -3% but QQQ/SPY gap > -1%)
candidates.exact_rule: Delay the exit to 10:00 only when the NVDA gap-down is not market-wide.
candidates.mechanism: Diagnostic split: stock-specific gaps reflect news being priced and do not revert at the open.

candidates.name: Gap-down hold-through (NVDA <= -3%: skip the 09:31 exit and the 15:52 re-entry, hold to next morning)
candidates.exact_rule: If NVDA open <= -3%, do not sell the overnight leg at 09:31; hold it through the session and the next night (sell at next morning's 09:31). Delta = 2x return 09:31->15:52 + 0.30% round-trip cost saved.
candidates.mechanism: Captures the 09:31-10:00 rebound plus the cost saving, but then holds the flat-to-negative rest of the session at 2x. Dominated by C1-A: similar mean, worst event -14.3% vs -6.1%, lower t.

candidates.name: Gap-down early entry of the overnight leg (buy NVDL at 10:00 or 10:30 instead of 15:52)
candidates.exact_rule: On a gap-down day, enter the overnight NVDL position at 10:00 (or 10:30) rather than 15:52. This is not a day trade if it is held overnight. Delta = 2x return T->15:52.
candidates.mechanism: The rebound is over by 10:00; the rest of a gap-down session drifts lower (QQQ 10:00->15:50 after gap <= -3%: -0.49%).

candidates.name: Unconditional exit delay (sell the overnight leg at 09:35/09:45/10:00 every day instead of 09:31)

candidates.mechanism: Gap-ups fade in the first 30-60 minutes. This confirms the current 09:31 exit is right on gap-up mornings.

notes: Bottom line: no day trade in this family clears the bar; the PDT slots stay idle. The one useful change is to the 09:31 overnight exit: after a large market-wide gap-down, sell at 10:00 instead of 09:31 (C1-A, or C1-D as the alternative). It uses no PDT slot, adds no cost, and does not affect the 15:52 entry.

C1 numbers: about +$8-9/yr at E=103 (+0.03%/night averaged over all nights). It lowers simulated 60-session P(PAUSE) by about 3 points and roughly halves P(KILL), because it acts on the worst nights. Pre-register ONE form, either A (NVDA open <= -3%) or D (QQQ open <= -1.5%), with exit at 10:00 and no tight stop.

Recent-decay caution on C1: since 2019 the per-event median is only about +0.4-0.5% for A and D (+0.1% for the -1% trigger). Over the last 2 years the mean excluding the top 3 events is about 0. The expectancy rests on crash-open rebounds (2024-08-05, 2025-01-27, 2025-04-07). That skew helps PAUSE risk, but most live events will look small or negative.

Multiple testing: I tried thresholds -1..-5%, 9 exit times from 09:35 to 15:50, NVDA vs market triggers, and stops. The effect is robust as a family rather than at one setting: it grows with gap size, every exit from 09:40 to 10:30 is positive, it appears in all four underlyings, and every subperiod and real NVDL/NVDX agree. In/out-of-sample labels are by time (H1 2011-07..2018, H2 2019+, last 2y, 2005..2011-06), but the threshold was chosen after seeing all the data.

Operational notes for C1: the 2x position typically dips about another 2.5% after 09:31 before rebounding. On NVDA <= -3% days, the 09:30-10:00 low was more than 0.5% below the 09:31 price on 83% of days. A tight stop destroys the edge: an NVDA -1% stop turns +1.98 into -0.17%/event. The 10:00 exit needs the always-on loop (or a 09:58 one-off wake); if it is missed, sell immediately per §5.

Data limits: Robinhood intraday history is real only for the last few months. 30-min/hour bars start about 2025-12/2026-01, 5-min about 2026-02-23 (fully real from 2026-03-23), and 1-min only the last ~5 weeks. Everything earlier is interpolated filler with constant prices (e.g. SPY 773.28 in 2015). For history I used a third-party 1-min set (HuggingFace mito0o852/OHLCV-1m, 2005-01..2026-03) that the intraday-momentum sibling had downloaded; I only read it. I checked it against Robinhood official daily open/close. From 2011 on the agreement is good (median open-to-close error 0.005-0.04%). In 2005-2010 there are many mismatches (e.g. SPY 94 bad days in 2010), so that period is a robustness check only. For 2026-04..10, 5-min bars have no 09:31 price, so the official open stands in for it.

NVDA earnings dates: the Robinhood earnings API confirms 2026-05-20. The list in wf2/joint-risk/prep.py has 2026-05-27, which is wrong; wf/risk/load.py has it right. Before 2018 I used a conservative heuristic, excluding both the highest volume-ratio day and the largest-gap day in Feb/May/Aug/Nov. Volume ratio alone matched only 26 of 34 known dates.

Side finding outside this family, relevant to the overnight-timing reviewer: modeled with the specified 0.15%/side cost, the baseline overnight leg (synthetic 2x NVDA, 15:52->09:31, 93% exposure, earnings nights in cash) is negative before 2019: -0.125%/night in 2005..2011-06 and -0.166%/night in 2011-07..2018. It is +0.079%/night in 2019..2026-10 and +0.015%/night over the last 2 years. Gross 2x NVDA overnight was only about +0.12-0.17%/night before 2019, so the 0.30% round trip decides whether the core edge exists. Real NVDL fill costs should be measured; the C1 comparison is unaffected because it adds no cost.

Daily long-sample context (Robinhood 2000-2026, official open/close): NVDA ex-earnings after gaps <= -3%, open->close +1.20% (t 2.9, n=216; 2000-12 +1.30, 2013-26 +1.02, last 2y +1.02 n=14); QQQ after gaps <= -3%, +1.31% (t 2.7, n=39). In 2011+ intraday data most of this is 09:31->10:00, and 10:00->close is flat to negative (NVDA -0.10, QQQ -0.49, SPY -0.32, IWM -0.72), which is why early-entry and hold-through variants are dead or dominated. Gap-ups show no consistent continuation or fade.

sweeps.family: EVERYTHING ELSE FOR IDLE CAPITAL (09:31-15:52): cash-like ETFs, cross-sectional and pair relative value, other documented anomalies (asset-class intraday drift, short-vol, bitcoin, single-stock attention effects)

candidates.name: A1 Park cash in a T-bill ETF intraday (SGOV; BIL/USFR/TFLO/SHV also checked)
candidates.exact_rule: After the 09:31 NVDL/NVDX exit fills, buy floor(0.98*E/ask) SGOV at the ask at 09:32 and sell at the bid at 15:50, on every PDT-allowed day (cap 2 per rolling 5 sessions, about 100 per year).
candidates.instrument: SGOV (also BIL, USFR, TFLO; SHV at $110.18 cannot be bought at E=$103)
candidates.in_sample: Long-sample open->close: BIL 2017-2021 +0.0021%/d (t 6.0); SHV 2007-2026 +0.0015%/d (t 5.5); SGOV 2020-05..2021 -0.0015%/d (t -4.5). In 2017-2021 the daily accrual was near zero.
candidates.out_of_sample: SGOV 2023-2026 open->close +0.0007%/d (t 2.7) against non-ex-date close->open +0.0169%/d, so only 4% of the daily accrual shows up intraday. Last 2y: +0.0010%/d, 6%. BIL 3-4%, SHV 9-11%, USFR/TFLO 11-13%. One 1-cent tick is 0.0099% of SGOV's price (quote 100.53/100.54 on 2026-10-14). Net of spread only: -0.0090%/trade (t -29) over the last 2y.
candidates.mechanism: T-bill ETF NAV accrues by calendar day, and the opening print already includes the new day's accrual. An intraday holder therefore captures about 0. Ex-date drops happen at the open, and the distribution requires owning the shares before the ex-date. The gross ceiling, holding $100 intraday every session at zero cost, is about $0.25/yr. Spread-only cost gives -$0.90/yr; the instructed cost (half-spread + 0.05% per side) gives -$10.96/yr.

candidates.name: A2 Earn T-bill yield without a day trade (residual cash, or a T-bill ETF instead of NVDA-2x overnight)
candidates.exact_rule: (i) Put cash left over after the 15:52 basket into SGOV overnight; or (ii) buy SGOV at 09:32 and sell at the next day's 09:31; or (iii) hold SGOV overnight instead of NVDL/NVDX.
candidates.out_of_sample: SGOV non-ex close->open 2023-2026 is +0.0169%/night (about 4.3%/yr), versus the NVDA-2x planning edge of +0.30%/night, about 18 times larger. (i) is impossible in whole shares: the leftover after NVDL plus NVDX filler is under about $20, and one share of SGOV is $100.54, BIL $91.53, USFR $50.47. (ii) ties up the cash the 15:52 entry needs. (iii) gives up most of the edge.
candidates.mechanism: Yield accrues to whoever holds the shares at the close or overnight. The only window that is free is intraday, and it carries no accrual (A1). No cash yield can be captured without a day trade while the cash has to be free at 15:52.
candidates.data_used: As A1, plus quotes for SGOV, BIL, USFR, NVDL ($35.29) and NVDX ($19.85) on 2026-10-14.

candidates.name: B3 Intraday short volatility (long a -1x VIX-futures product such as SVIX, or SVXY) 09:32-15:50
candidates.exact_rule: On every PDT-allowed day, buy the -1x short-term VIX-futures ETF (synthesized from VIXY: (1-r_cc)/(1-r_co)-1) at 09:32 and sell at 15:50. SVXY actual is the -0.5x variant.

candidates.instrument: XLE / XLU / XLB / XLF / XLP (1x sector SPDRs)
candidates.in_sample: 2006-2015, 1x, unconstrained: n=311, +0.314%/trade (t 1.8), +0.442 relative to equal-weight sectors (t 4.0). The effect sits in 2006-2009; 2010-2015 is about 0 (n about 54). After the PDT cap of 2, affordable-5 filter and costs: +0.084 (t 0.4).
candidates.out_of_sample: 2016-2026 unconstrained: n=428, +0.192 (t 2.4). Last 2y: n=119, +0.168 (t 1.2). 2026 30-minute check, 73 events: open->close +0.196, 10:00->close +0.149, so the 09:32 entry is not only an opening-print artifact. After PDT cap 2, affordable-5 filter and costs: H2 +0.081 (t 0.8), last 2y +0.010 (t 0.1), about 23 trades/yr. candidates.exact_rule: z = (co_A - beta*co_B)/sd, with beta and sd from a trailing 250-session regression of overnight returns. If z < -1.5 (or < -2), buy A at the open and sell at the close as a single leg. A hedged pair would need 2 PDT slots.

candidates.name: D1 Single-stock gap-down laggard intraday rebound (24 large caps)
candidates.exact_rule: Each day, take the stock with the most negative (gap - cross-sectional mean gap) among AAPL MSFT AMZN GOOGL JPM BAC WFC C XOM CVX PFE MRK KO PEP WMT HD INTC CSCO ORCL T F DIS MCD CAT. If it is < -2%, buy at the open and sell at the close.
candidates.mechanism: There is no reliable rebound after idiosyncratic gap-downs, which are mostly news or earnings and tend to continue. This is consistent with the literature: the attention effect is buy-side. The sample uses today's survivors, so it is biased upward if anything.
candidates.data_used: Robinhood daily bars 2006-2026 for 24 large caps.

candidates.name: D2 Fade attention-driven gap-ups (Berkman et al. 2012) via single-stock inverse ETFs
candidates.exact_rule: If a name with a listed inverse ETF (AAPL AMZN MSFT GOOGL META NVDA TSLA AMD NFLX) opens more than 3% above its prior close in excess of SPY's gap, buy its -1x (or -2x) inverse at 09:32 and sell at 15:50; if several qualify, take the largest gap. Cost: 0.15% per side.
candidates.instrument: Single-stock inverse ETFs (AAPD, AMZD, MSFD, GGLS, METD, NVDQ/NVD, TSLS/TSLQ, ...)
candidates.in_sample: The documented effect appears in staid large caps without inverse ETFs (19 names). Gap - SPY gap > 5%: 1x open->close 2006-2015 -0.750 (t -1.7); > 3%: -0.287 (t -1.1). In the most-positive-relative-gap cross-section of 24 names (> 3%): -0.880 (t -2.7).
candidates.mechanism: Retail buying at the open inflates gap-ups in low-attention large caps, which then revert intraday. That effect is real here, but harvesting it needs a short, which is not allowed. The only names with inverse ETFs are high-momentum, retail-heavy stocks whose gap-ups continue. The single-stock inverse ETFs date from 2022 and have wide spreads.
candidates.data_used: Robinhood daily bars 2006-2026 for 28 stocks (24 above plus META 2012+, TSLA 2010+, AMD, NFLX), NVDA and SPY.

notes: Bottom line: none of the 11 candidates in this family adds expected growth after realistic costs with out-of-sample support. The best one (C1, sector gap-laggard) makes about +0.08%/trade net, t 0.7, about $0.9/yr at E=$103, and fails replication on a sister universe of industry ETFs. Recommendation: leave the 09:31-15:52 cash idle and keep the 3 PDT slots reserved for emergency same-day exits of the overnight leg (RULES_v3 section 7).

Cash yield is not capturable. T-bill ETF accrual (SGOV/BIL/SHV/USFR/TFLO) shows up about 87-97% at the open (2023-2026 non-ex close->open +0.014..0.017%/d versus open->close +0.0005..0.0024%/d). Intraday SGOV carry is about 1/10 of a 1-cent tick. Even a free intraday hold every session would earn about $0.25/yr on $100. With a day trade it nets -0.009%/trade on spread alone, or -0.109% at the instructed cost. Without a day trade the cash cannot be free at 15:52. Leftover cash after the basket (under about $20) cannot buy a whole share of any T-bill ETF. Uninvested-cash sweep interest is tied to end-of-day balances, and at the end of the day the cash is in NVDL/NVDX; this is qualitative, not measured.

Multiple testing: 32 ETFs scanned for intraday drift, 15 pairs x 4 rules, sector rules at 3 signals x 4-5 thresholds, and 2 stock universes. Only two effects reach full-sample |t| >= 3: EWJ intraday (+3.6 bp/d, t 3.4) and the staid-large-cap gap-up fade. The first is below cost; the second cannot be traded long-only.

Recurring pattern: effects that are strong in 2006-2015 (sector and pair overnight-to-intraday reversals; GDX, UNG and UUP intraday drift) vanish in 2016-2026. That is consistent with stale opening prints in early ETF data and with arbitrage. Do not adopt any rule supported mainly by pre-2012 daily open prices.

Data limits: Robinhood 30-minute history exists only from 2026-01-30 (earlier bars are interpolated), and 5-minute data is similar. Long-sample tests therefore use the official daily open as the entry. The open-to-09:32 haircut could only be checked on 2026 for C1: 10:00->close kept +0.149 of the +0.196 open->close.

No joint overnight + intraday PAUSE bootstrap was run, because no candidate passed the after-cost out-of-sample screen. B2, B3, B4 and D2 have single-day tails of -11% to -49% on leveraged or inverse products and would raise PAUSE and KILL risk materially. C1 at 1x (52-96% of E, about 21 trades/yr, worst -11.7% in 2008 and -6.3% since 2016) would add little variance and little return.

Overnight effects found incidentally (out of scope; a second overnight instrument cannot be funded): GLD close->open +0.051%/d (t 4.2) with open->close about 0; XBI close->open +0.085%/d (t 6.7); GBTC close->open including weekends +0.325%/d (t 4.5); IBIT +0.187 (t 2.1).
PDT arithmetic: a hedged pair uses 2 day trades per signal. A greedy cap of 2 per rolling 5 sessions, keeping 1 slot in reserve, cut C1 from 40 to about 21-23 trades/yr and lowered its net mean.

Scripts (python3) and data are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/wf3/cash-and-other/: a_cash.py and a_cash2.py (+a_cash2.json), b_scan.py, b_ewj.py, c_sector*.py, c_sector_m30.py, c_industry.py, c_pairs.py, d_vix.py, d_btc.py, d_stocks.py, d_leader.py, e_sector_sim.py (+e_sector_sim.json), f_misc.py; raw Robinhood JSON is in data/. SPY/QQQ/IWM/NVDA daily bars were reused read-only from wf3/intraday-momentum/rh/rhday_a.json and rhday_b.json.

candidate.name: B9 Full-size early overnight entry on an NVDA noise-band breakout
candidate.exact_rule: Skipped on NVDA earnings days. For each checkpoint h in {11:00, 11:30, ..., 15:30}: sigma_h = mean over the prior 14 sessions of |NVDA(h)/NVDA open - 1|, and UB_h = max(today's open, prior close) x (1+sigma_h). At the first h where NVDA's price at h is above UB_h, buy the whole §3(c) NVDL/NVDX position at h+1 min (marketable limit) instead of at 15:52. Hold to 09:31 as usual. No stop and no same-day sell. If there is no breakout, enter at 15:52.
candidate.instrument: NVDL / NVDX (synthetic 2x NVDA; on real NVDL signal days 2023-03..2026-10: n=226, +0.197%, t 1.35, corr 0.989 with synthetic)
candidate.in_sample: H1 2005-01..2015-11: n=748 signal nights, +0.196%/signal night, t 1.84
candidate.mechanism: Volatility-scaled breakout momentum (Zarattini et al. 2024): once NVDA leaves its usual intraday range, dealer gamma hedging and the rebalancing of NVDA single-stock leveraged ETFs (NVDL/NVDX/NVDU) push the same way into the close. Entering every night at 11:01 earns +0.026% (t 0.58), so the edge is conditional, not drift. Lower-band breakdown days go the other way (-0.139%). No added trading cost, since it replaces the 15:52 fill. The catch is tail risk: worst afternoon -17.75% (2020-03-20) and sd 2.76%/signal night. In a joint block bootstrap with the overnight leg, P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) rises from 26.5% to 33.7% (2y), 28.4% to 35.4% (8y) and 26.1% to 31.9% (2005-2026). Log growth/session changes by -6.1 / +3.8 / +4.5 bp. This fails the do-not-raise-PAUSE goal.
candidate.data_used: 1-min NVDA 2005-01..2026-03 (HF mito0o852/OHLCV-1m) + RH 10-min tail; real NVDL 1-min 2022-12..2026-03 and RH 10-min to 2026-10-13 for validation; earnings-proxy days excluded
candidate.family: INTRADAY MOMENTUM (Gao-Han-Li-Zhou 2018 first/last half-hour; LETF-rebalancing into the close; Zarattini-Aziz-Barbon 2024 noise-band breakout; plus moving the NVDL overnight entry earlier or later than 15:52)

votes.candidate: B9 Full-size early overnight entry on an NVDA noise-band breakout
reasons: It fails the stated goal, and I confirmed this independently. I ran a joint 5-day-block bootstrap: 60-session paths, 93% exposure, earnings nights in cash, PAUSE = E <= 0.8 x the rolling 20-session high. Adding B9 raises P(PAUSE) in every window: 29.0% -> 35.0% for 2005-2026, 36.2% -> 43.1% for the last 8y, and 31.0% -> 38.0% for the last 2y. It also lowers 5th-percentile 60-session equity in every window. In the last 2y it lowers log growth per session (25.1 -> 23.6 bp). Raising PAUSE by 6-7 points is material.

The first half never established the edge on its own. Re-derived from the raw 1-min data, H1 (2005-01..2015-11) gives +0.189% at t 1.79. If the noise band uses the official opening print (RH daily open) instead of the first 1-min trade, H1 falls to +0.123% at t 1.21. Most of the full-sample significance comes from H2.

The windows that matter for live trading show nothing. On synthetic 2x NVDA over the last 2y (2024-10-14+): n=118, -0.038%, t -0.16, median -0.254%. Rolling 2y mean last value is -0.023%, with a minimum of -0.172% on 2026-07-07. The 2025-26 two-year block gives +0.021%. On real NVDL prices on my signal days, 2023-01..2026-10: n=244, +0.140%, t 0.95, median +0.036%. Real NVDL over the last 2y: n=117, -0.043%, t -0.18, median -0.231%.

This is a max-of-many result. The generating agent's final*.txt files hold about 95 full-sample variant results. 20 of them have |t| > 2, and B9's t 3.27 is the largest. My clean re-derivation gives t 2.99 (2.57 with the official open). Two-sided p is about 0.003-0.01. A family-wise correction over even about 20 effective tests leaves it borderline, around 0.06-0.2.

The stated mechanism is contradicted by when the effect appears. The effect is present in 2005-2015, when no NVDA single-stock LETF existed. It disappears in 2024-26, when NVDL/NVDX/NVDU assets and rebalancing flows are largest. So LETF rebalancing does not explain it.

The edge sits almost entirely in the first checkpoint and in a few large days. Entries at 11:00 give n=852, +0.276%, t 2.69. Breakouts from 13:00 to 15:30 (n=279) average about 0%, which does not fit 'breakout momentum at any time'. Dropping the best 10 signal days gives +0.144% (t 2.08); dropping the best 20 gives +0.090% (t 1.33).

In fairness, the long sample is not a pure artifact. It holds when the checkpoint grid is shifted (11:05..11:25 starts: +0.21..+0.23%, t 3.0-3.3, but last 2y -0.21..+0.04%). It holds for fill lags of 0-10 min (about +0.216%) and across lookbacks 5-60 and multipliers 0.5-2.0 (+0.13..+0.49%, all t >= 2.3). 17 of 22 years are positive (year-level t 3.20), and a month-block bootstrap gives P(mean <= 0) = 0.0008. It also replicates on SPY 2x (+0.084%, t 2.99) and QQQ 2x (+0.126%, t 3.01), but not IWM (+0.032%, t 0.87). So the historical phenomenon is probably real but small. The problem is that the full-size implementation buys it with materially higher PAUSE risk, and there is no evidence it persists in the current regime.

Candidate reported +0.236%, t 3.27.
With the RH official open in the band: ALL +0.183% t 2.57, H1 +0.123% t 1.21, H2 +0.244% t 2.45, L2 -0.060%.
Earnings exclusion choices: candidate's top-4-next-gap proxy +0.219% (t 3.02, L2 -0.084%); no exclusion +0.224% (t 3.12).
Unconditional 11:01 entry on every night: +0.019% (t 0.43). Lower-band breakdown days: -0.203% (t -2.46).

Outlier sensitivity: winsorized at 1% +0.218% (t 3.18); drop best 10 +0.144% (t 2.08); drop best 20 +0.090% (t 1.33). Year-level: 17/22 years positive, t 3.20. Month-block bootstrap P(mean <= 0) = 0.0008, 90% CI +0.106..+0.337%.

Real NVDL on signal days, 2023-01-23..2026-10-05: n=244, +0.140%, t 0.95, median +0.036%, corr 0.992 with synthetic. Last 2y: n=117, -0.043%, t -0.18, median -0.231%. Charging an extra 0.05% entry cost gives +0.090% (t 0.61).

Partial-size variant (about 34% of E, i.e. 1 NVDL share, bought early; the rest at 15:52): P(PAUSE) 29.0 -> 29.3% (full), 36.2 -> 37.0% (8y), 31.0 -> 31.8% (2y). Log growth +1.8 / +1.5 / -0.4 bp/session.
votes.survives_if: Full-size B9 as written does not survive. It raises PAUSE by 6-7 points in every window, and its edge is about zero in the last 2y and statistically insignificant on real NVDL. A different, smaller variant might be acceptable: buy only 1 NVDL share (about 34% of E) early on an 11:00-11:30 breakout, keep the rest of the 15:52 entry unchanged. In my bootstrap that adds only 0.3-0.8 points of PAUSE, for about +1.5-1.8 bp/session of long-run log growth (-0.4 bp in the last 2y). reasons: The mechanics hold up under this lens. Buying the share early only moves the time of a purchase that would otherwise happen at 15:52. It fails on the actual instrument at realistic latency. Each morning the agent would have to compute 10 noise-band thresholds (14-session mean of |P_h/open-1| per checkpoint), wake exactly at each :00/:30 from 11:00 to 15:30, and place the order within about 1 minute. Risk and growth, from my own paired joint block bootstrap (5-day blocks, 6000 paths, fraction 0.37, overnight leg net of 0.10%, true earnings nights in cash). Data-snooping: by the candidate's own account, this variant came after the pre-specified (b) variants failed, and the strong numbers come mostly from pre-NVDL years. After 2016-04: n 13, +0.533% (t 1.20), median +0.08%, carried by 2022-06-15 (+3.49%) and 2022-07-27 (+4.44%).

At E=$103 and 75% weight the realized historical value is about $0.85/yr, not $2.80/yr. §3(f) has not fired in the last 257 nights, so the near-term expected value is about $0. No live sample at this frequency can ever validate the conditional subset.

What survives is the underlying 1x effect, and it is not refuted. The QQQ FOMC-eve close->open is +0.252% (t 4.95); first half +0.214% (t 2.84); second half +0.290% (t 4.20); +0.208% (t 4.52) without the mega-cap nights. Neighboring nights (k=-3,-2,-1,+1,+2) are all near zero (|t|<1.6). A permutation test against random nights matched on year and weekday gives one-sided p 0.011 for the first half and 0.004 for the second. So the phenomenon is real, but its 3x after-cost form clears zero robustly only after 2016.

In normal mode the NVDA-2x leg already holds overnight into FOMC day; the generator's own numbers give +0.93% gross on those nights (t 4.1), and swapping to TQQQ there scored -0.17%. So the candidate adds nothing outside cash mode, and the only nights it acts on are the sparse, unvalidated ones in cash mode.

votes.survives_if: It survives only as a low-stakes optional rule, and only if the reviewer accepts two things. First, the published pre-FOMC literature plus the robust 1x QQQ/SPY effect (both halves t>2.8, neighbor nights flat) must stand in for leveraged after-cost evidence in the first half, which is absent. Second, its value must be restated honestly: about $0-1/yr, about 1.8 qualifying nights/yr when §3(f) is active, and +0.31%/event (not +0.46%) once coincident mega-cap earnings nights are removed. A stronger case would need either a pre-registered shadow log of all FOMC eves, at executable 15:52->09:31 TQQQ prices with net mean >= +0.3% over >= 24 events, or evidence that real TQQQ round-trip costs are <= ~0.10%. votes.candidate: FOMC-eve TQQQ while the overnight leg is in cash mode (conditional)
reasons: The trade costs too little in fees for costs to sink it. TQQQ was quoted 75.92/75.93, a 1-cent spread (half-spread about 0.007%). A realistic round trip is about 0.10-0.12%, not the 0.30% the candidate assumed. Even at 0.40% round trip the full-sample mean stays positive (+0.356%, t 2.33).

It is feasible mechanically. A 15:52 buy and 09:31 sell is not a PDT day trade. In cash mode the cash is idle by definition, so the 15:52 entry has no conflict. One share (about $76) is 74% of E. TQQQ's highest close in the last 12 months ($87.22) stays under the 0.98*E cap of about $101. The worst night (-9.09% synthetic, 2011-03-14) times 74% is about -6.7% of E. With the rest of the account flat that cannot trigger PAUSE (needs -20%) or KILL.

It fails on materiality. By design it trades only while §3(f) has the overnight leg in cash. That switch has never fired live (the rules note a +0.05% trailing-120 minimum over 257 nights). On my reconstruction of the switch (gross 2x NVDA close->open, Monday checks, earnings nights excluded by proxy), cash mode covered about 25% of nights from 2000 to 2026. That gives 40 FOMC eves in 20.8 years, about 1.9 trades a year, not 7.9. Expected value at E=$103 is about $0.68-0.97 a year. The headline $2.80 a year assumes cash mode all year, which never happened in the history. Live to date the value is $0.

Where it would actually trade, the evidence is weak. The 40 cash-mode FOMC eves average +0.655% net (t 2.11), but most of that is 2008-09. Without 2008-09 it is +0.373% (t 1.30, n 28). Each half is t 1.49 (2006-15, n 25) and t 1.59 (2016-26, n 15), and 2010-2026 is t 1.36. Neither half is significant on its own.

The unconditional effect reproduces (+0.456%, t 2.98, n 165) but is fragile. Before mid-2011 it was +0.135% (t 0.40, n 44). Without the 5 best nights the mean is +0.27%. It is much stronger in megacap-earnings months (Jan/Apr/May/Jul/Oct/Nov: +0.676%, t 2.59) than in the other months (+0.282%, t 1.57), so part of it is earnings-night contamination. 2020-11-04 (+6.5%) was the night after the US election. With about 15 calendar-effect tests in this family, t 2.98 only just clears a Bonferroni bar.

I could not check the gap between actual fills (15:52 entry, 09:31 exit) and the daily close/open prices the backtest uses. Robinhood intraday history for TQQQ starts only on 2026-01-30 at 30-minute resolution, and earlier minute and 5-minute requests returned only filler bars. The model's close->open prices are unverified at executable times for every FOMC eve.

votes.candidate: E-TOM+3: move the NVDL entry to 09:31 on the 3rd trading day of the month
reasons: The headline numbers reproduce from fresh Robinhood daily bars, so this is not an arithmetic error. I used synthetic 2x NVDA with the exact daily-reset formula, a 0.08% haircut and 0.30% saved per round trip. Results: 2006-2026 +1.350%/event (t 3.09, n 250), 2006-2016 +1.625% (t 2.45), 2016-2026 +1.096% (t 1.90), last 2y -0.460% (t -0.66, n 24). Real NVDL TOM+3 intraday minus overnight: +1.724% (t 1.44, n 46). The refutation rests on how fragile these numbers are, not on whether they compute.

Points in the candidate's favour, stated honestly. The cell holds in the pre-2006 sample, which the candidate never used: 1999-10 to 2005, NVDA excess +1.48% (t 2.05), QQQ +0.59% (t 2.06), winsorized t 2.11. A within-month permutation of 23 day-of-month cells gives family-wise p 0.034 for 2006-2026 and p<0.001 for 1999-2026. A Mann-Whitney test on 2006-2026 gives p 0.013. So the historical pattern is probably not pure mining.

An honest walk-forward fails. Each year I picked the best of 23 TOM cells by trailing NVDA t-stat and traded it the next year. The out-of-sample gains are not significant: K=5y +0.141%/event (t 0.47), K=7y +0.459% (t 1.11), K=10y +0.602% (t 1.51). With K=10, a forward-looking trader would have dropped TOM+3 for TOM+11 or TOM+12 in 2019-2025. TOM+3 looks special mainly with full-sample hindsight.

The edge is tail-driven. 10 of 250 events (2006+) supply 243.8 of the 337.5 total points (72%). The mean of the other 240 events is +0.39%/event, against +0.08% for a swap on any day. The two largest events are not turn-of-month flow effects:
- 2024-08-05, the yen-carry crash: +50.4%.
- 2008-07-03, NVDA's unscheduled profit-warning gap of -28% overnight: +43.9%.

The skip-if-earnings filter cannot remove events like these.

The real-NVDL evidence comes from one crash day and the 2023 cluster. With 2024-08-05 removed it drops from +2.02% to +0.95% (t 1.75), and to +0.77% (t 1.47) with 2025-04-03 also removed. The 2023 events alone give +2.31% (t 3.38, n 12). Real NVDL last 2y: -0.374% (t -0.56). 2025-2026: -0.566% (t -0.79, n 22).

The effect is decaying and the most recent window fails. NVDA TOM+3 excess by period: 1999-2005 +1.48%, 2006-2015 +0.79%, 2016-2026 +0.56%, last 2y -0.12%. The last 2y sit about 2.1 standard errors below the 2006-2026 estimate of +0.673%, and the last-2y Mann-Whitney p is 0.63. A linear trend fitted from 1999 projects the gain now at +0.18%/event.

The NVDA-specific part, which makes the magnitude about 3x QQQ, has gone. NVDA's id-on residual over its QQQ beta (1.58) on TOM+3 was +0.59% (t 1.98) in 2006-2015. It was +0.15% (t 0.84) in 2016-2026 and -0.59% (t -1.86) in the last 2y. So the $15/yr magnitude rests on a component that has not held up.

The market-wide mechanism is weak where it should be strongest. SPY's TOM+3 ranks 5th of 23 cells (family-wise p 0.70) and QQQ's 2006-2026 family-wise p is 0.35. In 2016-2026 TOM+3 is not even NVDA's top cell (TOM+17 has t 2.13), and several unrelated cells reach t 1.7-1.8. Cells with t around 2 are common in this family, and the candidate tested about 40 cells across event types.

The profile around TOM+3 has no shape. TOM+2 shows +0.16% (t 0.85) and TOM+4 +0.03% (t 0.14) in 2006-2026, which does not fit a smooth turn-of-month inflow story. The weak overnight into TOM+3 has no explanation, by the candidate's own admission.

Realistic forward value is about $2-7/yr, not $15.35, at roughly $96 deployed and 12 events a year:
- Excluding the top 10 events: +0.39%/event, about $4.5/yr.
- Walk-forward: +0.14% to +0.60%/event, about $1.6-6.9/yr.
- Last 2y: -0.46%/event, about -$5.3/yr.

The per-event sd is 6.6% (about $6.3), so the annual sd is about $22. Live trading could never confirm or refute the edge in any useful time.

Over at least 24 further events the mean gain must be above 0 after excluding crash-gap days with |overnight| > 8%, and the QQQ TOM+3 excess must stay positive. The case would also need a mechanism that explains why the effect sits only on TOM+3 and not on TOM+2 or TOM+4. If it were adopted anyway as a near-zero-cost swap (the any-day placebo is about 0), it should be planned at no more than +0.3-0.5%/event (about $4/yr), never $15/yr. votes.candidate: E-TOM+3: move the NVDL entry to 09:31 on the 3rd trading day of the month (flat on the TOM+2 night, hold from 09:31 TOM+3 to 09:31 TOM+4)
reasons: FEASIBILITY IS FINE, AND EXECUTION TIMING DOES NOT HURT. The rule uses no PDT slot: buy 09:31 TOM+3 and sell 09:31 TOM+4. It has no 15:52 cash conflict, and whole-share sizing is the same as the base case. I priced it at the real execution times, 09:31 and 15:52, from 1-minute bars (2006 to 2026-03): +1.198%/event (t 3.05), against +1.183% (t 2.84) on open/close bars, n=235. The objections below are statistical and cost-related, not mechanical.

THE 'SAVED ROUND TRIP' IS OVERSTATED. Netting the trades, the rule removes the TOM+2 15:52 buy, the TOM+3 09:31 sell and the TOM+3 15:52 buy, and adds a TOM+3 09:31 buy. The real saving is therefore about 2x the cost of a 15:52 trade, not 0.30%. The 15:52 trade is the cheap one: live 15:52 fills land at the quoted ask (mean -0.007%, n=35), and NVDL's 1-minute bar range is 0.16% at 15:52 against 0.80% at 09:31. At a realistic half-spread + 0.05% (about 0.07%/side) each event loses about 0.16%: 2006-26 drops from +1.396% to +1.236% (t 2.83 -> 2.51), and 2016-26 from +1.057% to +0.897% (t 1.83 -> 1.55).

TWO ONE-OFF SHOCKS CARRY THE MEAN. The rule happened to be flat on 2008-07-03 (NVDA profit warning, -28% overnight, 2x swap +74.5%) and on 2024-08-05 (yen-carry Monday gap, -14% then +9% intraday, +50.3%). Excluding just those two days at 0.07%/side: 2006-26 +0.744% (t 2.15), 2006-15 +0.992% (t 1.82), 2016-26 +0.515% (t 1.18) on daily bars. Real NVDL (2022-12+) falls from +1.91% to +0.70% (t 1.20) without 2024-08-05, and real NVDX to +0.49% (t 0.71).

THE LAST 2 YEARS ARE NEGATIVE IN EVERY VERSION. NVDA synthetic 2x on daily bars: -0.42% / -0.58% / -0.66% per event at 0.15 / 0.07 / 0.03%/side. Real NVDL: -0.36% / -0.52%. Real NVDX: -0.33% / -0.49%. Executable 09:31/15:52 prices (2024-10..2026-03, n=17): -0.50% to -0.66%, median about -1.2%, 41% positive.

PAUSE RISK DEPENDS ON THE COST ASSUMPTION AND GETS WORSE RECENTLY. In my rolling 60-session simulation at 92% exposure, the last 2y P(PAUSE) goes from 24.5% to 34.7% at 0.07%/side, 34.2% to 36.3% at 0.15%, and 24.5% to 24.5% at 0.03%. Log growth per session in the last 2y is -0.019% to -0.029%. The long-sample gains (+0.04 to +0.06%/session, PAUSE -1 to -3 points) come mostly from the history the outliers dominate. The swapped intraday segment is also riskier than the night it replaces: 2x intraday falls below -8% on 4.8% of TOM+3 days, against 2.4% for the 2x overnight.

THE CELL IS ISOLATED AND CANNOT BE CHECKED FORWARD. Same swap at 0.15%/side, by trading day of the month (k=1..6): -0.36, +0.31, +1.40, +0.03, -0.60, -0.14%. The neighbours of k=3 are null, which fits a data-mined spike among about 40 calendar cells. At 12 events/yr and sd 3.5-6%, confirming +0.8%/event would take more than 10 years of live data.

THE DOLLAR VALUE IS SMALL AND CAN BE NEGATIVE. At about $95 of exposure, 12 events/yr and 0.07%/side, the gain is about +$8/yr on the long-sample mean without the two outliers, and about -$6.6/yr at the last-2-year mean. Neither is near the claimed $15.35/yr, which assumes 0.15%/side and includes the outliers.

Per-trade results: 2006-2016Q1 +0.950% (n=123), 2016Q2-2026 +0.855% (t 1.97), last 2 years +0.137%, 2006-2026 +0.902% (t 2.68), all matching the candidate. However, 0.30% of every one of those figures is the round trip that is not paid. Any hold-through day gets that saving, so holding through EVERY day from 2006-2026 shows +0.326%/trade (t 4.64). The t of 2.62 is mostly a cost accounting effect, not evidence about TOM+3.

The TOM+3-specific part is the excess over other days: +0.605% (t 1.76) for 2006-2026. It looks like the best result of a search. Of the 23 trading-day-of-month slots, TOM+3 ranks 1st over 2006-2026, but only 4th in each half and 12th of 23 over the last 2 years. Under a within-month permutation null (400 reps), the median of the best slot's t is 1.93, above the observed 1.76, and the 95th percentile is 2.90. Family-wise p(best slot t >= 1.76) = 0.64 for 2006-2026 and 0.645 for 2001-2026. That is before counting the rest of the calendar family (FOMC, pre-holiday, opex, FOMC-cycle weeks, x3 forms each).

No day-of-month structure exists to exploit. Across 21 slots, the spread of the 2006-2026 mean returns (sd 0.313%) is no larger than sampling noise alone (average se 0.326%), so the estimated true spread is 0. Shrinking toward the common mean moves TOM+3 from +0.602% to +0.019%, which equals the grand mean. Slot excesses in the first half correlate -0.17 with those in the second half. The first half's best slot (+12) ranks 10th in the second half (t 0.22).

A selection rule fixed in advance would not have found it. In a yearly walk-forward I chose the slot with the best trailing excess t from 2001 onward, then held it through the next year. That rule picked +12 in almost every year, with training t 2.0-2.76, never TOM+3. Its out-of-sample 2x intraday mean was +0.326% (t 1.04, n=249). A slot with a trailing t of about 2.5 is ordinary noise here, and TOM+3 at t 1.76 is weaker than that.

The out-of-sample record does not hold up. Excess by half: t 1.33 (2006-16) and t 1.14 (2016-26). Pre-sample 2001-05, the only data not used in the original selection: +0.71%, t 0.58, rank 7 of 22. Over the last 2 years the synthetic excess is -0.021% (t -0.03) and real NVDL -0.004%. Over the last 1 year it is -0.85% (n=12). Years with positive excess, 2006+: 12 of 21. Real NVDL since 2022-12 shows +1.34% excess (t 2.01), but almost all of that comes from 2023-24 (2024 year excess +5.55%).

The mechanism claim is weak. In the broad market, TOM+3 intraday excess over 2006-2026 is SPY +0.061% (t 1.06), QQQ +0.098% (t 1.31) and IWM +0.013% (t 0.17). In NVDA itself, the standard turn-of-month window (last day of the month through TOM+3) shows no intraday excess for 2x NVDA: +0.121% (t 0.68), and +0.003% for 2006-16. The '+3' day was picked from inside a window that does not work as a whole. The NVDA-specific excess (1x +0.31%) is about 3x QQQ's, so it is idiosyncratic rather than a turn-of-month fund-flow effect.

What is left is the generic 'hold any day' benefit, and its sign depends on cost and on the period. Mean log growth per hold-through day at 93% exposure: 2006-26 any day +0.192% with 0.30% saved, +0.052% with 0.15% saved. Last 2 years any day: +0.058% / -0.082% (2x NVDA intraday drift -0.143%/d). TOM+3 last 2 years: +0.089% / -0.051%. RULES §5 sells at bid minus a 0.15% limit buffer, which caps the slippage rather than measuring it, so the real round-trip saving may be well under 0.30%. The fair expected value is the generic hold-through value of about $2-4/yr at E=$103 in the long sample and about $0 recently, not $10.18/yr. Any 12 random days would earn the same.
