votes.survives_if: It survives only if it is restated as a generic 'hold NVDL through some days to save the round trip' rule. That rule must be judged against random hold-through days, with measured real NVDL exit and entry slippage rather than an assumed 0.15%/side, and it must show positive log growth after its added intraday variance over the last 2-5 years (it does not at 0.15%/side). Any TOM+3-specific claim needs a forward test fixed in advance. Example: at least 24 live or shadow TOM+3 days with excess over the other days of the same months above 0 at t >= 2. That is roughly a 2-year wait, because the historical evidence cannot be told apart from best-of-23-slots noise (family-wise p ~0.64, shrunk excess ~0).

votes.candidate: H-TOM+3: hold NVDL/NVDX through the 3rd trading day of the month (skip the 09:31 exit and the 15:52 re-entry; sell 09:31 on TOM+4)
reasons: The rule is feasible, and the problem is not there. It uses no PDT slot: the TOM+3 hold was bought the day before, so even an emergency intraday exit is not a day trade. It does not conflict with the 15:52 cash need, because the position is already held. Whole shares and $103 are not a constraint, and skipping the 15:52 re-sizing is a minor issue. One clause is needed: if PAUSE trips during TOM+3, sell down to 1 NVDL at 15:52. That sale is also not a day trade.

The headline is driven by an inflated cost assumption. The +0.887%/trade, t 2.62 and $10.18/yr figures credit a 0.30% round-trip saving (0.15% per side). That is the limit-price buffer in RULES §4/§5, not the fill cost. Live T3X fills compared with 1-minute bar OHLC4 show the real cost: NVDL/NVDX entry -0.006% (n 25, se 0.015) and exit -0.020% (n 25, se 0.035), so the round trip is about 0, give or take 0.04%. Across all 53/54 live overnight fills (including METU/AMZU/AAPU) the round trip was +0.013%. A live quote today showed NVDL at 34.95/34.96, a full spread of 0.029%, and NVDX at 19.66/19.67, 0.051%. A realistic saving is about 0.03–0.05%; even half-spread + 0.05% per side gives only about 0.13%. Counting the 0.15%/side buffer as a benefit is not conservative.

Re-derived from fresh Robinhood daily NVDA data (2003–2026) using a synthetic 2x leveraged return. The intraday haircut of 0.06%/day was measured as real NVDL minus synthetic (-0.061%/day, n 949). With the candidate's 0.30% saving I reproduce its result: +0.922% t 2.74 for 2006–26, halves +0.970 (t 1.87) and +0.875 (t 2.02), last 2y +0.157. With a 0.05% saving: +0.672% t 2.00 for 2006–26, but the halves are only t 1.39 and t 1.44, last 2y is -0.093% (t -0.15) and last 1y is -1.051% (t -1.10). With the live-measured 0.013% saving: 2006–26 t 1.89, halves t 1.32 and 1.36. Once costs are realistic, neither out-of-sample half is significant.

The TOM-specific part is weak and has vanished recently. Compared with holding through any other day, TOM+3 earns +0.604% excess (t 1.75) over 2006–26: +0.703% (t 1.33) in the first half, +0.509% (t 1.14) in the second, -0.021% over the last 2y and -0.854% over the last 1y. On real NVDL open-to-close prices, TOM+3 since 2024-10 averaged -0.088% (n 24), and the last 12 averaged -1.014%; 7 of those 12 were negative. Over the full 2022-12 to 2026 NVDL history TOM+3 shows +1.34% (t 2.07), but that is front-loaded in 2023–mid-2024 and includes the +21.8% synthetic day on 2024-08-05. Trimming 5 trades from each tail leaves +0.49% (t 1.77).

The dollar value is small and noisy at $103. Whole-share sizing at today's quotes is 2 NVDL + 1 NVDX = $89.59 (87% of E), not the ~$95.6 implied by the $10.18 claim. With a 0.05% saving that gives +$7.2/yr on the 2006–26 mean, +$6.7/yr on 2016–26, -$1.0/yr on the last-2y mean and -$11.3/yr on the last-1y mean. Against that, the standard deviation is about $16.5/yr: 12 events × 5.3% per-event sd × $89.6. It would take about 20 years of live trading to tell this apart from zero.

The PAUSE impact is not clearly immaterial. I re-simulated it as a first hit within 60 sessions at w = 0.87, using synthetic 2x NVDA overnight returns plus the TOM+3 intraday hold. Under the candidate's own 0.30% cost, 2006–26 goes from 31.8% to 35.1% (+3.3 points, against the claimed 33.9 to 34.1). With realistic costs it goes from 25.2% to 26.7% (0.05% round trip) or from 27.4% to 32.4% (0.13% round trip). The 2016–26 and last-2y changes are about 0. The results are path-noisy, with flips clustered in a few episodes (2006–07, 2012, 2015, 2022–23). The worst TOM+3 intraday is -12.4% (2008-07-03), about -10.8% of equity at 87% exposure. Mean 60-session log growth falls with the hold over the last 2y (+9.56 to +7.98% with a 0.05% saving), while the full sample improves.

Execution-window check: holding means owning the 09:31 to 15:52 window, while the evidence uses open to close. On 164 sessions of 10-minute NVDL data, 15:50 to close averaged -0.045% (t -0.68), and on 25 live-window minute sessions 09:30 to 09:31 averaged -0.151% (t -1.39). The proxy shows no material bias in either direction, so this point neither rescues nor sinks the idea.

votes.survives_if: It would survive only as a no-cost, low-confidence tweak, and only if both of these hold: (a) the 20-year synthetic TOM+3 intraday strength (+0.6% vs other days, t 1.75) is accepted as real despite last-2y about 0 and last-1y negative on both synthetic and real NVDL; and (b) the expected value is restated honestly as about +0.6%/trade (+$6–7/yr at $103) with a saving of 0.03–0.13%, not 0.30%. To pass the evidence bar it would need, at a realistic saving of 0.13% or less, t ≥ 2 in each half on the TOM-specific excess (currently 1.33 / 1.14), a non-negative last-2y mean on real NVDL 09:31→15:52 prices, and a PAUSE increase that stays at or below 1 point across cost assumptions. None of these hold now. The rule is operationally feasible: no PDT use, no 15:52 cash conflict, whole shares fine, with a PAUSE-on-TOM+3 sell-down clause.

candidate.name: Turn-of-month TQQQ day trades on TOM+2 and TOM+3
candidate.exact_rule: On the 2nd and 3rd trading days of the month, after the 09:31 NVDL exit, buy 1 TQQQ at 09:31 and sell at 15:49. Uses 2 PDT slots within a 5-day window.
candidate.mechanism: Turn-of-month inflows during the cash session. About +0.07%/day excess on the index, which is too small to clear a 3x round-trip cost unless costs are near the 1-cent spread. It is $3.52/yr at 0.06%/side.
candidate.data_used: Daily QQQ/SPY 2006-2026, synthetic 3x
candidate.family: CALENDAR & EVENT EFFECTS: pre-FOMC drift, turn of the month, pre-holiday sessions, options expiration, FOMC-cycle even weeks. Each is tested in three forms: an intraday day trade (uses PDT slots), holding NVDL through the day instead of the 09:31 exit (or moving the entry to 09:31), and swapping the overnight instrument on specific nights.

votes.candidate: Turn-of-month TQQQ day trades on TOM+2 and TOM+3 (buy 1 TQQQ at 09:31 and sell at 15:49 on the 2nd and 3rd trading days)
reasons: The edge is not significant at any honest cost, and its sign depends on the cost assumption. I rebuilt synthetic daily-reset 3x QQQ open->close from fresh daily bars. It tracks real TQQQ with correlation 0.998 over 2010-2026 and comes out about 0.02%/trade richer on TD2/3. For TD2+TD3 over 2006-2026 (n=500), the gross mean is +0.316% (t 2.10). Net is +0.196% (t 1.30) at 0.06%/side and +0.015% (t 0.10) at 0.15%/side. Only the gross figure reaches t of about 2, and that is before costs.

The positive 'out-of-sample' half comes almost entirely from the last 2 years. Without them, 2006-2024.10 (n=452) nets -0.050%/trade at 0.15% and +0.130% (t 0.81) at 0.06%. 2016-2024.10 nets -0.12%/trade at 0.15% (2016-2020: -0.118%; 2021-2024.10: -0.008%). At 0.15% the last 48 trades contribute +30.5 points of a +7.7-point 2006-2026 cumulative sum, so the other 452 trades are net negative.

Results flip sign between periods. In non-overlapping 2-year blocks from 2000 to 2025, TD2+3 is negative in 5 of 13 blocks at 0.06%/side and 7 of 13 at 0.15%/side. Only 2024-25 is significant (t 3.44); the next best is 2010-11 (t 1.83). The last 1 year has already faded to +0.438% (t 0.68) at 0.06%.

The choice of TD2+3 is selection bias. Among 15 consecutive day-of-month pairs, TD2+3 ranked only 3rd in-sample (2006-2015), and the IS winner TD8+9 was negative OOS (-0.19%, t -0.87). TD2+3 ranks 1st in 2016-2026 only because of the last 2 years; over 2016-2024.10 it ranks 4th, behind TD3+4 and TD4+5. TD2 alone averaged +0.039%/day gross on QQQ in 2016-2024.10 (t 0.3).

A walk-forward rerun of the selection kills it. Each year 2009-2026, I picked the best pair on a trailing 10-year window and traded it the next year (n=428 trades). Restricted to the 5 turn-of-month pairs, it nets -0.001%/trade (t -0.01) at 0.06%/side and -0.181% (t -1.21) at 0.15%/side. Across all 15 pairs it nets -0.077% and -0.257%. So the edge exists only when the day pair is chosen with hindsight.

The underlying excess is weak and does not hold in the pre-sample period. QQQ intraday excess on TD2/3 vs other days is +0.086% (t 1.18) in 2006-15, +0.097% (t 1.31) in 2016-26 and +0.069% (t 0.51) in 2021-2024.10. SPY is -0.005% (t -0.05) in the 1999-2005 holdout. IWM is -0.012% in 2016-20 and -0.040% in 2021-2024.10. The literature's turn-of-month effect is measured close-to-close around days -1..+3, so this intraday cut of it is itself one of many variants tested (5 event types x 3 forms x day choices in this family). Familywise, a t of 1.3 to 2.1 is roughly what chance alone would produce.

The last 2 years depend on a few news days. The top synthetic trades are 2025-04-02 +6.64%, 2026-08-04 +6.50% and 2026-04-02 +5.97%. Dropping the top 3 cuts the last-2y gross mean from +0.937% to +0.575% (t 1.60).

It fails the stated goal on risk. My path simulation used every 60-session window: overnight leg at 93% in 2x NVDA close->open, plus 1 TQQQ share (~$78.8, about 76% of $103 equity, 3x) on TD2/3. P(PAUSE) rises 29.4->30.8% (0.06% cost) and ->31.9% (0.15% cost) over 2006-2026 with 0.05%/side overnight costs. With 0.15%/side overnight costs it rises 35.9->37.8/37.9%. Over 2006-2024.10 it rises 35.1->37.9/38.0%. The change in 60-session log growth over 2006-2024.10 is +0.0032 to +0.0049 at 0.06% and -0.0022 to -0.0041 at 0.15%. That is more PAUSE risk for zero or negative growth unless costs are at the floor.

Expected dollars are trivial and depend on cost. At 1 share x 24 trades/yr: 2006-2026 gives +$3.70/yr at 0.06% and +$0.29/yr at 0.15%. 2006-2024.10 gives +$2.45 and -$0.95. 2016-2024.10 gives +$2.07 and -$1.33. The worst single trade is -13.65% (2008-11-05, synthetic) and -11.40% (real TQQQ, 2010+). The win rate is about 51-53% at 0.15%.

I could not check whether 09:31/15:49 fills match the daily open->close model. The broker only has real minute bars for the last ~6 weeks (earlier requests returned all-interpolated bars). On the 4 available TD2/3 sessions, 09:31->15:49 differed from open->close by -0.6 to +0.6 points per trade. The day-leg review measured a ~0.16%/leg haircut for 09:32 fills on TZA, so 0.06%/side may be optimistic for the open.

Walk-forward is about 0 to negative, 2006-2024.10 is negative at 0.15%, and P(PAUSE) rises 1.4-2.9pp.

votes.candidate: Turn-of-month TQQQ day trades on TOM+2 and TOM+3 (buy 1 TQQQ at 09:31, sell at 15:49)
reasons: Costs decide this result. At the brief's default 0.15%/side, the trade has no edge. Synthetic 3x QQQ for 2006-2026 makes +0.015%/trade (t 0.10, n 500). Real TQQQ open-to-close for 2010-02 to 2026 makes +0.055% (t 0.35). Gross TOM+2/+3 is +0.32%/trade synthetic and +0.36% real, so breakeven is about 0.16-0.18%/side. At 1 share (74% of E), log growth falls by about 0.6%/yr.

At the TQQQ-specific realistic cost of about 0.06%/side, the edge is still not statistically clear. The spread is 1 cent on $75.92 (0.013%), so half-spread plus 0.05% comes to about 0.057%/side. At that cost the result is +0.196%/trade, t 1.30 (2006-2026 synthetic). By half: 2006-15 +0.147% (t 0.70) and 2016-26 +0.240% (t 1.12). Real TQQQ 2010+ is +0.235% (t 1.49). Without the last 2 years it drops to +0.130% (t 0.81), so a large part of the edge comes from the recent window.

The choice of these two days is cherry-picked. TDM2&3 is the best of 17 turn-of-month buckets (END-3..TDM6, single days and adjacent pairs). A permutation test under an iid null puts the chance of a best bucket this good at 0.40 (QQQ) and 0.29 (SPY) for 2006-2026, and 0.79-0.81 for 2006-2015. The classic turn-of-month window (END-1..TDM3) is about 0 intraday in 2006-15 (QQQ -0.001%, t -0.02). The wider family (pre-FOMC, pre-holiday, opex, FOMC weeks, three forms each) adds even more multiple testing.
The year-by-year record is unstable. Summed TOM+2/+3 returns are negative in 8 of 21 calendar years, including 2014-2018, 2021 and 2022.

The dollar payoff is small next to the tail risk. The expected gain is +$0.12/yr at 0.15%/side and +$3.41/yr at 0.06%/side (1 share at $76, 24 trades). The worst single trade is -13.9% (about -$10.6, roughly 10% of E), which is half of the 20% PAUSE buffer in one session.

The joint simulation shows more risk for little or no gain. Setup: synthetic 2x-NVDA overnight leg at 93%, 0.15%/side, 60-session windows from every start date. For 2006-2026, P(PAUSE60) rises from 35.9% to 37.1% at 0.15% (36.8% at 0.06%) and P(KILL60) from 4.98% to 5.58% (5.44%). For 2006-2015, P(KILL60) rises from 4.21% to 5.37%, about +28% relative. Risk only improves in windows starting from 2021, and those are the same recent windows the edge depends on.

Execution cannot be verified over a long sample. Robinhood minute and 30-minute history is interpolated before about September 2026, so the 09:31/09:32 entry and 15:49 exit can only be checked on 30 recent sessions (4 of them turn-of-month days). In that sample the 09:32 OHLC4-to-15:49 result differed from open-to-close by +0.14% in the trade's favour (t 1.74, noise). There is no long-run check of whether the turn-of-month excess is front-loaded into the first minute, which a 09:32 entry would miss.

Feasibility is fine but costs a buffer. 1 share at about $76 fits E=$103, cash from the 15:49 sale is usable at 15:52 in a limited-margin account, and TQQQ liquidity is deep. However, the two trades fall on consecutive days and use 2 of the 3 PDT slots. That leaves only 1 emergency same-day exit for the overnight leg (which RULES §7 reserves the budget for) over about 8 business days each month. It also brings back the 09:31 -> day leg -> 15:49 -> 15:52 order chain that the day-leg review removed. The candidate also labels TQQQ '3x SPY'; it is 3x NDX, though its numbers match the QQQ-based synthetic.

candidate.name: Quad-witching inverse day trade, SPXU
candidate.exact_rule: On quarterly opex Fridays (3rd Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec; next 2026-12-18), after the 09:31 NVDL exit fills, buy 3 SPXU (about 97% of E) at 09:31 and sell at 15:49, flat before 15:52. Never hold inverse overnight.
candidate.in_sample: 2006-2016: +0.743% (t 2.13, n 41). Underlying SPY quad-witching intraday 2006-13 -0.343% (t -2.57) after an overnight of +0.494%.
candidate.out_of_sample: 2016-2026: +0.776% (t 1.46, n 42). SPY 2014-21 intraday -0.542% (t -2.72). Decay: 2022-2026 SPY quad-witching intraday +0.007% (n 19); trade -0.311% (t -0.61); last 2y -0.756% (n 8). At 0.06%/side the full sample is +0.940% (t 2.96). Positive in 15 of 21 years. No change to PAUSE risk in simulation.
candidate.mechanism: Expiration-day opening pressure (SPX AM settlement on the special opening quotation, hedge unwinds) inflates the open, then it reverts during the session. The effect seems to have disappeared in the 0DTE era (2022+), so the long-sample mean is likely overstated going forward.
candidate.data_used: Daily SPY/QQQ 2006-2026; dividend-corrected overnight (SPY ex-dates fall on quad-witching Fridays)
candidate.family: CALENDAR & EVENT EFFECTS: pre-FOMC drift, turn of the month, pre-holiday sessions, options expiration, FOMC-cycle even weeks. Each is tested in three forms: an intraday day trade (uses PDT slots), holding NVDL through the day instead of the 09:31 exit (or moving the entry to 09:31), and swapping the overnight instrument on specific nights.

votes.candidate: Quad-witching inverse day trade, SPXU (buy ~97% of E in SPXU at 09:31 on quarterly opex Fridays, sell at 15:49)
reasons: The historical SPY anomaly is real, so the issue is not that the candidate's numbers are wrong. Using fresh daily SPY bars 2006-2026, quad-witching open->close averages -0.340% (t -3.33, n 83). Among 60 calendar classes (month-mod-3 x nth weekday x weekday), it is the most extreme, at t -3.59; it is the only class with |t|>=3. A permutation test against random Fridays gives p~0.0001. The candidate's trade numbers also replicate: synthetic -3x net of 0.30% round trip is +0.742% (t 2.37), 2006-15 +0.758% (t 2.16), 2016-26 +0.728% (t 1.42). The trade still fails out of sample, for the reasons below.

The out-of-sample half rests on one year. 2016+ without 2020 is +0.099% (t 0.30), with a median of -0.13%. The single day 2020-03-20 (+17.27%) is 28% of all P&L, and calendar 2020 is 45%. Removing 2008-09 and 2020 leaves +0.242% (t 1.16) with a median of +0.006%. Over the full sample, the median trade is +0.33% and the hit rate is 57%. Dropping the top 5 trades leaves +0.23%. The edge is mostly a crash-day payoff, not a reliable quarterly effect.

The effect is gone in the current era. Since 2022 (n=19), SPY quad-witching open->close is +0.007%. The trade is -0.312% net (t -0.61), with a bootstrap 90% CI of -1.15% to +0.47%. The last 2 years (n=8) are -0.751%. The pre-2022 vs 2022+ difference is t 2.13, so the decay is itself statistically visible. It also fits the candidate's own explanation: daily 0DTE expiries make quad witching less special. Nothing indicates the effect is coming back.

The placebo does not support the stated mechanism. Monthly non-quad opex days also settle SPX in the morning, yet they show nothing in the recent decade: SPY open->close 2016+ is +0.003% (n 87), and the -3x trade net is -0.306%. Fridays one week before or after quad witching are about 0 (t 0.37 to 0.64).

The start date flatters the result. 2000-2005 quad witching (n 24) is only +0.247% net (t 0.39). The SQQQ variant is weaker everywhere: full sample +0.691% (t 1.79), real SQQQ +0.673% (t 1.56), and 2022+ -0.648%.

Current conditions are the weak bucket. SPY 20-day realized vol on 2026-10-13 is 9.3%. Quad-witching trades with trailing vol below 13% net +0.129% (t 0.55, median -0.14%); below 11% they net +0.305% (t 1.44). The significant part of the result comes from high-vol quad-witching days (vol >= 15%: +1.58%).

The stated mechanism is an inflated open that reverts, and daily open->close bars include the reversal that a 09:31-09:32 entry cannot capture. On 1-minute and 5-minute bars for the 2026 quad-witching days, SPXU rose +0.67% (03-20) and +0.70% (06-18) from the open to 09:35. On 06-18 that turned a +0.46% open->close into -0.40% from 09:35 to 15:50. Long intraday history is not available from this data source (intraday bars before roughly 2026 come back interpolated), so the executable edge cannot be verified. It is likely below the daily-bar figure.

Multiple testing. This is one of at least 15 to 30 tests in the calendar/event family (5 effects x 3 forms x instruments and variants). The trade-level t of 2.37 (two-sided p~0.02) does not survive a Bonferroni correction, which needs roughly t >= 2.9-3.1. Only the SPY-level statistic survives, and that one has decayed.

The payoff is small and the tail is real. Even at the claimed +0.76%, the trade earns about $3 a year on E=$103 from 4 trades. The best estimate of the forward mean is about 0 or below once you combine the 2022+ results, cost and entry slippage. The worst trades at 97% of E are -5.0% (2024-12-20), -4.94% and -4.64% (2022-03-18). These are expected-negative losses that add a little drawdown risk for no expected gain.
recomputed_numbers: 2020-03-20 trade +17.27%; 2020 sum +27.44 pts of 61.6 total; years positive 15/21
Decay test: SPY QW o->c pre-2022 -0.443% (n 64) vs 2022+ +0.007% (n 19), diff t 2.13; 2022+ bootstrap 90% CI of net mean -1.145% .. +0.470%
Calendar-class scan (60 classes): QW class t -3.59 is #1, only class |t|>=3; 9 classes |t|>=2; permutation p vs random Fridays 0.0001
votes.survives_if: Only if a pre-registered forward shadow log shows the effect has returned in the 0DTE era. That means at least 12 more quad-witching Fridays (about 3 years) scored at real 09:32 entry and 15:49 exit prices, with mean net >= +0.5% and t >= 2. Over the same period, SPY quad-witching open->close since 2022 would need to turn significantly negative again (t <= -2 over at least 20 observations), and it would have to hold in low-vol regimes (20-day rv < 13%), not only on crash days. Until then: no live trade, shadow log only. A shadow log uses no PDT slot and puts no capital at risk.

votes.candidate: Quad-witching inverse day trade, SPXU (buy about 3 SPXU at 09:31 after the NVDL exit on the 3rd Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, sell 15:49)
reasons: The headline numbers reproduce from fresh Robinhood daily bars (SPY 2004-2026, real SPXU/SQQQ 2009-06+). But the edge is negative in the period the trade would actually run. 2022-2026: -0.311%/trade at 0.15%/side and -0.132% at 0.06%/side (n 19). Last 2 years: -0.749% (n 8). Calendar years 2022, 2024 and 2025 were each -4% to -6% cumulative. Real SPXU open->close in 2022+ is -0.026% gross. The proposer agrees the effect seems gone in the 0DTE era.

The long-sample mean is driven by crises, not by a steady per-event edge. The 3 largest days make up 52% of all cumulative net P&L: 2020-03-20 +17.6%, 2008-09-19 +7.6%, 2009-03-20 +7.6%. Dropping only 2020-03-20 cuts the mean from +0.74% to +0.54%. Dropping the top 5 gives +0.22% (t 1.15). Excluding 2008 and 2020 gives +0.35% (t 1.59, median +0.025%). The trimmed and winsorized means stay positive (+0.47% / +0.55%) only because of pre-2022 data.

Execution: the backtest is SPY open->close, but the rule can only buy after the 09:31:05 NVDL exit fills. That is about 09:31-09:34, or later if the exit falls back to re-price or market. It sells at 15:49. Robinhood intraday history only covers 2026: 1-minute data is available from about mid-September 2026, and 30-minute data on a few earlier 2026 dates. So exactly one quad-witching day (2026-09-18) can be checked at the executable window, and the bias on witching days cannot be measured.

The proposer's own mechanism (an inflated opening print that then reverts) puts the move right at the open, the part a post-09:31 entry gives up. On witching days SPY's open is within 0.05% of the day's high 18% of the time, against 6-7% on ordinary days and other Fridays. Those 15 open-near-high days average +1.45%/trade and supply 35% of total P&L. On the 2026 witching days with 30-minute data, the first 30 minutes held 42% of the day's drop (03-20) and more than all of it (06-18: -0.40% by 10:00 vs -0.14% for the day).

The generic haircut on 22 recent SPXU sessions (1-minute bars) is -0.12%/trade with 0.36% sd of model error: 09:32 OHLC4 -> 15:49 close gives -0.105%, against +0.011% open->close. The 15:49 exit gives up the 15:49->close move, +0.106% (t 1.7) on those sessions. On witching days that window contains the index-rebalance closing auction, whose sign is unknown.

Costs alone do not kill it. The SPXU spread is $0.01 at $33.77 (0.03%), so 0.15%/side is conservative. Real SPXU tracks the synthetic -3x model to within -0.035%/trade. Even at 0.06%/side, though, 2022+ is negative.

Whole-share sizing does not match the stated rule. At E = $103 the account's own 0.98*E cap ($100.94) is below 3 x 33.77 x 1.0015 = $101.46, so the order is 2 shares (66% of E), not '3 SPXU about 97%'. 3 shares needs E of about $103.5 or more at today's SPXU price. Exposure therefore jumps between about 66% and 96%. Sizing must use floor(cash/limit) so a 3-share order cannot draw on limited-margin buying power.

The dollar stakes are trivial and the forward sign is negative. At 3 shares: +$3.0/yr on the full-sample mean, +$1.4/yr ex-crisis, -$1.3/yr on 2022+ (-$0.5 at 0.06%/side), -$3.0/yr on the last 2 years. It also uses one of the 3 PDT slots RULES_v3 section 7 reserves for emergency exits for a week each quarter, and adds a step between the 09:31 exit and the 15:52 entry (a stuck 15:49 sell would under-size the weekend NVDL entry).

Feasibility points that hold for the candidate: no conflict with the 15:52 entry (sale proceeds are usable at once). PAUSE risk barely changes: one day with sd of about 2.5% every ~63 sessions adds under 1% to the 60-session P&L sd of about 20%. Witching days are also distinct from placebo days over the long sample: SPY open->close -0.34% (t -3.3) vs +0.044% on other Fridays and -0.06% on monthly opex Fridays. These points do not rescue the forward expected value.
recomputed_numbers: Outlier dependence (net 0.15%/side): drop top 1 +0.539%; drop top 3 +0.370% (t 1.71); drop top 5 +0.224% (t 1.15); ex-2020 +0.431% (t 1.80); ex-2008/2020 +0.350% (t 1.59, median +0.025%); top 3 days = 31.8 of 61.4 cumulative net percentage points.
Robust central tendency (pre-2022 driven): 10% trimmed +0.473% (t 3.44); winsorized 5/95 +0.553%.
Real SPXU open->close on witching days: 2009-06+ +0.886% gross (n 69) vs synthetic +0.921% on the same days. Real minus synthetic -0.035%/trade. 2022+ real -0.026% gross.
SQQQ variant, real open->close gross: 2022+ -0.301%; last 2y -0.909%.
Placebos 2006+ (net trade / SPY open->close): monthly non-quarterly opex -0.115% / -0.062%; other Fridays -0.429% / +0.044%; all days -0.355% / +0.017%.
SPY open within 0.05% of day high: witching days 18%, other Fridays 6%, all days 7%. Witching open-near-high days: n 15, mean +1.451%/trade, sum 21.8 of 61.4.
2026-09-18 (only witching day with 1-minute data): SPXU open->close -0.042%; 09:32 OHLC4->15:49 close -0.006%; open->09:32 -0.121%; 15:49->close +0.085%.
Dollars per year at 3 shares: full-sample +$3.00; ex-2008/2020 +$1.42; 2022+ -$1.26 (-$0.53 at 0.06%/side); last 2y -$3.04.
votes.survives_if: It survives only if two things hold. (a) The pre-2022 mean (+0.35% ex-crisis to +0.74% full sample) carries into the 0DTE era, even though 2022-2026 shows -0.31% (n 19) and the last 2 years -0.75%. (b) The executable window (about 09:32 to 15:49) on witching days captures most of the open->close move. No long intraday history exists to check (b), and the mechanism itself puts the reversion at the open. Even then it is worth about $3/yr at most. A defensible path would be a no-cost shadow log: the 09:32 SPXU OHLC4 x 1.0015 entry and the 15:49 exit, scored at each witching day from 2026-12-18. It should go live only if at least 8 shadow legs show a positive mean, together with a positive 2022+ open->close mean, with sizing by floor(0.98*cash/limit).

candidate.name: Hold NVDL through Tuesday of opex week
candidate.exact_rule: On the Tuesday of the week containing the 3rd Friday, skip the 09:31 exit and the 15:52 re-entry; sell 09:31 Wednesday
candidate.in_sample: 2006-2016: +0.962% (t 2.19, n 123); excess vs other days +0.719% (t 1.59). Excluding FOMC-1/FOMC/FOMC+1 days the 2006-16 excess falls to +0.189% (t 0.40).
candidate.mechanism: Weak and partly confounded. In the first half it is mostly FOMC overlap (FOMC Tuesdays often fall in opex week); otherwise opex-week dealer-hedging flows or a CPI-date overlap. A single weekday found among 5 opex-week days and about 30 tags looks data-mined. The TQQQ day-trade version on the same day is dead (+0.139%, t 0.68; 2016-26 -0.049%).
candidate.data_used: Daily NVDA/SPY/QQQ 2006-2026; real NVDL 2022-12+
candidate.family: CALENDAR & EVENT EFFECTS: pre-FOMC drift, turn of the month, pre-holiday sessions, options expiration, FOMC-cycle even weeks. Each is tested in three forms: an intraday day trade (uses PDT slots), holding NVDL through the day instead of the 09:31 exit (or moving the entry to 09:31), and swapping the overnight instrument on specific nights.

votes.candidate: Hold NVDL through Tuesday of opex week (skip Tue 09:31 exit and 15:52 re-entry; sell Wed 09:31)
reasons: Multiple testing. I built a 57-cell calendar family: 25 cells for week relative to opex (-2..+2) by weekday, trading-day-of-month 1-22, month-end -1..-5, and the 5 plain weekdays. Opex Tuesday is the best cell, but its family-wise significance is weak. I shuffled the 2x-NVDA intraday returns within each calendar year, 2000 times. Its full-sample excess t of 2.57 is beaten by the best null cell 24% of the time (null median best t 2.23, 95th percentile 3.11). Its worse-half t of 1.58 is beaten 17% of the time. Even inside the 25-cell opex grid alone, p is 0.12 and 0.08. The real scan was larger (about 30 tags x 3 forms x several instruments), so the true correction is harsher.

Calendar cells do not persist from one half to the other. Across the 25 opex-grid cells, the correlation between the 2006-16 and 2016-26 t-stats is -0.04. Example: the Monday of the week before opex flips from t -2.67 to +2.32. The candidate's 'out-of-sample' is not a holdout: the cell was picked with both halves visible.

The effect comes from a different source in each half, which suggests the label is matching noise rather than a stable mechanism. 2006-16: it was market-wide and tied to FOMC. The 23 opex Tuesdays in an FOMC window averaged +3.05%; excluding them, the excess is +0.24% (t 0.52). SPY excess was +16.6bp (t 1.82), and NVDA's own component (NVDA minus 1.5x QQQ) was +4.5bp (t 0.27). 2016-26: it is NVDA-specific and not FOMC. FOMC-window days averaged only +0.26%; excluding FOMC, the excess is +1.09% (t 2.22). SPY was -0.6bp (t -0.10), QQQ +5.9bp (t 0.66), and NVDA's own component +35bp (t 2.49).

There is no broad mechanism in the recent decade. Across 10 other large caps and ETFs, the 1x opex-Tuesday excess was positive for 10 of 10 in 2006-16 (mean t 1.57; these names move together, so this is roughly one market-wide observation). In 2016-26 the mean t fell to 0.33 (AMD +24bp, SMH +13bp, MU 0bp, IWM +1bp). In the last 2 years only 2 of 10 were positive (mean t -0.34). Opex-week dealer flows should show up in the indices. The neighbouring days also show nothing: Monday of opex week has excess -0.26% (t -0.77) and Wednesday -0.03%.

The 2016-26 result rests on a few days. Of the +125.3% summed over 127 opex Tuesdays, the top 8 days gave +94.4%: 2022-02-15 +18.4%, 2020-03-17 +15.9%, 2022-03-15 +13.4% (the day before an FOMC decision), 2023-02-14 +13.0%, and 4 days of +7.8% to +9.5%. Without them the mean is +0.26%, against +0.11% on other days. Dropping 13 Tuesdays that fell 0-2 days before an NVDA earnings report (one of them was 2022-02-15) cuts the excess to +0.70% (t 1.60). Pre-earnings days in general show no effect (-0.23%).

Recent evidence is flat or negative. Last 2 years on synthetic 2x NVDA: -0.258% gross, excess -0.21% (t -0.25), n 25. Real NVDL in the last 2 years: -0.26% open to close (t -0.34). Its extra log growth is -0.02% per instance, against +0.12% for holding through an ordinary day. The real-NVDL figure since 2022-12 (+1.07%, t 1.84) comes from the 2023 to mid-2024 AI-boom run; from 2024 on it is +0.67%.

The candidate's t of 3.55 is against zero after adding the 0.30% of saved round-trip cost. That saving is available on any hold-through day, so it says nothing about opex Tuesday. The opex-specific excess is only t 2.57 before multiplicity, and below 2 in each half once returns are scaled by trailing volatility (t 1.69 and 1.87; last 2 years t 0.01).

The one genuine pre-sample holdout, 1999-09 to 2005, has the right sign but is not significant. NVDA 2x excess +1.14% (t 0.95; it shrinks from +1.76% in 1999-2003 to +0.46% in 2003-05). SPY +0.16% (t 1.32), QQQ +0.22% (t 0.97). That fits a market-wide effect that has since faded, not an NVDA edge to rely on.

Practical conflict: the next instance, Tuesday 2026-11-17, is NVDA's earnings day (report after the close). Under RULES v1.7 §3(d) the overnight leg is in cash that night. Holding through Tuesday and selling Wednesday 09:31 would carry NVDL through earnings, so the rule must be skipped there anyway.

votes.survives_if: It would survive only with evidence that does not rely on in-sample selection: (1) a pre-registered forward or paper record of at least 24 opex Tuesdays, skipping the earnings-conflicted 2026-11-17, that shows a positive excess over ordinary hold-through days; or (2) evidence that the opex-week mechanism has come back market-wide in 2016-26, with SPY/QQQ/SMH excess positive at t >= 2 and spread across the week rather than a single Tuesday spike; and (3) a family-wise corrected p < 0.05 over the calendar tags actually scanned. Until then, plan for an opex-specific excess of about 0. Any value left is the generic saved round-trip cost, which is not specific to opex Tuesday and comes with a -13% single-session tail at about 93% exposure.

votes.candidate: Hold NVDL through Tuesday of opex week (skip the Tue 09:31 exit and the Tue 15:52 re-entry, sell Wed 09:31)
reasons: Costs, PDT, whole shares and 15:52 cash do not kill this candidate. It saves two executions, uses no PDT slot (bought Monday, sold Wednesday) and needs no cash at 15:52. On the 146 sessions of real NVDL 5-minute bars (2026-02-23 to 10-13), the executable window (about 09:35 to 15:50) differs from open-to-close by only -0.011% a day, so the daily-bar proxy is not biased. It is refuted because the evidence does not clearly survive.

The headline after-cost figure (+1.075%, t 3.55) is inflated. It adds a generic saving of 2 x 0.15% to every observation. Adding a constant raises both the mean and the t-stat, and that saving would apply to holding through any day. Live fills show the real per-side cost is far below 0.15%: 15 NVDL/NVDX entries average -0.005% against the 15:52 one-minute bar open. A realistic saving is about 0.06-0.10% per event, not 0.30%. The right test is the opex-specific excess over other days: +0.80% (t 2.57) for 2006-26, +0.68% (t 1.48) for 2006-16, +0.91% (t 2.16) for 2016-26 and -0.21% (t -0.25) for the last 2 years.

The mechanism changes between the two halves, so there is no stable effect for costs to act on. In 2006-16 the effect sits in non-earnings months (+1.16%, t 2.21) and FOMC/quarterly months (+2.03%), while NVDA earnings months show -0.19%. Excluding FOMC-adjacent days cuts it to +0.15% (t 0.32). In 2016-26 it sits in NVDA earnings months (Feb/May/Aug/Nov +1.97%, t 2.72, n 43), where opex Tuesday falls about 1-6 sessions before the report. Other months show +0.54% (t 1.10). SPY on opex Tuesdays in 2016-26 shows +0.022% vs +0.024% on other days, so there is no market-wide opex flow. The second-half 'effect' looks like NVDA's pre-earnings run-up plus outliers (2022-02-15 +18.4% and 2023-02-14 +13.0% at 2x).

It looks data-mined. Shifting the day relative to opex Tuesday gives similar t-values at arbitrary offsets: +4 sessions (the next Monday) has t +3.02 in 2016-26 and t +2.20 in 2006-26, and +3 (opex Friday) has t -2.17. Third-Tuesday-of-month gives a similar result (2006-26 +0.69%, t 2.17; last 2y -1.07%).

The recent record is negative. Over the last 2 years: synthetic 2x -0.26% (t -0.33, n 25, 12 wins out of 25), real NVDL the same. In 2025 the 12 opex Tuesdays averaged -1.02%. In the 2026 sample with intraday data, real NVDL averaged +1.29% over 8 events, which is too few to count.

Growth and risk, from my own calendar-preserving 60-session windows (2x NVDA, f=0.9, earnings nights in cash). Log growth increment per session: 2006-26 +0.045% (0.15%/side) or +0.036% (0.05%/side); 2016-26 +0.051 / +0.042; last 2 years -0.008 / -0.017. Placebo holds through the 1st, 2nd or 4th Tuesday add -0.008 to +0.016, so most of the gain is the in-sample opex mean, not the cost saving. P(PAUSE within 60): 2006-26 30.4->29.5% (0.15%) and 26.0->24.9% (0.05%); last 2 years 24.5->36.1% (0.15%) and 24.5->24.5% (0.05%). P(equity <= 0.485 x start within 60 sessions, a proxy for KILL at $50): 3.95->4.30% and 2.44->2.85% (2006-26); last 2 years 0.68->2.04% at 0.05%. That is a small rise in severe-loss risk with no recent payoff.

Feasibility conflict: the very next instance breaks the rules. Robinhood lists NVDA earnings for 2026-11-17 (pm, verified), which is the Tuesday of November opex week (3rd Friday is 11-20). The rule as written ('sell 09:31 Wednesday') would hold through earnings and violate RULES_v3 §3(d). It needs an exception: sell at about 15:50 Tuesday, which is not a day trade, but then no cost is saved. A second conflict is §5: 'a LATE exit wake (even 10:30+) still exits immediately'. A backstop or restart wake on Tuesday would sell the position unless a state flag overrides §5, which adds operational risk.

Tail risk: the worst opex-Tuesday intraday move at 2x is -13.4% (2009-05-12), about -12% of E at 89-98% exposure. The worst full Monday 15:52 to Wednesday 09:31 hold is -25.4% (2008-01-15), and -17.4% on 2022-09-13 (a CPI day). Either one triggers PAUSE in a single event.

votes.survives_if: Costs are not the obstacle. The candidate would survive only as a pre-registered, shadow-logged rule with all four of the following. (1) An explicit earnings exception: on an NVDA-report Tuesday (next one 2026-11-17), sell about 15:50 Tuesday instead of holding to Wednesday. (2) A state flag that overrides §5's 'late exit wake exits immediately' on that Tuesday. (3) Promotion only if the excess holds up outside its confounds: the 2016-26 non-earnings-month opex-Tuesday excess reaching at least about +0.5% with t >= 2 (now +0.54%, t 1.10), and the trailing 2-year mean turning positive (now -0.26%). (4) Long-run logic stated with realistic costs (about 0.05%/side), so the claimed edge is the opex-specific excess and not the generic two-side saving. Until then, keep the standard 09:31 exit and 15:52 re-entry.

candidate.name: SKIP_DOWN_SESSION (UPONLY): hold overnight only when NVDA is up on the session at 15:50
candidate.exact_rule: At the 15:48 ENTRY wake, read NVDA's regular-session official open for today and NVDA's last price at 15:50. If last_1550 >= open, run the normal §3(c)/§4 15:52 entry (NVDL first, then NVDX filler). If last_1550 < open, place no entry and hold cash overnight. The 09:31 exit is unchanged and the earnings-night blackout is unchanged. No day trade is involved: skipping is simply not buying.
candidate.in_sample: Rule fixed a priori as the mirror of §1, so there is no fitted parameter. Daily close->open 2x NVDA excluding earnings nights: 2001-2013H1 after-UP +0.295%/night vs after-DOWN -0.011% (diff t -2.31). 1-minute executable 15:50 signal, 1552->0931 2x gross: 2005-2015 UP +0.151% vs DOWN -0.038%.
candidate.out_of_sample: Daily 2013H2-2026: UP +0.385% vs DOWN +0.067% (diff t -2.96). 1-minute data, 2016-2021.03: UP +0.545% vs DOWN +0.128%. 2021.04-2026.03: UP +0.630% vs DOWN +0.014%. REAL NVDL 2022-12..2026-03: UP +0.708% (t 4.1, n374) vs DOWN +0.006% (n349). Last 2y daily: diff -0.243% (t -0.8), same direction. candidate.mechanism: NVDA-specific overnight continuation after up sessions: attention-driven overnight and pre-open buying after strong days (Berkman et al. 2012). Volatility clustering also concentrates gap-down risk after down sessions. 2016-2026: 58 of 1275 down-session nights were <= -6% (2x) vs 25 of 1350 up-session nights; 2005-2015: 46 vs 29. Not a market-wide effect: QQQ/SPY 2x show no difference, and only 6 of 11 large caps share the sign. It looks NVDA- and high-attention-specific (TSLA and MU have it too).

votes.candidate: SKIP_DOWN_SESSION (UPONLY): hold NVDL/NVDX overnight only when NVDA's 15:50 price is at or above its open
reasons: The rule was not fixed a priori. RULES §1 predicted the opposite: after a down session the next night is about 2x better. The candidate flips that sign after looking at the data, and it was picked from a large grid (4 entry times x 4 exit times plus conditional entries and exits).

The claimed in-sample period does not hold up on the tradable signal. I rebuilt the 15:50 signal and the 15:52->09:31 2x return from the 1-minute data. For 2005-2015, UP nights averaged +0.109% and DOWN nights +0.003% (diff +0.106%, t 0.89). That is not significant. The daily 2005-2015 result is also weak (diff +0.128%, t 1.18).
The daily first half (2001-2013H1, t 2.43) depends on one year. Without 2008 the diff falls to +0.156% (t 1.19). In 2008 alone the diff was +2.17% (t 3.0).

There was a 7-year reversal that someone following the rule in real time would have lived through. By the start of 2009 the daily expanding-window t was already 3.06. Over 2009-2015 the diff then turned negative: daily -0.137% (t -1.22), 1-minute -0.111% (t -0.89), and 2013 alone -0.50% (t -3.19). Over those years UPONLY did worse than simply holding a half-size position every night: -26.5%/yr log growth vs -18.2%/yr at 0.07%/side. So the signal itself had negative value then.

The strong evidence comes from one decade. On 1-minute data, 2016-2026.03 gives diff +0.523% (t 3.85). The headline +0.382%/trade (t 4.29) uses only that decade. Over the whole 2005-2026.03 tradable sample, the UPONLY per-trade after-cost mean is +0.153% (t 2.52) at 0.07%/side and -0.007% (t -0.11) at the 0.15%/side cost the task specifies.

Recent data runs against the rule. Over the last 12 months of daily data, UP nights averaged +0.215% and DOWN nights +0.533% (diff -0.318%, t -0.94); 2026 to date is -0.340%. On real NVDL close->open after the 1-minute data ends (2026-04..10), the diff is -0.318% (t -0.71). On RH 5-minute bars for the same period, the sign depends on the exit minute: -0.186% with a 09:30 exit, +0.426% with a 09:35 exit. That is noise, not confirmation. Among 21 large caps over the last 12 months, NVDA ranks 20th of 21 on this measure.

The effect is not a market-wide or lasting stock trait. QQQ and SPY show about zero. Across 20 peers the average t is -0.67 in 2005-15 and -0.14 in 2016-26. The stocks that carried the effect in 2005-15 (AAPL t 2.83, META 2.12, NFLX 2.02) lost it in 2016-26 (-0.07, 0.05, -1.12). NVDA has since become a mega-cap. This fits an attention-era effect that fades.

Shrinking the estimate for out-of-sample use removes the growth claim. Across 18 stocks, a stock's average diff over the prior 3 years predicts the next year's diff with a slope of only 0.42 (0.46 using 2016+). For NVDA the predicted next-year diff is about 0.12-0.21%, against an in-sample 0.4-0.6%. I re-ran a block bootstrap on 2016-2026.03 with the diff shrunk to 0.14%. At 0.07%/side, UPONLY's expected log growth is +19.7%/yr vs +22.0% for the current rule (median equity after 250 sessions 126 vs 131). So it no longer adds expected growth.

The PAUSE/KILL improvement mostly comes from holding a position about half as often, not from the signal. Even with zero signal, UPONLY's P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) is 14.3% vs 38.9% for the current rule. Holding a half-size position every night gives about 4%. Most calendar-year wins also come from lower exposure in years when the overnight leg lost money. In the 9 years when the current rule made money, UPONLY beat it in only 4 at 0.07%/side.

Peer cross-section (2x close->open, 0.5% winsorized), NVDA vs 20 others: NVDA t 0.41 in 2005-15 (peer mean t -0.67, 7 of 20 positive); t 2.78 in 2016-26 (ranked 2nd after TSLA 4.06; peer mean -0.14); last 1y t -0.91 (ranked 20 of 21).

Strategy, 1-minute 2005-2026.03, 0.88 exposure, 0.05%/night drag. At 0.07%/side, annual log growth: A (current) -10.6, B (UPONLY) +12.3, C (half-size every night) -2.5. 2009-2015: A -39.7, B -26.5, C -18.2. 2016-2026.03: A +21.0, B +40.0, C +13.4. B per-trade: 2005-2015 -0.081% (t -1.02), 2016-2026.03 +0.402% (t 4.36), full sample +0.153% (t 2.52). At 0.15%/side: full sample -0.007% (t -0.11), 2016+ +0.242% (t 2.63). Block bootstrap (20-session blocks, E=103, 0.07%/side), 2016-2026.03 as measured: P(PAUSE within 60) A 37.2% / B 12.5% / C 4.0%; P(KILL within 250) 6.0 / 0.7 / 0.1; median E250 129 / 155 / 119. With the diff shrunk to 0.14: P(PAUSE) A 36.1 / B 14.2; KILL 6.3 / 1.8; median E250 131 / 126; expected log growth A +22.0% vs B +19.7%. With no signal at all: B P(PAUSE) 14.3%, median E250 118, expected log growth +13.4%.
votes.survives_if: It survives only as a risk-reduction filter, not as a growth add. With the effect shrunk to about 0.14% (2x), it gives roughly the same or slightly less expected growth than the current rule at 0.07%/side, with P(PAUSE within 60) of about 14% instead of 36%. Adopt it only if the owner explicitly wants that trade-off, and compare it with simply cutting position size. It would add growth on its own merits only if (a) realistic costs are about 0.15%/side or more, where down-session nights lose money after costs regardless of the signal, or (b) a pre-registered forward test confirms the signal. For that test, log the 15:50-vs-open sign every night for at least 120 nights from 2026-10-15 with no parameter changes, and require the UP-minus-DOWN NVDL 09:31 result to be positive with t of at least 1.5. The current live regime (last 12 months, 2026-04..10) shows the opposite sign.

votes.candidate: SKIP_DOWN_SESSION (UPONLY): hold the 15:52->09:31 NVDL/NVDX position only when NVDA's 15:50 price is at or above its session open
reasons: Feasibility holds. The rule uses no PDT slot. On a skip night the cash just stays idle, so it never conflicts with the 15:52 entry. Whole-share sizing and the $103 equity are unchanged. The signal can be computed with read-only tools: get_equity_quotes has no session open, but a 5-minute historicals call returns it (today, 2026-10-14, the first bar opened at 225.65). The signal is also robust to which open is used. The official open and the first trade disagree on only 0.92% of days. A ±0.25% deadband, or a quote-only version that compares against the prior close, gives the same direction and size of result in both halves.

Costs work in the candidate's favour, not against it. Skipping about 49% of nights avoids about 49% of round trips, so UPONLY's advantage over the current rule grows as costs rise. Over 2016-2026Q1 the log-growth gain per night is +0.034% (t 0.78) at 0.03%/side, +0.079% (t 1.80) at 0.07%, and +0.148% (t 3.36) at 0.15%. Over 2005-2015 it is +0.080% (t 1.84), +0.125% (t 2.89) and +0.196% (t 4.49) at the same three costs.

Caveat: the growth gain comes from costs and variance, not from the claimed continuation mechanism. With zero costs the 2016-2026 log-growth gain is -0.003% per night (t -0.06). UPONLY's arithmetic expected dollars are lower at zero cost ($67.5 vs $74.3 a year), and it wins only 10 of 22 calendar years. The UP-vs-DOWN gap itself is real (2016-26 gross UP +0.576% vs DOWN +0.062%, t 3.78). But DOWN nights are about zero-mean, not negative, so skipping them only pays because it avoids the costs and the left tail. The headline t of 4.29 is the wrong test. The t-stat of the improvement over the current rule is 1.28 (arithmetic) or 1.80 (log) at 0.07%/side for 2016-26, and about 0 for the last 2 years.

Live fill calibration. On 19 live NVDL nights between 09-09 and 10-12, compared with RH 1-minute last-trade prices: entry cost averaged -0.004% and exit cost +0.038% per side, with an exit SD of about 0.3%. Real NVDL tracked synthetic 2x at -0.026% per night (RH 5-minute data, 2026). The true all-in cost is therefore about 0.03-0.07% per side. At the bottom of that range the growth gain is positive over the long sample but not significant, and it is negative in recent windows. At 0.03%/side: last 2 years -0.010% per night, last year -0.064% per night.

The risk reduction is robust at every cost level. 20,000-path block bootstrap (block length 10), 2016-2026Q1, starting equity $103, exposure 0.88. P(PAUSE within 60 sessions): UPONLY 10.9-12.2% vs 33.8-43.9% for the current rule. P(KILL within 250 sessions): 0.4-1.7% vs 3.5-19.2%. UPONLY also beats a feasible half-size always-hold (1 NVDL + 1 NVDX, about 0.52 exposure) on growth: median equity at 250 sessions 171 vs 136 at 0.03%/side. That half-size version has a somewhat lower P(PAUSE), 6.6% vs 10.9%. Against a random-half control, UPONLY's log growth ranks at the 96th percentile in 2005-15 and the 100th in 2016-26.

Execution timing matters somewhat. In 2016-26, 0.114 of the 0.514 UP-minus-DOWN gap comes from the 15:52->16:00 segment (t 4.23), which looks like a close-auction or rebalancing flow. Entering at 15:55 instead of 15:52 cuts the gap to 0.445. A re-priced or late fill keeps most of the edge but not all. In RH 5-minute real NVDL data (2026-02-23..10-13, n=159), the sign of UP minus DOWN flips depending on the 5-minute timing proxy (+0.33 vs -0.16). On the 29 nights with real 1-minute data (2026-09..10), exact 15:52->09:31 timing gives UP +1.16% vs DOWN -0.14%. Recent evidence is noisy, not decisive.

The recent reversal is real but not significant. Daily close->open 2x, last year to 2026-10: UP +0.215% vs DOWN +0.533% (t -0.94). At 0.07%/side UPONLY would have made about $2.6 a year against $44.6 a year for the current rule. This regime question belongs to the out-of-sample lens. It does not change the cost and feasibility conclusion.
recomputed_numbers: Synthetic 2x NVDA, 15:52->09:31, 1-minute data 2005-01..2026-03, earnings nights excluded, gross per night: 2005-15 UP +0.166% / DOWN -0.042% (t 1.76); 2016-26Q1 UP +0.576% / DOWN +0.062% (t 3.78); last 2y UP +0.720% / DOWN +0.175% (t 1.58); last 1y to 2026-03 UP +0.405% / DOWN +0.267% (t 0.31)
Per held night after costs, 2016-26: +0.386% at 0.07%/side + 0.05% drag; +0.226% at 0.15%/side (candidate: 0.382 and 0.222); held 51.3% of nights (about 129 a year)

Expected $ a year at E=103, 0.88 exposure, 2016-26: at 0.07%/side the current rule makes $30.9 and UPONLY $45.2 (+$14.3); at 0.15%/side -$5.6 vs +$26.5; at 0.03%/side $54.7 vs $57.4; at zero cost $74.3 vs $67.5

votes.survives_if: 1. Present it as risk reduction at no cost to growth, not as a growth-adding signal. The robust result is that P(PAUSE) falls about 3x and P(KILL) about 10x. The growth gain is real only while the all-in cost (spread, slippage and NVDL drag) is at least about 0.1-0.15% per round trip. At zero cost it is about 0 over 2016-26; at the live-measured cost (about 0.03%/side plus 0.026% drag) it is positive but not significant. 2. Enter at 15:52 sharp: about 22% of the UP/DOWN gap comes from 15:52->16:00. 3. Read the signal from the first 5-minute bar's open (or the official open) and NVDA's price at 15:50. 4. Expect long-term growth about equal to or better than the current rule, and accept that it can lag in some years: the last 12 months lagged by about $40 a year at 0.07%/side. Pre-register a review that compares skipped-night outcomes with held-night outcomes. Do not adopt it on the t 4.29 per-trade figure.

candidate.in_sample: Chosen POST HOC from a 2x2 sign table, so treat it as data-snooped. The both-down bucket was ~0 gross in every 1-minute period: 2005-2015 -0.014%, 2016-2021.03 -0.007%, 2021.04-2026.03 -0.075% (2x gross). Daily 2001-2013H1: skipped nights -0.009% vs kept +0.254% (t -1.97).

votes.candidate: SKIP_BOTHDOWN: skip the 15:52 NVDL/NVDX entry when NVDA at 15:50 is below both today's open and the previous close
reasons: No real out-of-sample test exists. The rule was picked after the fact from a 2x2 sign table built on the whole sample, and the BOTHDOWN variant was preferred over UPONLY and SKIPDOWN because it held up better in 2026. That is selection on the most recent data. The claimed 'OOS' daily split (2013H2-2026) was part of the selection set.

The first decade of 1-minute data (2005-2015) does not support it. Skipped vs kept 2x gross was -0.029% vs +0.099%, a difference of -0.129% at t=-1.04. With 1% winsorizing the difference is -0.039% (t=-0.37), and a rank test points the other way (z=+1.60). Against a random skip of the same frequency, the rule was better in only 5 of 11 years. Its edge over that control is +90 log-points for the decade, but -30 without 2008, and 2008 is driven mostly by a single night: the 2008-07-02 profit warning, -28.6% at 1x, which fell in the skip bucket.

The sign of the effect flips between eras in the same regime. In 2005-2015, when NVDA's trailing 60-day return was positive, skipped nights did better than kept nights (+0.259%, t=+2.15). In 2016-2026 under the same condition, skipped nights did worse (-0.670%, t=-4.53). On daily data, 2009-2016 shows no effect at all (diff +0.031%, t=+0.29).

It does not carry over to related assets, so the stated mechanism is weak. On 1x close-to-open nights, QQQ, SPY, MSFT, INTC and AVGO show skipped nights doing as well or better than kept nights in both 2005-2015 and 2016-2026 (QQQ t=+1.05 and +0.89; SPY t=+0.73 and +1.03). Only AMD and MU show some same-sign effect, and only after 2016. It also contradicts RULES section 1's own claim that the night after a down intraday session is better.

The effect has faded or reversed recently. On NVDA daily data, the last 2 years give a difference of -0.175% (t=-0.54) and the last 1 year +0.307% (t=+0.90). On the executable 15:50 signal in the last year, kept nights net at 0.07%/side were +0.178% and skipped nights would have been +0.218% (difference t=+0.12). On real NVDL from 2026-04 to 2026-10, skipped nights averaged +0.373% vs +0.251% for kept nights.

The candidate's '2026-04..10 real NVDL ~break-even' result comes from look-ahead in the signal. It used the daily close sign as a stand-in for the 15:50 signal. With RH 10-minute bars and the real 15:50 price, the two signals disagree on 8 of 134 tail nights. On those nights the close-based signal skipped NVDL losses of -4.7% and -6.9% (the drop after 15:52 is known only at 16:00). With the executable signal, real NVDL at 0.07%/side made x1.06 (+12% CAGR) vs x1.17 (+35%) for the current rule. The close-based signal gives x1.22 (+46%). Last year: +17% vs +31% CAGR.

votes.candidate: SKIP_BOTHDOWN: skip the 15:52 NVDL/NVDX entry when NVDA at 15:50 is below both today's official open and yesterday's official close
reasons: Feasibility passes. The rule only removes trades. It uses no PDT slot, does not change whole-share sizing (about 2 NVDL + 1 NVDX, roughly 86-88% of $103), and does not touch the cash needed at 15:52. It needs three numbers: NVDA's last price at 15:50, the official open and the previous close. get_equity_quotes gives previous_close but not the open. The open can come from the first intraday bar: the first-bar open matched the official-open signal on 99.5% of 1-minute nights and on 100% of the 2026 5-minute nights.

Costs help the candidate, not hurt it. Skipped nights have about zero gross return, so each one avoided saves a full round-trip cost. Over the last 10 years with executable 15:52->09:31 prices, the rule adds +18.7 points a year per unit of exposure at 0.07%/side and +34.1 points at 0.15%/side. At 0.15%/side the current always-enter rule is about flat over the last 10 years (+0.019% a night after costs) and loses in 2021.10-2026.10, while SKIP still has +0.249% a night on the nights it keeps (t 2.95).

Out of sample the result holds across long windows. In 1-minute executable data, nights kept under the 15:50 signal beat skipped nights in 2016-2021.03 (2x gross +0.570 vs -0.004, t -3.00) and in 2021.04-2026.03 (+0.567 vs -0.079, t -3.00). The second half 2015.08-2026.03 gives t -4.29. 2005-2015 is weak on gross (+0.079 vs -0.002, t -0.66), but SKIP still beats ALWAYS there because it pays fewer costs while the whole strategy loses money. The result also beats a control that skips a random 38% of nights: last-10y CAGR is +59.6% vs +17.7% at 0.07%/side, and P(PAUSE within 60) is 10.8% vs 17.7% vs 33.1% for always-enter. So the PAUSE reduction is not only lower exposure. Since 2016, 17 of the 25 nights at or below -10% (2x) fell on skip days.

Execution flaw in the candidate's evidence: a signal at the close is not the same as the signal you can trade at 15:50. The two disagree on about 4% of nights, and those nights carry a large gap. Nights the 15:50 signal skips but the close signal keeps averaged +0.57% (2005-15) and +0.19% (2016-26) at 2x. Nights the 15:50 signal keeps but the close signal skips averaged -0.55% and -0.69%. Daily close-based backtests therefore overstate what can actually be traded. The candidate filled its 2026 tail with the daily close sign, and that is what produced its 'break-even in the adverse regime' claim.

That claim is refuted with fresh Robinhood 5-minute prices. For real NVDL 2026-04-01..10-13, trading 15:50->09:30 with earnings nights excluded and full exposure: gross ALWAYS +42.5% vs SKIP(15:50) +19.1%. At 0.07%/side it is +18.5% vs +6.3%; at 0.15%/side -4.0% vs -6.6%. Only the close-sign version comes out near even (+37.9% gross, +23.8% at 0.07%/side). Over the last year the rule costs -18.6 points a year at 0.07%/side and -2.1 at 0.15%/side. In the current regime its expected dollar value is negative: about -$17 a year at 0.07%/side and E $103.

The headline after-cost figure (+0.372%/trade, t 4.67) only holds at 0.07%/side over the last 10 years; I get +0.409 there (t 4.85). At 0.15%/side the kept-night mean is +0.249 for the last 10 years, +0.142 for the last 2 years (t 0.76), -0.020 for the last year, and -0.017 for 2005-2026.03 (t -0.30). Realistic live cost is probably about 0.03-0.07%/side: today's spreads were NVDL 34.61/34.62 and NVDX 19.47/19.48, roughly 0.015-0.026% half-spread. The worst kept night is close to the claim: -29.0% (2019-01-25, 1-minute data).

reasons: The headline direction reproduces, so this is not a data error. Synthetic 2x NVDA built from fresh data (RH daily NVDA 2000-11..2026-10 and raw 1-minute HF NVDA 2005..2026-03), with earnings nights in cash, 0.07%/side cost and 0.02%/night ETF drag, gives 2016-2026 CAGR of DOWN1 +46.3% vs CUR +30.4% vs UPONLY +52.6% (1m data) and +30.4% vs +15.8% vs +36.6% (daily data).

Against a constant exposure matched to DOWN1's average (0.64), the 2005-2015 value added is +3.5%/yr log (t=+0.74). Without 2008 it is -3.5%/yr (t=-0.90). Against CUR without 2008 it is +2.9%/yr (t=+0.53) on 1m data and 0.0%/yr on daily data. The raw 2x down-minus-up night difference for 2005-2015 is -0.106% (t=-0.88), and for 2010-2015 it has the opposite sign (+0.084%).

Out of sample at realistic NVDL costs, the gain over CUR is not clearly significant. For 2016-2026 at 0.07%/side it is +11.5%/yr log (t=1.57, 1m) and +11.9%/yr (t=1.75, daily), with block-bootstrap p of about 0.04-0.05. The arithmetic gain is only +0.023%/night (about $6/yr at E=103). Most of the CAGR uplift is lower volatility drag from carrying less exposure, not a better mean.

The value is concentrated in a few crash years. Of the 343 log-points of cumulative DOWN1-minus-CUR advantage over 2000-2026, 262 come from 2001, 2008 and 2022. The median year is +3.5%. DOWN1 beats CUR in only 15 of 27 years and 29 of 52 half-years. In bull regimes (NVDA above its 200-day average) the 2001-2015 down-minus-up difference is +0.007% (t=+0.14), so there was no signal. The current regime is bull: 95% of nights since 2025-10 were above the 200-day average.

The live regime has reversed, and the size of the reversal is extreme. On daily data for 2025-10..2026-10, DOWN1 minus CUR is -27.3%/yr log, with block-bootstrap P(diff<=0)=0.98. The trailing 250-night difference (-28.5% log) is at the 0.5th percentile of all rolling windows since 2000. On real NVDL at 0.07%/side, 2025-05..2026-10 gives DOWN1 +36.6% vs CUR +48.3%, and 2026-04..10 gives +14.9% vs +35.0%. Expected value over the last 12 months is about -$32/yr at E=103.

The P(PAUSE) benefit does not come from the signal. Whole-share bootstrap from E=103 gives P(PAUSE within 60) of CUR 37.4%, DOWN1 14.6%, UPONLY 10.6%. A constant 0.64 exposure gives 15.2% (16.8% on 2016-2026 daily data; 18.9% vs DOWN1 15.7% on 2024-10..2026-10), so the risk reduction comes from lower average exposure.

Data-snooping: the candidate is a compromise picked after UPONLY failed the most recent window, taken from a large grid (4 entry times x 4 exit times x conditions). RULES §1 claimed the opposite sign (down nights about 2x better) from 62 live nights. When the sign depends on which window you look at, the conditional is unstable.

Costs: at 0.15%/side DOWN1 looks strongly better (t about 3.1-3.7), but only because CUR itself is net negative at that cost (2016-2026 1m CUR CAGR -9.8%). That points against the overnight leg at that cost, not in favour of the signal.

votes.candidate: DOWN_1SHARE: on nights after a down NVDA session (NVDA at 15:50 below today's open), hold exactly 1 NVDL (~34% of E) instead of the full §3(c) basket (~88%); exit at 09:31 as usual
reasons: Mechanics are not the problem. The rule is feasible under every constraint I checked: no PDT slot is used, it does not conflict with the 15:52 cash, whole shares work (1 NVDL = $34.65 = 33% of E at E=105.8), and the signal can be computed in time. A 15:48 signal instead of 15:50 changes the result by only +0.0015%/night of log growth.

The claimed growth gain comes from the cost assumption, not from the signal. The gain over the current rule on a given night is (0.345-0.88) x (down-night return - 2c), where c is the cost per side. The rule therefore adds arithmetic return only if c is more than half the gross down-night mean. That breakeven is 0.031%/side on synthetic 2x NVDA 2016-26, 0.048%/side on real NVDL 2024-02..26-10, 0.063% for the last 2 years and 0.146% for 2026 YTD. The candidate assumed 0.07%/side, which is above most of these breakevens, so its +$6.5/yr is built in by the cost choice.

Measured execution cost is about 0, not 0.07%. I compared 25 live overnight fills (2026-09-09..10-13) with Robinhood 1-minute bars. Against the bar typical price, entries averaged -0.006% and exits -0.020%, i.e. slightly better than the reference. Against the last trade, entries were +0.009% and exits -0.035%. Exit noise is large (sd 0.33%, n=25), so 0.07% cannot be excluded, but the point estimate is about 0.

At realistic low costs the expected-dollar gain is zero or negative. At 0.03%/side: 2016-26 synthetic -$0.1/yr (t -0.02); last 2 years -$4.6/yr; 2026 YTD -$16.6/yr. On real NVDL 2024-26: -$2.5/yr at 0.03% and -$6.8/yr at 0. Even at the task's half-spread+0.05% (about 0.065%), the gain is +$5.2/yr (t 0.81) for 2016-26, +$1/yr (t 0.06) for the last 2 years, +$3.1/yr (t 0.22) on real NVDL and -$10/yr in 2026. It is not significant in any window from 2016 on.

The first-half (2005-15) support is all 2008. Down nights lost -1.46%/night that year, and 2008 alone adds +142% of log growth to the candidate's advantage. Without 2008, the up-minus-down night difference in 2005-15 is -0.019% (t -0.18), and the candidate trails the current rule (CAGR +6.5% vs +9.3% at 0.02%/side). In 2016-26 at 0.03%, the total log gain of +50.5% falls to +19.9% without 2022 and to +10.8% without both 2018 and 2022. So the gain is bear-market insurance, not a steady edge.

The most recent regime runs against it. On real NVDL 2026-04..10 at 0.02-0.03%/side, CAGR is +56.6% vs +75.9% for the current rule. For 2026 YTD synthetic it is +66.5% vs +92.9%. Down nights in 2026 averaged +0.27..0.29% gross.

What does survive is risk reduction, and it holds in every dataset and at every cost level. In my block bootstrap (from E=105.81 with a 20-session high of 107.02), P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) falls from 30-34% to 11-14% at 0.02-0.07%/side. P(KILL within 250) falls from 0.7-3.5% to 0-0.4%. Median equity is about the same: 2016-26 synthetic at 0.02%, 250 sessions, median 175 vs 182 and mean 194 vs 192; real NVDL median 216 vs 218 and mean 238 vs 230. But it is a de-risking rule with roughly zero expected-growth gain, not the growth adder that was claimed.

If anything, use only a catastrophic stop. On all other mornings keep the 09:31 exit. A late wake after 10:00 sells immediately. Triggering on NVDA's 09:31 trade <= -3% instead of the open gives the same result (n=81, +2.02%, t 3.7).

votes.candidate: C1-A: Conditional exit delay (NVDA gap-down >= 3% -> sell overnight NVDL/NVDX leg at 10:00 instead of 09:31)
reasons: The rule as written is refuted. Its -3% trigger and its per-event numbers (+1.94%/event, t 3.3, 4.7 events/yr) do not hold out of sample. Since 2019 the whole edge comes from crash opens of -5% or worse. The -3% to -5% band, which is 72% of 2019+ events, has had zero edge.

My reproduction from the 1-min data (UTC converted to ET, gap from Robinhood official open vs prior close, the same earnings-reaction list excluded) is close to the reported figures. ALL 2011-07..2026-03: n=77, +1.92%/event on 2x, t 3.5. H1: n=19, +3.31, t 3.1. H2 2019+: n=58, +1.46, t 2.3, median +0.44, mean without the top 3 events +0.73. Last 2y: n=11, +1.45, t 1.0, mean without the top 3 events -0.57. Pre-2011: n=46, +1.91, t 2.2. So the headline numbers are real in sample.

H2 split by gap size: the (-5%,-3%] band (n=42) averages +0.01%/event at 10:00, median -0.72%, about a coin flip. It contributes 0.0003%/night. Gaps of -5% or worse (n=16) average +5.26% (t 3.2) and contribute 0.0432%/night, which is all of the H2 gain (0.0435%/night). This does not depend on where the cut is placed: the band from -3% down to -4, -4.5, -6 or -7% has a mean of -0.17 to +0.11 and a negative median every time. Adding the candidate's own market-panic filter (QQQ gap <= -1%) still leaves the H2 band at n=34, +0.24, t 0.5. Last-2y band: n=7, mean -0.64.

Multiple testing: I ran a sign-flip max-t check over the same family the researcher searched (7 thresholds x 14 exit times = 98 cells). On the full sample the chosen cell survives (t 4.04, p=0.0016). Within H2 alone it does not: t 2.27 vs a null 95% max-t of 2.88, p=0.15.

The 10:00 exit was chosen with hindsight. Walk-forward selection by t-stat, using only prior years, picks (-3%, 09:35) every year from 2009 to 2026. That rule earns +0.70%/event out of sample in H2 (t 2.4) and +0.74 in the last 2y (-0.07 without the top 3), half of what the chosen cell shows. Walk-forward selection by $/yr picks -1.5% and fails: H2 +0.10, last 2y -0.12. Pre-2019 data favoured 09:35-09:45 exits, and in H2 the moderate band's bounce is gone by 10:00 (medians: 09:40 +0.66, 10:00 -0.72).

The result leans on a few events and one crisis. H2 year-clustered t is 1.60. Dropping 2020 alone takes H2 to +0.92, t 1.27. The top 5 events supply 73% of the H2 total. By year in H2: 2019 -5.1, 2020 +42.3, 2021 +20.6, 2022 -12.9, 2023 +3.8, 2024 +20.0, 2025 +15.9 (sums of 2x deltas, %).

What does hold: crash opens of -5% or worse are positive in every period (pre-2011 n=8 +5.94 t 2.2; H1 n=2 +9.99; H2 n=16 +5.26 t 3.2; last 2y n=4 +5.11) and at every exit from 09:35 to 10:30 in H2 (+2.0 to +6.0). That fits a market-panic overreaction mechanism. The -3% wrapper adds about 6 zero-edge, higher-variance mornings a year, and its worst cases are -6.1% / -5.4% on the 2x position on days already deep in drawdown.

The three events after the research period (Robinhood 5-min bars, official open used in place of the 09:31 price, all in the -3% band) came out +2.67, +1.28 and -0.42. That is too few to decide anything, and the open proxy is biased.

Not refuted on expected value: the -3% rule's H2 gain is about the same as a crash-only rule's. It is refuted because the stated mechanism, frequency, per-event edge and confidence for the -3% trigger do not survive out of sample. The P(PAUSE)/P(KILL) bootstrap claims rest on in-sample means and need to be re-run on the narrowed rule.

votes.candidate: C1-A: Conditional exit delay (NVDA gap-down >= 3% -> sell overnight NVDL/NVDX leg at 10:00 instead of 09:31)
reasons: Through the costs, execution and feasibility lens I could not refute it. The rule adds no orders: on event days the single planned sell moves from 09:31 to 10:00. There are no extra transaction costs, no PDT slot, no conflict with the 15:52 cash (proceeds arrive by about 10:02 under limited margin), and no whole-share or $103 sizing problem, because the position is the one already held.

There is no cost asymmetry against the delayed exit. On event days, the NVDL and NVDX 1-minute high-low range matches 2x NVDA's at both 09:31 and 09:59, so neither time shows extra ETF microstructure cost (median excess -0.04 / -0.07 pts at 09:31 vs -0.04 / -0.18 at 09:59). Their premium to 2x NAV is about 0 at both times from 2024-07 on. Volatility in the 09:31 bar is about twice that of the 09:59 bar, so a 10:00 fill is if anything cheaper and less noisy. The 7 live 09:31 exits (10/06-10/14) filled between -0.55% and +0.43% of the 09:30-bar close, which shows how noisy the first minute is.

Real ETFs track the synthetic. NVDL, 18 events 2023-02..2025-11 (1-min data): real 09:31->10:00 +2.09%/event (t 1.5) vs synthetic +2.21, corr 0.988; its 2023 rows are distorted by early NVDL premium and illiquidity. NVDX, n=14: real +2.57 vs synthetic +2.57, corr 1.000. Of the three 2026 events after the 1-min data ends, two (04-28, 06-23) use the 5-min open as the 09:31 proxy, which is approximate. On those days real NVDL was +2.57% (open->10:00) and +1.26%, and on 09-14 it was +0.34% (09:31->10:00 from 1-min bars).

Main execution caveat: the measured gain is front-loaded right after 09:31. If the baseline exit were at 09:32 the gain falls from +1.86 to +1.38; at 09:33 it is +1.27 and at 09:35 +0.73. The comparison is valid only because live 09:31 exits really are sent at 09:31:09-12, which I checked in orders.jsonl. The late side is robust: exiting at 10:05 gives +1.85 and at 10:30 +1.76.

Trigger feasibility: Robinhood get_equity_quotes has no official-open field (I checked: it returns last trade, bid/ask and previous_close), so the '09:30:30 official open' wording needs an extra minute-bars call. Use NVDA's last trade at 09:31 vs previous_close instead. It does at least as well: 2011-07+ n=92, +1.89 (t 3.9); 2019+ n=59, +1.54 (t 2.4). Days where the open was <= -3% but 09:31 had recovered above -3% average about 0 (n=15, -0.04).

Concentration risk, which matters for the dollar estimate: the edge sits in crash opens. Gaps <= -6% give n=21, +6.97% (t 5.0), and are consistent in every period. Gaps from -3% to -6% since 2019 give n=44, about -0.17%/event. Excluding the top 3, the last-2y mean is -0.08 (n=11). Because the delay costs nothing in transactions, the weak bucket mainly adds variance, not cost.

The candidate has small bookkeeping errors. It lists 2024-08-05 as a last-2y driver, but that date is outside 2024-10-14..2026-10-13; the actual top 3 there are 2025-04-07, 2025-01-27 and 2026-04-28. My event counts are higher (H1 2011-07..2018 n=22 vs 16; pre-2011-07 n=47 vs 31), and with more events the H1 mean is lower (+2.74 vs +3.91). The direction and significance are unchanged.

Risk is not raised. Worst event is -8.52% on the 2x position (2008-10-06), with H2 worst -6.14% and worst intra-window adverse excursion -11.5%. At about 88% exposure that is roughly -$7.5 at most from $103, nowhere near KILL. My paired block bootstrap (60 sessions, $103, 0.88 exposure, 0.30% round trip): P(PAUSE) 31.0->29.3% (2011-07+), 44.2->44.1% (2019+), 37.6->36.9% (last 2y). P(E<=50 with PAUSE sizing ignored) 0.43->0.19%, 1.20->0.54%, 0.86->0.25%. The PAUSE reduction is smaller than claimed for 2019+ (claimed 44.5->41.5), but it is never an increase.

Context outside this candidate: in my synthetic close->09:31 2x-NVDA series, the base overnight night after 0.30% round trip at 0.88 exposure averages -0.083%/night (2011-07+) and -0.006% (2019+). Costs consume nearly all of the overnight leg's gross edge. C1-A's +0.03%/night is a small, cost-free add-on and does not fix that.

Gap buckets since 2019: (-3,-4] n=23 +0.07; (-4,-6] n=21 -0.44; <= -6% n=14 +6.60 (t 4.3). All years, <= -6%: n=21, +6.97 (t 5.0). 2011-07+: 10 of 13 calendar years with events net positive.

Real ETFs on events: NVDL n=18, +2.09 (t 1.5) vs synthetic +2.21, corr 0.988. NVDX n=14, +2.57 vs +2.57, corr 1.000. Premium to 2x NAV 2024-07+ about 0 at both 09:31 and 10:00. ETF 1-min range = 2x NVDA range (no excess spread).
Paired per-night equity effect (0.88 exposure, 0.30% round trip, earnings nights in cash): 2005+ +0.0330% (t 3.8); 2011-07+ +0.0291% (t 3.2); 2019+ +0.0327% (t 2.2); last 2y +0.0301% (t 1.2).

Expected gain is about $1.3/event, about $9-10/yr at the H2 or last-2y mean, and only about $3-4/yr on a median basis. There is no incremental transaction cost.
votes.survives_if: It survives as a cost-free change to the existing 09:31 exit, under these conditions. (1) The trigger is NVDA's last trade at 09:31:00 vs the quote's previous_close (<= -3%), because Robinhood quotes have no official-open field. Optionally confirm the open with a minute-bar call. (2) The baseline exit on non-event days stays a real 09:31:05-09:31:15 marketable sell, since most of the measured gain comes from the first minutes after 09:31. (3) No stop tighter than a catastrophic one goes in during 09:31-10:00. (4) A late wake sells at once after 10:00, and the 15:52 entry is sized from the 10:00 proceeds as usual. (5) Expectations stay modest: about $3-10/yr at $103, driven almost entirely by crash opens (gaps <= -6%). The -3% to -6% bucket has been about zero to slightly negative since 2019, so the rule must not be widened, levered up, or turned into an extra intraday buy. A pre-registered review should compare realized 10:00 vs 09:31 counterfactual prices after about 10 events.

votes.candidate: C1-D: Conditional exit delay on market gap (QQQ open <= -1.5% -> sell overnight NVDL/NVDX at 10:00 instead of 09:31)
reasons: The headline numbers reproduce, so this is not a computation error. I re-derived everything from fresh Robinhood daily bars (QQQ/SPY/NVDA/IWM/DIA, 2004-2026, official open gaps) and my own extraction of the raw HF 1-minute files. Results (2x NVDA, 09:31->10:00): EARLY (SPY proxy) n=48, +2.54% (t 3.1); H1 n=32, +1.61 (t 2.9); H2 to 2026-03 n=82, +1.25 (t 2.7, month-clustered t 2.9); last 2y n=14, +1.16 (t 1.0, excluding top 3 -0.49). The threshold x exit-time surface is smooth and positive, so a cherry-picked cell is NOT the problem.

The out-of-sample problem is decay of the stated mechanism. Split events into 'ordinary' firings (-3% < market gap <= -1.5%, 83% of H2 events, ~9.4/yr) and 'crash' firings (<= -3%). Ordinary events decayed steadily, measured from 09:31: 2005-08 +2.90 (t 2.3), 2009-12 +1.20, 2013-16 +0.89, 2017-20 +1.21, 2021-23 +0.05 (t 0.1), 2024-26 +0.29 (t 0.4). Across all of H2, ordinary events are +0.27% (t 0.8) from 09:31 and -0.07% (t -0.2) from 09:32. Adding the 2026-04..09 Robinhood events gives a last-2y ordinary mean of about -0.13% (n=16, t -0.3). For most days it fires, the rule as written has had no edge since about 2021.

All of H2 and the last 2 years rests on a few crash days. H2 crash events (QQQ gap <= -3%): n=14, +6.02% (t 3.6, 8 month clusters). These include 2020-03-09 +10.5, 2020-09-08 +7.9, 2022-02-24 +8.3, 2024-08-05 +20.0 and 2025-04-07 +13.9. In the last 2 years, 2025-04-07 alone is about 85% of the summed gain: excluding it, the last-2y mean is +0.18% over 13 events. The candidate's own figures (last-2y median +0.08, excluding top 3 -0.24) are consistent with this.

The broader opening-reversal effect that is supposed to drive this has faded across instruments. The same rule, 1x 09:31->10:00, in H2 vs the last 2y: SPY +0.07 / -0.09, IWM +0.05 / -0.00, DIA +0.01 / -0.15. The reversal on market gap-ups (>= +1%) went from -1.18 (EARLY) and -0.64 (H1) to +0.11 in H2. Moderate down-gaps (-1.5% to -0.5%) went from +1.00 / +0.66 to -0.07 in H2 and -0.23 in the last 2y. This is a classic arbitraged-away anomaly. Only the extreme-panic tail still pays.

Execution timing matters a lot. The live exit bridges to 09:31:05 and then re-prices after 60 seconds, so fills land between the 09:31 and 09:32 prints. Measured from 09:32, H2 falls to +0.74% (t 1.7, clustered t 1.78). H2 excluding 2020 and 2022 is +1.22 (t 1.7). Some crash days flip on a 1-minute shift: 2020-03-18 is +5.76 from 09:31 and -0.24 from 09:32. About 0.5pp (2x) of the H2 effect is the 09:31->09:32 bounce (t 3.3), which the live 09:31:05+ marketable exit partly catches anyway.

Before 2019 the crash bucket is thin. It is +3.75% over n=13, month-clustered t 1.49, and the mean excluding the best month is +1.28. So 'crash days bounce in the first 30 minutes' is a plausible capitulation mechanism with roughly 27 observations in 21 years. It is not a clearly surviving out-of-sample edge, and narrowing the rule to <= -3% after seeing this split would itself be a post-hoc choice.

Expected value is overstated. The candidate's +1.23%/event and $8.9/yr assume the full-sample event mean applies to all firings going forward. Treat ordinary days as zero (their 2021+ value) and use only the crash component: about 1.3 crash days/yr long-run x +3.75% (pre-2019 mean) x 0.93 exposure x $103 is about $4.6/yr, and lower from 09:32. Using the H2 crash mean (1.9/yr x +6.02%) gives about $11/yr, but that depends on 2-3 single days.
