votes.survives_if: It survives only as a much narrower and explicitly low-confidence crash-day tweak. Delay the 09:31 exit only when QQQ's official gap is <= -3% (about 1-2 days/yr). Book its expected value at about +$3-5/yr, not $8.9: use the pre-2019 crash mean and measure from the realistic 09:31:05-09:32 exit. State plainly that it rests on about 27 events in 21 years, dominated by a handful of panic days, with a month-clustered t of about 1.5 before 2019. Pre-register a forward shadow log on executable 1-minute prices before relying on it. The -1.5% version as specified should not be adopted on the claim of +1.23%/event: its ordinary firings (83% of events) have shown ~0 (09:31 base) or slightly negative (09:32 base) returns since 2021. Its only defensible merit is that it costs nothing in trades or PDT slots, so ordinary-day firings are roughly mean-zero noise rather than a loss.

votes.candidate: C1-D: Conditional exit delay on market gap (QQQ open <= -1.5% -> sell overnight NVDL/NVDX at 10:00 instead of 09:31)
reasons: Lens = costs, execution and feasibility. I rebuilt everything from fresh Robinhood daily bars (QQQ/SPY/NVDA 2004-12..2026-10-13, NVDL/NVDX since listing) and my own checkpoint table from the raw 1-minute extract (2005-01..2026-03). I checked that extract against RH 5-minute bars on 2026-03-30: the labels are bar-start, and open, close, high and low match exactly. For the 5 events after 2026-03 I used RH 1-minute bars (09-14) and 5-minute bars (04-02, 06-23, 07-17, 07-23). Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/wf3/c1d-skeptic-cost/scripts/ (build.py, a1-a7.py).

Replication holds. The 2x synthetic NVDA return from 09:31 to 10:00 on market-gap mornings is: 2005-2011-06 (SPY proxy) n=48 +2.54% (t 3.1); H1 2011-07..2018 n=32 +1.61% (t 2.9); H2 2019..2026-03 n=82 +1.25% (t 2.7). My event counts differ from the candidate's in the early window (48 vs 29) but are close elsewhere.

Costs: the rule adds no transaction. It moves one exit that happens anyway from 09:31 to 10:00, and both use the same marketable-limit mechanics. Spreads on NVDL/NVDX are widest right after a gap-down open, so if anything the delay lowers execution cost. I could not measure historical spreads, so I credit no saving. After-cost increment = gross increment.

Execution timing is the main fragility, and it survives. About 40% of the H2 effect lands in the single minute 09:31->09:32 (+0.50% on 2x, t 3.3). Example: on 2026-03-30 NVDA moved +0.92% in that minute. Live exit orders go out at 09:31:09-10 (orders.jsonl), so the true baseline sits slightly after the model's 09:31:00 print. H2 increment by baseline time: 09:31:10 interpolated +1.17% (t 2.6); 09:31:30 +0.99% (t 2.3); worst case 09:32 +0.74% (t 1.7). Over the whole sample a 09:32 baseline still gives +1.27% (t 3.9).

The signal is observable in real time. The rule's 'official open at 09:30:30' may not be in the quote feed, but alternatives work as well or better. votes.survives_if: It survives as an exit-timing change only, with these conditions. (1) Define the trigger by a price the agent can see. Use QQQ's last trade at 09:30:30-09:31:00 vs the prior official close, or fall back to the 09:29 pre-market price. Do not rely on an 'official open' field that the quote feed may not carry. All of these give the same result. (2) Keep the normal 09:31:05 exit, filling by about 09:31:15, on every non-event morning. On event mornings, sell at 10:00:00 with the unchanged §5 marketable-limit ladder. Any wake after 10:00 sells immediately. (3) Apply it only when the leg is actually held, not on §3(f) decay-cash or earnings nights. Plan the value at roughly +$4-10 a year at E=103, not a firm +$8.9, because 35-51% of past events had the leg in cash under §3(f). (4) Do not stack a stop, any added exposure, or a re-entry on top of it. (5) Pre-register a live and shadow log of the 09:31 bid vs the 10:00 bid on every event, including events where the leg is in cash. Review it at the quarterly review, accepting that n will be small (about 4-11 events a year). Revert if the cumulative increment over the first 15 held events is negative, since the last-2y evidence (t about 1, negative without the top 3) cannot by itself rule out decay.

I reproduced the proposer's headline numbers closely. H2 incl. fresh: n=163, mean +0.55%, t 1.96, median +0.12 (claimed n=157, +0.53, t 1.9). L2: n=46, +0.43, t 0.94, ex-top3 -0.10 (claimed +0.47, t 1.0, -0.09). So the refutation does not rest on a data disagreement.

What separates C1-C from C1-D is the band -1.5% < QQQ gap <= -1.0%, and that band fails out of sample. Over 2019-2026 it averages -0.17% per event (n=77, t -0.54, median -0.34). C1-D beats C1-C in the OOS half. Over 2019-2026 the summed increment is +103.1 percentage-points for C1-D (n=86, per-night +0.053%, t 2.62) versus +89.9 for C1-C (n=163, per-night +0.046%, t 1.94). Widening the trigger to -1.0% doubles the number of holds, adds variance, and loses expected return.

Snooping evidence across 144-171 trigger x threshold x exit cells (QQQ/SPY/NVDA). The t-stats of a cell in H1 (2011-07..2018) and H2 have Spearman correlation -0.03, so in-sample ranking does not predict OOS ranking. The H1-best QQQ cell (-0.5%, 09:45 exit, t 5.5) collapses to +0.08% (t 0.58) in H2. The C1-C cell ranked only 57/144 in H1. Its 10:00 exit looks like an H2 local spike: in H2 the means are +0.27 at 09:45, +0.23 at 09:50, +0.64 at 10:00 and +0.46 at 10:10, so the exit was likely picked after seeing all the data. Selecting on pre-2024-10 data and testing on L2: median cell t 0.77, and only 1% of cells reach t>2.

The only data no one had seen when choosing the rule is the 2026-04..10 window, measured on real NVDL (open proxy, true 09:31 minute prices on 3 days): n=15, mean -0.36%, t -0.77, ex-top3 -0.95.

The result depends on a few crash rebounds. In H2 the top 5 events (2024-08-05 +20.0, 2025-04-07 +13.9, 2020-03-09 +10.5, 2022-02-24 +8.3, 2020-09-08 +7.9) make up 60.6 of the 89.9-point sum. Winsorizing H2 at +/-5% gives +0.27 (t 1.26). H2 without the 2020-02..04 and 2025-04 crash months gives +0.40 (t 1.42). Dropping just the 2 largest L2 events leaves 0.00.

The proposer's 'after-cost mean 0.78' and t 3.4 are dominated by 2005-2018 and do not describe the current regime. The $8.6/yr estimate assumes the H2 average persists, while the last 12 months give $0.

Costs are not the problem. Swapping the 09:31 exit for a 10:00 exit adds no trade, and spreads at 10:00 are usually no wider. The refutation is about out-of-sample performance and data snooping, not costs. The wider 'large gap-down reverses by about 10:00' family does have long-run support (2005-15 -> 2016-26 median cell t 2.8). C1-C's own extra content (the -1.0..-1.5% band) does not.

votes.candidate: C1-C: Broader market trigger (QQQ open <= -1.0% -> hold overnight NVDL/NVDX to a 10:00 exit instead of 09:31)
reasons: The rule is cheap and feasible to run. It is not a day trade (the position was bought the day before), so it uses no PDT slot. Cash is free from 10:00, well before the 15:52 entry. Whole-share sizing and the $103 equity do not change. The extra cost is about zero because there is still exactly one exit, at bid - 0.15% either way, and spreads are probably narrower at 10:00 than at 09:31 on gap-down days. Live exit orders go out at about 09:31:10 ET (orders.jsonl), so using the 09:31 price as the baseline is realistic. So costs and feasibility do not kill it. What fails is the part this candidate adds on top of C1-D.

The trigger can be observed in time, but the threshold edge is noise. get_equity_quotes has no 'open' field. Using QQQ's last trade at 09:31 or its 09:25 pre-market price instead of the official open gives the same results over 2011-2026: +0.83% and +0.88% per event against +0.87% (2x, 09:31->10:00). However, the 19 events that only the official open catches lose -0.64% in H2, and the 12 that only the 09:31-price version catches lose -0.46% in H2. Events near the -1.0% line carry no edge.

Main reason: everything C1-C adds over C1-D has no edge since 2019. These are the events with -1.5% < QQQ gap <= -1.0%. On synthetic 2x NVDA (09:31->10:00, NVDA earnings days excluded): 2005-2011/06 +1.04% (t 2.1), H1 2011/07-2018 +1.10% (t 2.3), but H2 2019-2026 n=77 -0.17% (t -0.5, median -0.61%) and the last 2 years n=27 +0.06% (median -0.44%). On real NVDL prices: n=35, +0.13%, median -0.63%, win rate 40%. On real NVDX: n=31, +0.22%, median -0.35%. In dollars the band is worth -$1.6/yr (H2) to +$0.8/yr (last 2 years) at E=$103 and about 93% exposure. Every positive H2 and last-2-year number in C1-C comes from the C1-D subset (QQQ <= -1.5%: H2 +1.22%, t 2.8).

Execution timing makes it worse. The H2 result for the whole rule depends on the exact minute. An exit at 10:00 gives +0.61% (t 2.0). Exits at 10:03 and 10:05 give +0.41% (t 1.3) and +0.33% (t 1.0), and the average of 10:00-10:04 gives +0.43% (t 1.3). A 10:00 order that goes through the re-price ladder realistically fills at 10:00-10:02. Within the added band, H2 falls to about -0.32% to -0.39% at 10:03-10:05.

Recent performance is about zero. Over the last 12 months (from 2025-10-14) there were 23 events at +0.09% (median -0.12%, excluding the top 3: -0.48%). 2026 so far: 20 events at -0.11%. Last 2 years: real NVDL n=46, +0.50% (t 1.1, median +0.05%, excluding the top 3: -0.04%). The positive last-2-year mean comes from 2024-08-05 (+20.3%), 2025-04-07 (+14.1%) and 2024-04-10 (+7.2%).

Risk check, not a reason to refute: it does not raise PAUSE or KILL risk. In a paired 60-session block bootstrap of the overnight 2x leg at 0.93 exposure, P(PAUSE) went 10.8%->7.3% (H1), 39.8%->39.2% (H2) and 39.4%->35.9% (last 2 years), and P(KILL) did not rise. Event-day losses from the prior close of -15% or worse drop from 10 to 4. The worst single extra loss from the delay is -6.9% in H2 and -8.5% overall (2008-10-06 and 2008-09-16).

Net: as its own rule, the -1.0% threshold is dominated by C1-D (-1.5%). The extra 10-13 events a year add about 30 minutes of 2x-NVDA exposure each (sd about 3%) with zero or negative expected value since 2019. The claimed $8.6/yr is C1-D's money plus noise. The one-year standard deviation of the whole rule's dollar result is about $14-16, so a live record could not tell it apart from zero for years.

It is positive in only 3 of the 8 years since 2019. In the fresh 2026-04..10 5-minute data, the 4 bucket events made -0.01% on real NVDL (09:35->10:00).

C1-B's own H2 evidence comes mostly from 2020. All H2 (n=146): +0.62%, t 2.00. Excluding 2020 (n=121): +0.32%, t 0.94, median -0.17%, win 49%. For 2021-2026: +0.42%, t 1.13, median -0.06%. 2020 alone contributes 52 of the 91 percentage points summed over H2. The top events are crash-day rebounds that C1-A captures anyway, for example 2024-08-05 (gap -14%, +20.0%) and 2025-04-07 (gap -7%, +13.9%).

It does not survive a multiple-testing correction in the out-of-sample windows. In H2 the C1-B cell's t of 2.00 has a single-test permutation p of 0.035 but a family-wise p of 0.34 against the 84-cell grid (null 95th percentile of the grid maximum: 3.10). In the last two years (to 2026-03) it has t 1.43, single-test p 0.064 and family-wise p 0.60. The proposer's grid printed H1, H2, L2 and EARLY side by side, so the selection already used H2. H2 is not a clean holdout.

A principled walk-forward procedure never picks -2%/10:00. An expanding-window selection by t-stat over the full grid picks -3%/09:35 in 15 of 17 years, with an H2 out-of-sample increment of only +0.0135%/night. With the exit fixed at 10:00 it picks -1%, not -2%. With the exit at 10:00, the per-night H2 increment is about +0.05% for -1%, -2% and -3% alike, so the -2% choice is noise-level.

The losses cluster in bear regimes, which works against the PAUSE goal. In H2, events where NVDA's prior close was below its 200-day moving average averaged -0.23% (n=58), and the (-3%,-2%] bucket in that regime averaged -0.53%. In 2022, C1-B's 41 events summed to -27.9 percentage points on 2x, versus -12.9 for C1-A. So the extra trades lose during drawdowns, exactly when PAUSE is close. The candidate's iid bootstrap showing lower P(PAUSE) cannot capture this clustering.

The result is sensitive to how the trigger is defined. Triggering on NVDA's 09:31 price (<= -2% vs prior close) instead of the official open gives H2 +0.43% (t 1.45) and last two years +0.51% (t 0.88, median +0.01%). Real NVDL tracks the synthetic closely (n=51, corr 0.997, +1.01% vs +1.00%), so this is not a modelling artifact. It does mean the edge depends on a specific trigger definition.

votes.candidate: C1-B: Lower NVDA threshold (NVDA open <= -2% -> hold overnight NVDL/NVDX to 10:00 instead of 09:31)
reasons: Mechanics are feasible, so this is not refuted on mechanics. Selling at 10:00 a position bought the day before is not a day trade, so no PDT slot is used. Cash is back long before 15:52, and whole shares do not matter. Exit cost does not go up and probably goes down: on event days the NVDL 1-minute high-low range is 1.23% at 09:31 and 0.63% at 10:00 (NVDX 1.21% vs 0.62%), and 1-minute volume is lower at 10:00 (median about 82k vs 352k shares). The trigger can be observed: at 09:31 the 09:30 RH minute bar gives the open. A first-1m-open trigger agrees with the official open on 302 of 334 days and gives the same result. get_equity_quotes has no open field. Triggering on the 09:31 last trade, which is all a quote gives you, drops H2 to +0.43% (t 1.4) and L2 to +0.51% (t 0.9).

The core problem: since 2019 all of the edge comes from the 16 crash-open days with gaps <= -5% (+5.26%/event, t 3.2). The -2% threshold is the only thing that sets this candidate apart, and in H2 the buckets it adds are flat: (-3,-2] n=88 +0.07% (t 0.3), (-4,-3] n=23 +0.07%, (-5,-4] n=19 -0.05%. That is about 130 events a year-weighted at roughly +0.05% each, each carrying a 30-minute 2x exposure with an sd of about 3% and a worst case near -7%. The candidate's mechanism ('the effect scales with gap size, so -2% gaps carry a weak edge since 2019') is not supported out of sample.

Because those extra events add risk and almost nothing else, the -2% rule makes risk worse on the historical H2 path. Synthetic 2x, 0.93 exposure, earnings nights in cash: maxDD is -71.0% vs -63.3% for the baseline. Historical P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) rises from 39.9% to 41.6%. H2 log growth is +0.618/yr, the same as a -5% threshold (+0.615) or a -3% threshold (+0.613). A -5% threshold has maxDD -64.0% and P(PAUSE) 35.6%. So the -2% rule is dominated by a higher threshold and goes against the goal of not raising P(PAUSE). It does lower P(KILL) in H2 (2.0% to 0.6%).

The result depends heavily on exact execution timing. H2 2x delta is +0.62% (t 2.0) for an exit at 10:00 measured from 09:31:00. Moving only the exit gives +0.50% (t 1.4) at 10:02 and +0.27% (t 0.8, median -0.06%) at 10:05. Moving only the baseline to 09:32 gives +0.33% (t 1.2, median -0.12%). Full sample, the 09:32 baseline gives +0.53%; real NVDL gives +0.69% (t 1.4) vs +0.97%. The live loop sleeps up to 9 minutes between checks, and the 9/29 container restart left it dark from 10:14 to 11:04, so a precise 10:00 exit cannot be assumed. The 10:00 point is also a peak picked from a grid of exit times and thresholds.

Concentration and recent data: in H2, dropping the top 3 events leaves +0.33% (t 1.24) and dropping the top 5 leaves +0.21% (t 0.82). In L2, dropping the top 3 leaves +0.13% (t 0.3) and dropping the top 5 leaves -0.16%. 2026 events from the 1-minute data (Jan-Mar, n=3) average -1.35%. The 7 events from Apr to Sep 2026, from RH 5-minute bars plus exact 1-minute data for 9/14, average +0.18% (t 0.2). The last 12 months combined are n=13, +0.36%, t 0.48, median -0.22%.

Dollar value at E=$103 with 0.93 exposure: H2 has 20.2 events a year. $12.1/yr with a 09:31 baseline, $6.4/yr with a 09:32 baseline, and $1.0/yr if the <= -5% days, which a stricter rule would also catch, are removed. What this candidate adds over a crash-only rule is about $1/yr in exchange for higher P(PAUSE) and a deeper maxDD.

votes.survives_if: Only as a much stricter rule. One option is a crash-open version: NVDA official open gap <= about -5%, with the decision read from the 09:30 RH minute bar at 09:31 and the exit by about 10:00. That version keeps all of the H2 log growth, lowers historical P(PAUSE), and adds only about 2 events a year, but it rests on n=16 since 2019 and needs its own skeptic pass. The other option is the -2% rule validated forward: pre-registered live or shadow logging that shows the (-5%,-2%] gaps have a positive mean, with t >= 2 on executable 09:31:05 -> 10:00:05 fills. Until one of these holds, the -2% threshold adds variance and PAUSE risk with no out-of-sample edge, and the existing 09:31 exit should stay.

votes.candidate: C1 exit-time sensitivity: 09:40 instead of 10:00 (QQQ <= -1% trigger): on mornings when QQQ opens 1% or more below its previous close, keep the overnight NVDL/NVDX position past 09:31 and sell at 09:40.
reasons: Replication: I re-derived the numbers myself. Sources were fresh Robinhood daily bars for NVDA, QQQ and SPY (2004-06 to 2026-10-13), my own extraction from the raw HF 1-minute files (read-only) and fresh Robinhood 5-minute and 1-minute bars. I modeled a 2x daily-reset ETF on NVDA, measured each event from 09:31 to 09:40 relative to position value, and excluded NVDA earnings days. With the same scale-consistency filter the candidate used, I get exactly its in-sample numbers: H1 n=73, +1.09% (t 4.0); H2 n=143, +0.50% (t 2.4); last 2 years n=30, +0.35% (t 1.0). So the historical numbers are real; they just do not hold up recently.

Recent and post-sample results are flat to negative. My 1-minute data ends 2026-03-31; after that I found 15 qualifying events (Apr-Oct 2026). Using the official open in place of the 09:31 price, the mean is -0.59% (t -1.6). Robinhood still serves real 1-minute bars for 3 of them (2026-09-01, 09-10, 09-14), and all 3 lost: -0.58%, -1.42%, -1.20%. The open proxy overstates the 09:31 to 09:40 result by about +0.11% in the 1-minute sample, so the true post-sample result is probably slightly worse. Combining 1-minute days with post-sample days, the last 2 years give n=46, mean -0.02% (t -0.06).

The decline is statistically significant, not just noise. H1 vs last 2 years: Welch z = 3.1. The last-2-year mean sits 2.3 standard errors below the 2019 to Oct-2024 mean and 4.4 below the H1 mean. 2019-2022 alone was only +0.32% (t 1.3).

The H2 'out-of-sample' t of 2.4 rests on one crash day. 2024-08-05 alone contributed +15.1%. Over H2 including post-sample events: with that day n=162, +0.41% (t 2.1); without it +0.32% (t 1.8); without the top 3 +0.23% (t 1.4). Over the last 2 years, removing the top 3 turns the mean negative (-0.06%).

09:40 looks like a lucky pick, i.e. data snooping. In H2 at the -1% trigger, 09:40 is a local spike among neighboring exit times: 09:35 +0.24 (t 1.6), 09:36 +0.28 (t 1.8), 09:40 +0.52 (t 2.4), 09:46 +0.25 (t 1.0), 09:51 +0.22 (t 0.9). H2 was not a true holdout either: the researchers looked at the whole sample at once, and the family search printed about 600 configurations. Across my 98-cell grid of triggers and exit times, 86% of cells have t>2 in H1, 55% in H2, and only 5% in the last 2 years.

About half of the H2 gain comes from the first minute. The 09:31 to 09:32 step alone is +0.23 of H2's +0.52 (t 2.3), and that step is the part most exposed to opening-trade quirks. It is -0.03% in the last 2 years. If the base sell is measured at 09:32 instead of 09:31, holding to 09:40 adds only +0.29% in H2 (t 1.6) and +0.29% in the last 2 years (t 1.1).

The pattern is not specific to QQQ; it is a general bounce after a gap-down open, now fading. Every QQQ-gap-down threshold I tested shows it (-0.5% to -1% gaps: +0.31%, t 3.6 overall). Gap-up days show the mirror image (-0.33%, t -3.2 overall), and non-event days show nothing (+0.02%). The mechanism is plausible but widely known, and the trend in the data is downward.

The candidate has no real cost advantage either. Real NVDL and NVDX track the synthetic model closely (corr 0.998 and 0.995; real minus synthetic +0.005% and -0.018%), so the backtest is tradable. Both exits pay the same per-side cost, so the gain is cost-neutral at best. The 10:00 variant had a higher mean than 09:40 in every historical period I tested (all 1-minute data through March 2026); in the post-sample events both were negative. The 09:40 exit's only selling point is lower spread (event sd 2.77% vs 4.00%). The worst single event is -8.64% (2007-11-09), about -$8 at $103 equity and 93% exposure.

Expected dollars: about 20.8 events a year (2019+). At the last-2-year estimate (-0.02%/event) that is about $0/yr; at the post-sample estimate (-0.59%) about -$12/yr; even at the optimistic H2 figure without the one crash day (+0.32%) only about +$6/yr. The candidate's +$7/yr assumes the long-run average still holds, and recent data contradicts that.

votes.candidate: C1 exit-time sensitivity: 09:40 instead of 10:00 (QQQ <= -1% trigger), NVDL/NVDX
reasons: The basic numbers reproduce, so the problem is not the backtest. I rebuilt them from fresh data: Robinhood daily bars from 2005 for the official QQQ/NVDA gaps, an independent extraction from the HF 1-min files (I checked they are labelled by bar start; 92% of 5-min closes match Robinhood exactly), Robinhood 1-min bars for Sep 2026 and Robinhood 5-min bars for Apr-Oct 2026. Measured from the 09:31:00 price to the 09:40:00 price, NVDA earnings mornings excluded: H1 n=77 +1.15% (t 4.4), H2 n=150 +0.49% (t 2.3), last 2y on 1-min days n=34 +0.14% (t 0.4), last 2y with the 5-min open-proxy days added n=46 -0.02% (t -0.06).

The H2 edge depends on fills landing exactly on the minute boundaries, which this bot cannot do. Split minute by minute (2x NVDA, H2 event days), the 09:31->09:32 minute adds +0.23% (t 2.3). The real baseline sell (wait until 09:31:05, write the intent line, sell NVDL, then NVDX) fills partly inside that minute, so the baseline price is better than the model assumes. The 09:40->09:41 minute loses -0.30% (t -4.5; NVDA 1x -0.134%, t -4.1, on H2 gap-down days, against +0.044% in H1). A real 09:40:05+ fill pays part of that drop. The interior minutes 09:32->09:40 add only +0.27% (t 1.5).

With realistic fill timing the out-of-sample edge is gone. Both legs filled 1 minute late (09:32 -> 09:41): H2 -0.05% (t -0.3), last 2y -0.02%, only H1 survives at +0.87%. Both fills at the middle of their minute: H2 +0.21% (t 1.15), last 2y +0.06% (t 0.2). Exit anywhere from 09:38 to 09:42 with the baseline at 09:31: H2 +0.33% (t 1.7), last 2y -0.02%. Neighbouring exit times in H2: 09:41 +0.18% (t 0.9), 09:42 +0.20% (t 1.0), 09:45 +0.24% (t 1.0). So 09:40:00 is a local peak, not a plateau.

The dollar value at $103 is small and not robust. Sizing per §3(c) at live prices (NVDL 34.53, NVDX 19.43) gives 2 NVDL + 1 NVDX = $88.49 (86% of equity). With exact-minute fills that is about $10.0/yr over 2011-26 (15.9 events/yr), $9.1/yr in H2 (21.2/yr) and $3.0/yr in the last 2y (23.5/yr). With a 1-minute delay on both legs it is -$0.89/yr in H2 and -$0.41/yr in the last 2y. The claimed $7/yr rests on the full-sample exact-minute mean.

Risk goes up a little, not down. The candidate adds 9 minutes of 2x NVDA exposure on mornings that are already in drawdown: on event mornings the overnight leg to 09:31 averages -5.7% (2x unscaled), and 51% of them are already at -5% or worse. In a historical path simulation (overlapping 60-session windows from E=103, 88% exposure, 0.15% per side, earnings nights in cash), P(KILL) rises even with exact-minute fills: H2 1.20% -> 1.43%, 2011-26 0.58% -> 0.69%. With 1-minute-late fills in H2, P(PAUSE) goes 39.7% -> 39.9%, P(KILL) 1.66% -> 2.12%, and log growth per session falls (+0.0591% -> +0.0579%). The PAUSE reduction seen with exact-minute fills does not survive realistic timing.

Feasibility checks that pass, so the refutation does not rest on them. It uses no PDT slot (the position is bought at 15:52 and sold the next morning). Cash for the 15:52 entry is unaffected, because the limited-margin account can use sale proceeds immediately. Whole-share sizing does not change. The trigger can be seen in time: a QQQ 09:31-price trigger gives H2 +0.46% (t 2.1) and a pre-market trigger +0.51% (t 2.4), both at exact-minute timing. The always-on loop's 9-minute sleep can reach 09:40.

Two factors favour the candidate but cannot make up for the timing fragility. Real NVDL/NVDX track the synthetic 2x series on event days (NVDL n=47: real +0.76% vs synthetic +0.755%, corr 0.998). The 09:40 bar is calmer than the 09:30 bar (median 1-min high/low range on event days: NVDL 1.44% vs 0.67%), so spreads at a 09:40 exit are probably tighter. That is worth a few basis points at most.
It is also dominated by its parent rule: in the last 2y (1-min days) the 10:00 exit gave +0.66% (t 1.1) against +0.14% (t 0.4) at 09:40.

votes.survives_if: It survives only if real fills show the edge. Requirement: shadow-log the bot's actual NVDL/NVDX bid at its real 09:31 baseline fill time and at a 09:40 exit placed with the same §5 mechanics, on at least 30 QQQ <= -1% gap mornings, and the mean increment must be >= +0.2% with t >= 2. Alternatively, define the rule with a sub-minute exit (for example, fill completed by 09:39:45, to avoid the 09:40-minute drop) and validate it on 15-second bars across many events. It must also hold when the fill lands anywhere in 09:40:00-09:41:00, and it must not raise P(KILL). On current evidence the out-of-sample edge (H2 and the last 2 years) disappears with a 1-minute execution delay. It is also dominated by the 10:00 variant.

candidate.name: Gap-down hold-through (NVDA <= -3%: skip the 09:31 exit and the 15:52 re-entry, hold to next morning)
candidate.exact_rule: If NVDA open <= -3%, do not sell the overnight leg at 09:31; hold it through the session and the next night (sell at next morning's 09:31). Delta = 2x return 09:31->15:52 + 0.30% round-trip cost saved.
candidate.mechanism: Captures the 09:31-10:00 rebound plus the cost saving, but then holds the flat-to-negative rest of the session at 2x. Dominated by C1-A: similar mean, worst event -14.3% vs -6.1%, lower t.
candidate.data_used: Same as C1-A.
candidate.family: OPENING-GAP AND OPENING-AUCTION EFFECTS (SPY/QQQ/IWM/NVDA gaps; 3x day trades 09:35->10:00/10:30; conditional replacement of the 09:31 overnight exit; gap-conditional entry/hold-through; pre-market and opening-auction exit)

votes.candidate: Gap-down hold-through (NVDA open <= -3%: skip the 09:31 exit and the 15:52 re-entry, hold NVDL/NVDX to the next 09:31)
reasons: The edge does not hold up out of sample. Excluding earnings days, 2005-2026 has 128 events: mean +1.83%, t 2.43. That t comes from one block of 14 events in 2012-2018 (+7.07%, t 3.30). The other periods are weak: 2005-2011 n=53 +1.45% t 1.19 (median -0.89, win 45%); 2019-2026 n=61 +0.95% t 0.92 (median -0.32, win 49%); last 2 years n=14 +1.74% t 0.83. With 2012-2018 removed the result is n=114, +1.18%, t 1.51, median -0.86, win 47%.

There is no typical-case edge. The median is -0.01% and the strategy wins 64 of 128 events (sign test p=1.0). A few V-shaped crisis-rebound days carry the mean: 2008-10/11, 2018-11-20, 2022-02-24, 2024-08-05 and 2025-04-07. Dropping the best 5 events gives t 1.47; dropping the best 8 gives t 0.89. 0.30 points of the delta is just the cost saving; the 2x intraday hold itself has a median of -0.31%.

It is dominated by C1-A, as the candidate itself admits. All of the positive expectancy comes in 09:31->10:00 (2x +1.86%, t 4.04, win 60%; 2019+ +1.48%, t 2.38). The 10:00->15:52 piece that only the hold-through adds is negative: -0.32% overall (median -1.03%, win 44%) and -0.82% from 2019 (median -1.30%, win 43%). Against a 10:00 exit, the hold-through adds about -0.02% per event over the full sample and about -0.52% from 2019, with a worst leg of -15.8%.

The mechanism does not carry over to the indexes. On SPY and QQQ's own gap-down days, holding 2x from 09:31 to 15:52 (+0.30%) is no better than holding on any day (about +0.33%) after 2016/2019: SPY gap <= -1.5% from 2019 n=45 -0.02%; QQQ gap <= -1.5% from 2019 n=81 +0.14%. The candidate's own QQQ-trigger version also fails on recent data when I recompute it: NVDA delta when QQQ gaps <= -1.5% is +0.31% (t 0.38) from 2019 and -0.22% over the last 2 years. That leaves an NVDA-only effect, on a stock picked with hindsight.

Data-snooping. This is one variant among dozens in the opening-gap family: gap thresholds, SPY/QQQ/IWM/NVDA triggers and several exit times. A best t of about 2.0-2.4 is roughly what the maximum of 20-50 tries gives by chance. A threshold grid gives no recent support either: from 2019 the t-stat is 0.66-1.71 at every trigger from -1% to -7%.

Specification issue: 20 of the 148 gap days at -3% or worse are NVDA earnings reactions. Under §3(d) the leg is already in cash on those days, so they must be excluded; those 20 average -2.03%. My event counts also differ from the candidate's (2005-11: 53 vs 31; last 2 years: 14 vs 10), which suggests their 5-minute recent data could not see the 09:31 and 15:52 prices.

To be fair to the candidate, a simplified equity simulation with the PAUSE rule (0.93 exposure, 0.15% cost per side, 1-share pause about 0.40 exposure) shows no material rise in PAUSE risk. Over 60-session windows P(PAUSE) is 40.6% vs 40.1% (2016 on: 44.5% vs 43.5%). Log growth is somewhat better, mostly from the guaranteed 0.30% saving and the right tail. So it is not dangerous, but its edge is not demonstrated out of sample, and C1-A is the better version.
recomputed_numbers: Data and method: Robinhood split-adjusted daily NVDA/QQQ bars for 2005-2026 give the gap. 1-minute bars (an HF OHLCV-1m extract, raw prices, 2005-01 to 2026-03) give the within-day 09:31 and 15:52 prices. Robinhood bars cover the 3 events in 2026 (09-14 at 1 minute; 04-28 and 06-23 at 5 minutes, where the open stands in for 09:31). Delta = daily-reset 2x return from 09:31 to 15:52 + 0.30%. Daily open-to-close from the 1-minute data matches Robinhood with a median gap of 0.04%.

Gap <= -3% days 2005-2026: 149, of which 20 are earnings reactions. Including earnings: n=148, +1.31%, t 1.78. Excluding: n=128, +1.83%, med -0.01, t 2.43, win 50%, worst -15.23%, best +24.49%. Earnings days only: n=20, -2.03%.
Robustness: 10% trimmed mean +1.31%; drop top 3 t 1.86; drop top 5 t 1.47; drop top 8 t 0.89; sign 64/128; sign-flip permutation p=0.017 (full sample only).

Cross-asset hold on own gap days (2x, +0.30%), from 2019: SPY gap <= -1.5% n=45 -0.02%; QQQ gap <= -1.5% n=81 +0.14%. NVDA delta with a QQQ gap <= -1.5% trigger: all n=158 +0.91% t 1.43; from 2019 +0.31%; last 2 years -0.22%.

PAUSE simulation, 60-session windows, base vs candidate: P(PAUSE) 40.6% vs 40.1%; from 2016 44.5% vs 43.5%; P(equity <= 50% of start) from 2016 0.2% vs 0.4%; mean log growth from 2016 -1.36% vs -0.22%.

Side finding: the baseline gross 2x-NVDA overnight return (15:52->09:31, ex-earnings) is +0.040%/night in 2005-11, +0.112% in 2012-18, +0.363% in 2019-26Q1 and +0.307% over 2024-10 to 2026-03, against a 0.30% round-trip cost.
votes.survives_if: It would survive only as a cost-saving tweak, and only if C1-A (exit at 10:00 on gap-down days) is rejected. Even then it needs evidence that is not tied to 2012-2018. Two ways to get it: (a) a positive ex-earnings mean with t >= 2 over 2019-2026 plus a positive median, which it currently lacks (t 0.92, median -0.32); or (b) a pre-registered forward shadow record of at least 20 events with mean > +0.30% that is not driven by one or two crash-rebound days. If C1-A is adopted, the hold-through should be dropped: its extra 10:00->15:52 leg has non-positive expectancy and twice the tail risk.

votes.candidate: Gap-down hold-through (NVDA open <= -3%: skip the 09:31 exit and the 15:52 re-entry, hold to next morning) on NVDL/NVDX
reasons: Costs and mechanics are not the problem. The 0.30% round-trip saving is real, and on gap-down mornings it is probably understated because NVDL spreads are wider at 09:31. Changing the saving from 0.10% to 0.40% moves the mean by only -0.2 to +0.1 points. The rule needs no PDT slot and no cash at 15:52, and whole shares and the $103 account size do not limit it. The trigger can be decided by 09:31: classifying on the 09:31 price instead of the official open gives n 171, +1.76%, t 2.69. My synthetic 2x series matches real NVDL closely on the 20 events since 2022-12 (real minus synthetic: mean +0.01%, sd 0.19%). So I could not refute it on costs or execution alone.

The part that is new versus C1-A has no edge. Splitting the 2x return over the 129 eligible events (2005-2026): 09:31->10:00 is +1.82% (t 4.0) and 10:00->15:52 is -0.38% (t -0.63). Holding past 10:00 plus the 0.30% saving nets -0.08%/event (t -0.13); since 2016 it is -0.01% (t -0.01). The hold-through segment adds about 6.7% sd per event with no expected return. All the edge is the opening rebound, which C1-A already captures with a smaller tail.

The mean comes from a few crash-rebound days, and the median is about zero. Full sample: mean +1.73% but median -0.32%, win rate 49%. Dropping the top 5 events (2022-02-24, 2025-04-07, 2018-11-20, 2008-11-13, 2024-08-05, each about +20%) gives +0.92% (t 1.33); for 2016+ it gives +0.45% (t 0.55). By gap size, -3% to -4% gaps (n 62) average +0.28% (t 0.31); the edge is in rare -4% or worse capitulation gaps.

The recent out-of-sample evidence does not hold up. Last 2 years: n 14, +1.70% (t 0.82); without 2025-04-07 it is +0.15%, and without the top 2 it is -0.51%. NVDL era (2022-12+): n 21, +2.33% (t 1.37); without the top 2 it is +0.35%. On real NVDL prices: n 20, +2.34%, t 1.31.

Half the value needs an override of the PAUSE rule. In the synthetic equity path, 63 of 129 events fall on days when PAUSE is active or triggers at 09:31. The edge sits there (+3.07%, t 2.48). On non-PAUSE events it is +0.44% (t 0.52), or +1.18% (t 0.99) since 2016. Section 6 cuts exposure to 1 NVDL share on those days. A version that respects PAUSE keeps only about half the growth gain (+3.5 to +5.7%/yr versus +4.8 to +9.5%/yr held at full size). Over 2005-26 and 2016-26 it then trails C1-A by 1.0 to 1.7%/yr; it is ahead only in 2022-12+ and the last 2 years, by 2.5 to 3.6%/yr.

The left tail on the worst days gets heavier. Equity change on event days (prior 15:52 to 15:52), 2016-26: 5th percentile -14.6% becomes -17.4%, and the worst day goes from -26.8% to -31.3% (2025-01-27). Synthetic maxDD worsens by 2.6 to 3.0 points in 2016-26, 2022-12+ and the last 2 years; over 2005-26 both are about -100%. P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) is about flat (-0.6 to -0.7 points over long samples) but +2.3 points (45.0% to 47.3%) in 2022-12+. KILL rates are unchanged or lower.

Overall: the long sample looks fine (t 2.30, year-clustered t 2.57, both halves positive, smooth across thresholds). The specific claim that holding through the session adds value beyond a 10:00 exit has no support, its recent evidence rests on 1-2 events, and its full-size benefit depends on overriding PAUSE. It does not clearly pass the bar.

votes.candidate: TQQQ dip-buy day trade (QQQ official open <= -2% vs prior close: buy TQQQ 09:35, sell 10:00; 10:30 variant)
reasons: The headline number reproduces, but the -2% threshold result is a mix of two different groups. Days with QQQ gaps between -2% and -3% are flat to negative in all three indexes (QQQ -0.18%, SPY -0.31%, IWM -0.21% per trade, net, 3x). Every bit of the edge comes from crash-sized gaps of -3% or worse: about 19-20 events in 15 years, roughly 1.3 a year.

Results across gap sizes are not monotonic, which is a red flag for data-snooping. QQQ 09:35->10:00 net, by gap band: (-1.0,-0.5] -0.35% (t -5.3), (-1.5,-1.0] -0.29% (t -2.3), (-2.0,-1.5] -0.47% (t -2.7), (-2.5,-2.0] +0.38%, (-3.0,-2.5] -0.86% (t -1.9), <=-3.0% +2.83% (t 2.6). Moderate gaps keep falling, they do not reverse, so the 'opening-panic reversal' explanation does not hold at the chosen -2% threshold.

The first half (H1) is a single trade. 2015-08-24 (ETF pricing broke down at the open that day) earned +20.19% synthetic and +18.07% real. Without it, H1 2011-2018 is n=16, +0.06%, t 0.17. Over the full sample: drop the best trade and the mean is +0.61%; drop the top 3 and it is +0.39% (t 1.40); drop the top 5 and it is +0.19% (t 0.75). The median trade is only +0.55%.

The edge depends on entering at exactly 09:35 and fades within minutes. Synthetic net mean by entry time (exit 10:00): 09:33 +1.19%, 09:35 +0.98%, 09:36 +0.77%, 09:37 +0.33%, 09:40 +0.03%. On real TQQQ: 09:36 +0.69% (t 1.91), 09:37 +0.35% (t 0.98). A delay of 1-2 minutes, which is realistic for a scheduled agent order, erases most of it. On 2015-08-24, TQQQ printed 67.00 at 09:34 and 72.45 at 09:35, an 8% jump in one minute, so the biggest trade's fill cannot be relied on.

Multiple-testing check: I ran 385 combinations of threshold (-1 to -3%), entry (09:31-09:45) and exit (09:45-15:50) on 2011-2026. 28 have t>2 and the best is t 2.87. The chosen combination's t of 2.05 is what selection from that many tries would produce by chance. H1 t-stats never pass 1.4 for any combination.

Splits by period: H1 (2011-07..2018) n=17, t 1.01, so it was never significant in-sample. Last 2 years: n=7, +0.90%, t 0.79, so no confirmation. Excluding 2020 (16 of the 53 events): +0.88%, t 1.42. Clustered by month: 31 months, t 1.77. Year-cluster t is 2.00 on 13 years, and a year-block bootstrap gives P(mean<=0)=0.01. That support comes from crisis clusters (2015-08, 2020-03), not from a stable effect.

It does not carry over to other indexes at -2%. SPY gap <= -2%, 3x 09:35->10:00, 2005-2026: n=65, +0.52% (t 1.27); excluding 2008 and 2020, +0.16% (t 0.35). IWM <= -2%: n=91, +0.53% (t 1.62); 2019 onward -0.31%; excluding 2008 and 2020, -0.29%. Pre-sample QQQ test (QLD-implied, 2008-01..2011-03): n=18, +1.53% (t 1.46), but almost all of it is October 2008 (+8.8%, +12.5%, +7.7%). The other 7 events in 2009..2011-03 average -0.53%.

The dollar value is tiny even if the full-sample mean is taken at face value. With about $103 of cash, whole shares and TQQQ at $78.81, you can buy only 1 share, about 76% of equity. That gives roughly 3.4 trades/yr x 0.98% x $78.8 = about $2.6/yr with a perfect 09:35 fill, or about $1.8/yr with a 09:36 fill on real TQQQ. Each trade uses one of the 3 PDT slots on crash mornings, when the overnight NVDL leg is already down. The worst price drop inside the 09:35-10:00 window was -5.88%.

votes.candidate: TQQQ dip-buy day trade (QQQ open <= -2%: buy TQQQ 09:35, sell 10:00)
reasons: I reproduced the headline from scratch and it matches: 53 events from 2011-07 to 2026-10, using Robinhood daily official opens for the signal and real TQQQ 1-minute bars (2026 events from Robinhood 5-minute bars). With prices taken as of 09:35 and 10:00 and 0.30% round trip, the mean is +0.89% (t 2.03), as claimed. The problem is what that number rests on.

Execution killer 1 is one price that could not have been traded. 2015-08-24 (QQQ -8%, LULD chaos) alone adds +18.07 of the 47.37 total percentage points (38%). TQQQ's 09:35 one-minute bar that day ran from 66.75 to 74.00, a 10.4% range, so the modeled entry at 67.00 was not executable. Without it, the realistic-fill mean is +0.55% (t 1.77), and the first half (2011-07 to 2018, n=16) is -0.14% (t -0.39, median -0.03). The in-sample half has no edge without that one print.

Execution killer 2 is two market-wide circuit-breaker days. On 2020-03-09 trading was halted 09:34-09:49 and on 2020-03-16 from 09:30 to 09:45, so a 09:35 order cannot fill at 09:35. Without those two and 2015-08-24 the mean is +0.41% (t 1.35). Without all of March 2020 and 2015-08-24 it is +0.37% (t 1.16).

62% of the signals lose money after costs. In the -2% to -3% gap bucket (n=33) the realistic-fill net mean is -0.18% (t -0.74), and it is negative in both halves (H1 -0.45, H2 -0.03). All of the edge sits in about 20 extreme mornings (gap <= -3%, about 1.3 a year). Those are the same chaotic, halt-prone mornings that fill risk is worst.

The result is fragile to timing. The 09:35 entry and 10:00 exit are a local peak on the time grid. Entering 1, 2 or 3 minutes late gives +0.50, +0.31 and +0.18% (from +0.75 on the same 51 days), with t falling to 1.37, 0.89 and 0.54. Exiting 2 minutes early or late gives +0.67 or +0.54, and 5 minutes either way gives +0.48 or +0.50. The live order log shows real latency of 0.5 to 2.5 minutes: day-leg buys meant for 09:32 went in at 09:31:33 to 09:33:30, and exit re-prices ran to 09:32:49. A 1-2 minute slip is the normal case.

Fills within the minute matter as much as the edge. The median one-minute TQQQ range is 0.82% at 09:35 and 0.80% at 10:00. Buying at the 09:35 bar high and selling at the 10:00 bar low, with only 0.10% round-trip cost, gives -0.05% (t -0.16). The fixed cost is not the issue: the TQQQ spread was 1 cent (0.013%) on 2026-10-14, so 0.30% round trip is conservative.

Whole shares and $103 equity shrink it further. TQQQ was $74.90 on 2026-10-14, so only one share fits: about 68-74% of equity after the overnight loss on a gap-down morning, not 100%. Realistic dollars at E≈$95 and 3.47 events a year: about $1.88/yr with all events, $1.34/yr without 2015-08-24, and $1.01/yr also without the halt days. The candidate claimed $3.4/yr. Against a planning overnight edge of roughly $70/yr, this is noise.

PDT budget and cash conflict. Under §7 of the rules, the PDT budget is reserved for emergency same-day exits of the overnight leg. Signals cluster: 16 in 2020, 4 in 2025-04 within 6 business days. With one slot kept in reserve (2 per 5 business days) it skips 2020-02-28, 03-09, 03-11, 03-18 and 2025-04-07, and the mean on trades taken falls to +0.59. The candidate itself says C1 (keeping the overnight NVDL position until 10:00 on gap-down mornings) captures the same bounce for free from 09:31, and C1 triggers on QQQ <= -1%, which includes every one of these days. If C1 is adopted, this trade fires only when the account is already in cash; none of the 53 events in 15 years fell on a post-NVDA-earnings morning, when the rules say the account is in cash. So it would essentially never trade.

PAUSE interaction. In a rough synthetic 2x-NVDA overnight equity path, 30 of 51 event mornings were already at or below the PAUSE line after the overnight loss. The trade's mean was +1.07% on those mornings and only +0.31% on the 21 mornings not in PAUSE. The edge is concentrated on mornings when the de-risking rule is already active. The PAUSE-trigger count barely changes (44 vs 46 over 15 years), so this is a policy caveat rather than a large risk increase.

Pessimistic fill (buy at the 09:35 bar high, sell at the 10:00 bar low, 0.10% round trip): -0.05 (t -0.16). Median one-minute range: 0.82% at 09:35, 0.80% at 10:00.
PDT caps (per 5 business days): 3 skips 1 event (taken mean +0.80); 2 skips 5 (+0.59); 1 skips 13 (+0.65).
TQQQ $74.90 (bid 74.90, ask 74.91) on 2026-10-14: 1 share is 68-78% of E between $103 and $90. Expected value ≈ $1.0-1.9/yr, versus the $3.4/yr claimed.
Synthetic overnight path: 30 of 51 event mornings already in PAUSE after the overnight loss. TQQQ trade mean +1.07 on those vs +0.31 on the others. PAUSE triggers 44 vs 46 over 2011-2026.
votes.survives_if: It would only stand as a narrow side rule, worth about $1/yr, if all of these hold: (1) C1 (keep the overnight leg until 10:00 on gap-down mornings) is not adopted, because otherwise there is no cash at 09:35 and the trade never fires; (2) the threshold is tightened to QQQ open <= -3% (about 1.1-1.3 a year), since the -2% to -3% band is negative after costs; (3) the order is skipped if the market or TQQQ is halted, or if the 09:35 one-minute range is above ~2% (dislocation); (4) the order goes in within 60 seconds of 09:35 and the exit within 60 seconds of 10:00 (each minute of delay costs about 0.2-0.4%); (5) at least 1 PDT slot is left for emergency exits after this trade; (6) 1 TQQQ share fits under 0.98 x E. Even then the evidence is n=17 (only 4 in the first half) with t≈2.3, so it should be logged as a shadow trade, not adopted.

judge.rule_text: NO NEW RULE. RULES_v3 v1.7 stays as it is: the 15:52 NVDL/NVDX entry, the 09:31 exit, the TZA day leg suspended, and all 3 PDT slots kept for §7 emergency exits. The 09:31-15:52 cash stays idle. The only result that survived both skeptics confirms the status quo and needs no rule change: keep holding the NVDA-2x leg on FOMC-eve nights and never add an FOMC blackout (§3 'No other event blackouts' already says this). Two factual notes the owner may want to fix by hand (the judge did not edit anything): (1) The RULES §1 claim that 'after a down intraday session the next night averages ~2x better' is false over 25 years. The sign is reversed in 2001-2013, 2013-2026 and the 1-minute data, and holds only in the last ~12 months. (2) The NVDL ex-date of 10/28 is unverified, because NVDL's price history shows no October distribution. If GraniteShares declares one, exclude only the declared $/share from PAUSE and decay inputs, never the whole opening gap.
judge.rationale:
The bar was: survives both skeptics, has long-sample and out-of-sample after-cost evidence, has a mechanism, and does not materially raise P(PAUSE). One of 21 candidates survived both skeptics: 'FOMC-eve overnight (status quo)'. It adds $0 because the current leg already holds those nights, and it is not significant over the last 2 years (permutation p 0.37-0.67). So it is not an addition to adopt. Every other candidate was refuted by at least one skeptic. The four 'one-skeptic-not-refuted' cases (UPONLY, SKIP_BOTHDOWN, C1-A, C1-D) failed on the out-of-sample or data-snooping lens, and the skeptics who passed them used the cost/feasibility lens.

My own re-check, independent code on the gap-and-open 1-minute checkpoint table (2005-01..2026-03 plus RH 5-minute tail), earnings days excluded:

(a) C1 exit-delay family, 2x NVDA from 09:31 to 10:00 per event.
- C1-A (NVDA open <= -3%): H1 +3.20% (t 2.96), H2 2019+ +1.43% (t 2.25), last 2 years +1.45% (t 1.02; -0.57% without the top 3). Measured from 09:32 instead of 09:31, H2 is +0.95% with median +0.03.
- The (-5%,-3%] band, which is the bulk of C1-A's events, gives H2 -0.03% (median -0.72) and last 2 years -0.64%.
- C1-D (market <= -1.5%) has the same pattern. Its (-3%,-1.5%] band gives H2 +0.20% (t 0.58) and last 2 years -0.49%.
- All of the edge sits in crash opens. NVDA <= -5%: H2 n=17, +5.03% (t 3.25). QQQ <= -3%: H2 n=14, +6.02% (t 3.58).
- So the rules as specified are mostly mean-zero triggers wrapped around about 2 crash days a year. Their per-event and $/yr claims do not survive. The crash-only version was found after the fact by the skeptics, rests on n≈14-17 dominated by 2020-03, 2024-08-05 and 2025-04-07, and was never put through two skeptics. It cannot be adopted now.

(b) Skip-down-session rules, 2x NVDA from 15:52 to 09:31, kept nights minus skipped nights.
- UPONLY: 2005-2015 diff +0.138% (t 1.10, not significant); 2016-21 +0.42% (t 2.49); 2022-26 +0.54% (t 2.35); last year +0.37% (t 0.62); 2026 YTD +0.06% (t 0.09).
- SKIP_BOTHDOWN: 2005-2015 diff +0.05% (t 0.41); last year -0.03%; 2026 -0.27%.
- The first decade does not support either rule. The skeptics showed that most of the PAUSE reduction comes from lower average exposure (a constant 0.64 exposure gives similar P(PAUSE)). Shrunk to a realistic forward edge, the growth gain is about zero. The tradable 15:50 signal lost to the current rule on real NVDL over 2026-04..10, and the candidate's 'break-even' tail result used the non-executable 16:00 close.
- These are risk-reduction or de-levering choices for the owner, not validated growth edges, and they were chosen post hoc from a large grid.

Everything else is dead or decaying: B9/B9p breakout (flat last 2 years, timing-fragile, full size raises PAUSE 6-7 pts), the calendar cells (best-of-many, family-wise p 0.2-0.6, last 2 years negative), and the day trades (negative at realistic cost, use the emergency PDT slots, crash-only tails). The honest conclusion is to adopt nothing and shadow-log the few ideas worth watching.
judge.expected_effect: None. The strategy and its expected growth are unchanged. That avoids adding noise-level rules whose recent-window expectancy is zero to negative (for example C1-A's ordinary band since 2019 is -0.03%/event; UPONLY lost about $30-40/yr against the current rule in the last 12 months).
judge.risk_effect: None. P(PAUSE) and P(KILL) stay at the current rule's level. No PDT slots are spent, so §7 emergency capacity stays at 3. The skeptics' long-sample bootstraps show the current overnight leg's 60-session P(PAUSE) is about 30-45%, far above the earlier 1-year estimate of 4.5%. That is a pre-existing risk this decision neither raises nor fixes. If the owner wants lower PAUSE risk, a deliberate exposure decision (for example the UPONLY or BOTHDOWN filter, or a smaller basket) should be made openly as de-risking, not as an edge.
rejected_summary: FOMC-eve overnight (status quo): survived both skeptics but adds $0, because the current leg already holds these nights. The FOMC-specific premium is real over 20 years for SPY/QQQ (both halves t>2.8) but absent in the last 2 years (permutation p 0.37-0.67). NVDA first half t is 2.05, not >=2.7 as claimed. Keep it as is with no blackout; it is not a new rule.

FOMC-eve TQQQ in §3(f) cash mode: refuted by both skeptics. It only fires about 1.9 times a year (not 7.9) because §3(f) rarely triggers, worth about $0.7-1/yr. The cash-mode subset has t 1.49 and 1.59 by half and is mostly 2008-09. Excluding nights that coincided with mega-cap earnings gaps leaves a first half of about 0.

SKIP_DOWN_SESSION (UPONLY): one skeptic refuted it. My re-check gives a 2005-15 executable UP-minus-DOWN diff of +0.14% (t 1.10, not significant), 2009-15 was negative, and the last 1y/2026 diff is about 0 or reversed. With the effect shrunk to a forward ~0.14%, expected growth is at or below the current rule. The PAUSE drop (~36% to ~12%) comes mostly from lower exposure. It was chosen post hoc as the mirror of the false §1 claim. It is a de-risking choice, not an edge.

SKIP_BOTHDOWN: one skeptic refuted it. It was chosen post hoc from a 2x2 table, and my re-check gives a 2005-15 diff of +0.05% (t 0.41). It does not replicate on QQQ/SPY/peers. With the executable 15:50 signal it lost to the current rule over 2026-04..10 on real NVDL (+6% vs +18.5% at 0.07%/side). The candidate's 'break-even' result relied on the 16:00 close sign, which carries look-ahead.

DOWN_1SHARE: both skeptics refuted it. Against matched constant exposure, 2005-15 shows no value once 2008 is excluded. The gain changes sign between 0.03 and 0.07%/side cost (breakeven about 0.03-0.05%/side, and live cost is measured at about 0-0.03%). Last 12 months about -$32/yr. The PAUSE benefit equals a flat 0.64 exposure.

C1-A gap-down exit delay (NVDA <= -3% -> 10:00): one skeptic refuted it. My re-check shows the (-5,-3] band, about 72% of events, at H2 -0.03% (median -0.72) and last 2y -0.64%. Since 2019 all of the edge comes from 17 crash opens of -5% or worse. Last 2y without the top 3 is -0.57%, and with a 09:32 baseline H2 is +0.95% with median +0.03. In H2 it fails a 98-cell family-wise test (p 0.15).

C1-D market-gap exit delay (QQQ <= -1.5%): one skeptic refuted it. My re-check gives the (-3,-1.5] band at H2 +0.20% (t 0.58) and last 2y -0.49%. The crash bucket (QQQ <= -3%, n=14 in H2) carries everything. Last 2y is +0.97% (t 0.88), -0.59% without the top 3. The 09:31->09:32 minute carries about 40% of the effect, so it is sensitive to execution timing.

C1-C (QQQ <= -1.0%): both skeptics refuted it. The added -1.0..-1.5% band is negative out of sample at every exit time from 09:35 to 11:00 (H2 -0.17%). The rule is dominated by C1-D, and 2026-04..10 real NVDL averaged -0.36%/event.

C1-B (NVDA <= -2%): both skeptics refuted it. The added (-3,-2] bucket is H2 +0.07% (t 0.3), and the increment over C1-A is about $0.85/yr. It loses in below-200dMA regimes (2022), and in H2 it worsens maxDD (-71% vs -63%) and raises historical P(PAUSE).

C1 09:40 exit variant: both skeptics refuted it. Last 2y is -0.02% and post-sample 2026 is -0.59%. 09:40 is a local spike among nearby exit minutes, and the result disappears with a 1-minute execution delay (H2 -0.05%).

Gap-down hold-through (NVDA <= -3%): both skeptics refuted it. The median is about 0. The 10:00->15:52 leg it adds over C1-A is negative (-0.32%, 2019+ -0.82%). The t-stat depends on 2012-18 and half the value needs a PAUSE override.

TQQQ dip-buy day trade (QQQ <= -2%): both skeptics refuted it. 2015-08-24 (an untradable LULD print) supplies 38% of P&L, and without it H1 is -0.14%. The -2..-3% band is negative, the edge disappears with a 1-2 minute entry delay, it is worth about $1-2/yr, and it uses a PDT slot.

B9 full-size NVDA noise-band early entry: both skeptics refuted it. It raises P(PAUSE within 60) by about 6-7 points in every window. The last-2y edge is about 0 (real NVDL -0.04%) and turns negative with a 5-minute fill. H1 t is 1.79 (1.21 with the official open). The stated LETF-rebalancing mechanism contradicts the timing of the effect.

B9p (1 NVDL share early on breakout): both skeptics refuted it. Last 2y per-signal is -0.045% and real NVDL since 2024-10 is -0.05%. The edge decays by about 2 bp per minute of fill delay on real NVDL. P(PAUSE) still rises about 0.3-1.3 points, for about $2-4/yr. A 40-60 signal shadow log has no statistical power.

C1 QQQ noise-band TQQQ day trade: both skeptics refuted it. Before 2011 (QLD-implied) it nets -0.34%/trade (t -3.6). Breakeven cost is about 0.09%/side, and at 0.15% it is -0.12%. The last 2y are about 0. It uses PDT slots and adds 1-4 points of PAUSE.

E-TOM+3 (enter at 09:31 on the 3rd trading day): both skeptics refuted it. Two shock days (2008-07-03, 2024-08-05) carry the mean. Walk-forward cell selection gives t 0.47-1.51, the last 2y are negative on every measure, the NVDA-specific component has decayed, and last-2y PAUSE rises 24.5% to 34.7% at realistic cost.

H-TOM+3 hold-through: both skeptics refuted it. Most of the t-stat is the generic 0.30% saved cost. The TOM+3-specific excess is best-of-23 noise (family-wise p 0.64, shrinks to about 0). The real saving at the measured fill cost is about 0.03-0.13%.

Turn-of-month TQQQ day trades TOM+2/+3: both skeptics refuted it. At 0.15%/side it is +0.015%/trade, and at 0.06% the t is 1.30. Walk-forward pair selection gives about 0 or negative. It is positive only because of the last 2 years and raises P(PAUSE) 1.4-2.9 points.

Quad-witching SPXU day trade: both skeptics refuted it. 2022+ is -0.31%/trade (0DTE era, with decay significant at t 2.1). 2020-03-20 is 28% of P&L. Low-volatility regimes like the current one (rv 9.3%) show about 0, and at E=$103 only 2 shares are affordable.

Hold NVDL through opex-week Tuesday: both skeptics refuted it. The 57-cell family-wise p is about 0.24, and the effect comes from different sources in each half (FOMC overlap, then NVDA pre-earnings). The last 2y are -0.26%, and the next instance (2026-11-17) is an NVDA earnings day, which conflicts with §3(d).

All other screened ideas were killed at the sweep stage: Gao first/last-half-hour momentum (A1-A8, 15:31-15:50 gross about 0, so -0.12%/trade net), earlier or later unconditional 15:52 entries (15:52 is a local optimum), later or conditional exits (decayed since 2021), T-bill parking (accrual is in the open print), the 32-ETF intraday drift scan, short-vol, BTC, sector/pair/single-stock reversals, and inverse fades. None has after-cost out-of-sample support, and several add large tail risk.
follow_up_research: Measure real round-trip fill cost for NVDL/NVDX from the live trades log, against 1-minute bars and quotes at fill time, with n >= 60. Several verdicts flip between 0.03 and 0.15%/side, including whether the overnight leg itself has positive net expectancy (at 0.15%/side it is about 0 over 2005-2026). This is the highest-value unknown.

Re-estimate baseline risk for the current overnight leg. The long-sample bootstraps give 60-session P(PAUSE) of about 30-45% and P(KILL within 250) of 3-7%, against the 1-year 4.5% figure in prior reviews. Decide explicitly whether to reduce exposure (constant smaller basket vs the UPONLY/BOTHDOWN filters) as a risk choice, compared on equal average exposure.

Pre-registered zero-capital shadow log of the crash-open exit delay: on mornings with NVDA official open <= -5% or QQQ <= -3% vs prior close (earnings mornings excluded), record the NVDL/NVDX bid at the actual 09:31 exit fill time and at 10:00. Also log the -3%/-1.5% band events to confirm they stay mean-zero. Review at the 2027-01-11 quarterly review and again after >= 10 crash events, before considering live adoption.

Shadow-log the 15:50 NVDA-vs-open and vs-prior-close signs every non-earnings night, with real 15:52->09:31 NVDL outcomes for kept and would-be-skipped nights (UPONLY/BOTHDOWN), using no parameter changes. Judge after >= 120 nights at t >= 1.5. Until then, do not use the false RULES §1 down-day claim as a rationale for anything.

Optional shadow logs, no capital, low expectation: E-TOM+3 (record the TOM+3 09:31 vs prior-15:52 counterfactual monthly, next 2026-11-04 and 2026-12-03) and B9p restricted to the 11:00 checkpoint (record the real NVDL ask at the agent's actual detection time). Both need years of data to have any power.
Verify the NVDL distribution and ex-date with GraniteShares before the 2026-10-27 entry. If one is declared, exclude only the declared $/share amount from PAUSE and edge-decay inputs.
